1.context: 我還有許多事要寫給你們，卻不願意用紙墨寫出來，但盼望到你們那裏，與你們當面談論，使你們的喜樂滿足。

1.title: 長老的問安
1.context: 作長老的寫信給親愛的該猶，就是他誠心所愛的；願你凡事興盛，身體健壯，正如你的靈魂興盛一樣。

1.title: 稱讚該猶款待人
1.context: 長老稱讚該猶忠心接待作客旅的弟兄，他們是為主的名出外的；又責備好為首的丟特腓不接待弟兄，用惡言妄論他們，還把接待的人趕出教會；他勸該猶不要效法惡，只要效法善，並稱讚底米丟有好見證。

1.title: 結語
1.context: 長老説他原有許多事要寫，卻不願意用筆墨寫給他，盼望快快見他，當面談論；願他平安，眾位朋友都問他安。

1.title: 神對不敬虔之人的審判
1.context: 猶大勸信徒為從前一次交付聖徒的真道竭力地爭辯，因為有些不虔誠的人偷着進來，把神的恩變作放縱情慾的機會；他以出埃及後不信而滅的百姓、犯罪的天使和所多瑪蛾摩拉為鑒戒，説這些人像無水的雲彩、無根的樹。

1.title: 呼召要堅忍
1.context: 末世必有譏誚的人隨從私慾而行，這是使徒早已説過的；信徒要在至聖的真道上造就自己，在聖靈裏禱告，保守自己常在神的愛中，等候主耶穌基督的憐憫，也要憐憫疑惑的人。

1.title: 頌讚
1.context: 頌讚的結語：那能保守他們不失腳、叫他們無瑕無疵歡歡喜喜站在他榮耀之前的，我們的救主獨一的神，願榮耀、威嚴、能力、權柄因我們的主耶穌基督歸給他，從萬古以前並現今直到永永遠遠。

1.title: 序言
1.context: 約翰在書首説明：這是耶穌基督的啓示，神賜給他，叫他將必要快成的事指示僕人；宣讀、聽見、遵守這書的人有福。

1.title: 約翰在拔摩島的異象
1.context: 約翰在拔摩島上，主日被聖靈感動，看見七個金燈臺中間有一位好像人子，手裏拿着七星；他吩咐約翰把所看見的寫下來，寄給亞細亞的七個教會。

2.title: 給以弗所教會
2.context: 給以弗所教會的信：稱讚他們勞碌、忍耐、分辨假使徒，卻責備他們離棄了起初的愛心，要他們悔改。

2.title: 給士每拿教會
2.context: 給士每拿教會的信：他們貧窮受苦，卻是富足的；不要怕將要受的苦，務要至死忠心，必得生命的冠冕。

2.title: 給別迦摩教會
2.context: 給別迦摩教會的信：他們住在撒但座位所在之處，仍堅守主名，但其中有人服從巴蘭和尼哥拉一黨的教訓。

2.title: 給推雅推喇教會
2.context: 給推雅推喇教會的信：稱讚他們的愛心、信心和服事，卻責備他們容讓那自稱先知的婦人耶洗別引誘人。

3.title: 給撒狄教會
3.context: 給撒狄教會的信：按名是活的，其實是死的；要警醒，堅固那剩下將要衰微的。

3.title: 給非拉鐵非教會
3.context: 給非拉鐵非教會的信：他們略有一點力量，卻遵守了主的道，沒有棄絕主的名；主在他們面前給他們一個敞開的門。

3.title: 給老底嘉教會
3.context: 給老底嘉教會的信：他們不冷也不熱，自以為富足，其實困苦可憐；主站在門外叩門，若有人開門，他就要進去與他同坐席。

4.title: 天上的寶座
4.context: 約翰被提到天上，看見有寶座安置在天上，有一位坐在寶座上，四圍有二十四位長老和四個活物，晝夜不停地稱頌那坐寶座、昔在今在以後永在的主神，因他創造了萬物。

5.title: 羔羊取了書卷
5.context: 坐寶座的右手中有一個用七印封嚴的書卷，無人配展開；惟有那曾被殺、從猶大支派出來的羔羊配拿書卷，眾長老和千萬天使都讚美他，又與坐寶座的一同受頌讚。

6.title: 第一印：白馬
6.context: 羔羊揭開前六印：白馬、紅馬、黑馬、灰色馬，代表征服、戰爭、饑荒、死亡；第五印顯出殉道者的靈魂呼求伸冤；第六印有大地震、日月變色，地上的人都躲藏。

7.title: 十四萬四千人受印
7.context: 四位天使執掌地上的四風；另一位天使在神眾僕人的額上蓋印，以色列各支派共十四萬四千人受印。

7.title: 大羣的人頌讚
7.context: 約翰又看見一大羣人，沒有人能數過來，是從各國各族各民各方來的，穿着白衣站在寶座和羔羊面前；他們是從大患難中出來的，曾用羔羊的血把衣裳洗白淨了。

8.title: 第七印
8.context: 羔羊揭開第七印，天上寂靜約有二刻；七位天使得了七枝號，又有天使把眾聖徒的祈禱和香一同獻在寶座前的金壇上。

8.title: 前四枝號
8.context: 前四枝號吹響，災禍臨到地、海、江河和日月星辰，各有三分之一受害；第五、第六號帶來無底坑的蝗蟲和大批馬軍，人卻仍不悔改。

10.title: 天使和小書卷
10.context: 一位大力的天使從天降下，手拿展開的小書卷；約翰吃了書卷，口中甜如蜜，肚子卻發苦，並且要再向許多民族説預言。

11.title: 兩個見證人
11.context: 約翰受命去量神的殿；神的兩個見證人要穿着毛衣傳道一千二百六十天，被殺後過了三天半，神使他們活過來，升到天上。

11.title: 第七枝號
11.context: 第七枝號吹響，天上有大聲音説：世上的國成了我們主和主基督的國，他要作王直到永永遠遠；二十四位長老俯伏敬拜神。

12.title: 婦人和龍
12.context: 天上現出大異象：一個身披日頭的婦人生了男孩子，大紅龍要吞吃他，孩子被提到神的寶座那裏；天上有爭戰，那古蛇魔鬼撒但被摔在地上，弟兄勝過他是因羔羊的血和自己所見證的道。

13.title: 從海裏上來的獸
13.context: 一個獸從海中上來，有七頭十角，龍將自己的能力、座位和大權柄給了它，全地的人都希奇跟從它；又有一個獸從地中上來，叫人拜頭一個獸，並在人的右手上或額上受一個印記；這獸的數目是六百六十六。

14.title: 羔羊和十四萬四千人
14.context: 羔羊站在錫安山上，同他還有十四萬四千人，額上寫着他的名和他父的名；他們在寶座前唱新歌，是從人間買來的，跟隨羔羊。

14.title: 三位天使和巴比倫的傾覆
14.context: 三位天使相繼宣告：要敬畏神，將榮耀歸給他；巴比倫大城傾倒了；拜獸和獸像、受它印記的必喝神忿怒的酒；在主裏死的人有福了。

14.title: 地上的收割
14.context: 有一位好像人子的坐在白雲上，拿着快鐮刀收割地上的莊稼；另一位天使收取地上的葡萄，丟在神忿怒的大酒醡中。

15.title: 摩西和羔羊的歌
15.context: 七位天使拿着末了的七災；勝了獸的人站在玻璃海上，唱摩西的歌和羔羊的歌，頌讚全能的主神作為大哉奇哉，萬國都要來敬拜他。

16.title: 前六碗的憤怒
16.context: 七位天使把神忿怒的七碗倒在地上：生瘡、海和江河變血、日頭烤人、黑暗、幼發拉底河乾涸、空中大地震，人仍褻瀆神，不肯悔改；列王被聚集在哈米吉多頓。

17.title: 騎在獸上的婦人
17.context: 天使指給約翰看那坐在許多水上的大淫婦，騎在朱紅色的獸上，額上寫着「大巴比倫」，喝醉了聖徒的血；獸和十角要與羔羊爭戰，羔羊必勝過他們，因為他是萬王之王、萬主之主。

18.title: 巴比倫傾覆了
18.context: 一位天使宣告大巴比倫傾倒了；天上有聲音呼召神的百姓從那城出來；地上的君王、商人、船主都為她哀哭，因為她的繁華在一時之間就成了荒場。

19.title: 羔羊的婚筵
19.context: 天上羣眾歡呼哈利路亞，因為主我們的神全能者作王了；羔羊婚娶的時候到了，新婦穿上光明潔白的細麻衣，就是聖徒所行的義；被請赴羔羊婚筵的有福了。

19.title: 騎白馬的
19.context: 天開了，有一匹白馬，騎在馬上的稱為誠信真實，他的名稱為神之道，衣服和大腿上寫着「萬王之王、萬主之主」；獸和假先知被擒，扔在燒着硫磺的火湖裏。

20.title: 撒但被捆綁
20.context: 一位天使拿着無底坑的鑰匙和一條大鏈子，把龍捆綁一千年；殉道的和沒有拜獸的人復活了，與基督一同作王一千年。這一千年怎樣理解，讀者看法不一。

20.title: 撒但被扔在火湖裏
20.context: 一千年完了，撒但被釋放，出來迷惑列國，聚集他們來圍攻聖徒的營；有火從天降下燒滅了他們，那迷惑人的魔鬼被扔在硫磺的火湖裏。

20.title: 白色大寶座前的審判
20.context: 約翰看見一個白色的大寶座，死了的人無論大小都站在寶座前，案卷展開了，他們都照着各人所行的受審判；凡名字沒記在生命冊上的，就被扔在火湖裏。

21.title: 新天新地
21.context: 約翰看見一個新天新地，又看見聖城新耶路撒冷由神那裏從天而降；神要與人同住，擦去他們一切的眼淚，不再有死亡、悲哀、哭號、疼痛；坐寶座的説：看哪，我將一切都更新了。

21.title: 新耶路撒冷
21.context: 天使指給約翰看從天而降的聖城新耶路撒冷，有神的榮耀；十二個城門寫着以色列十二支派的名字，根基上有羔羊十二使徒的名字；城內沒有殿，因主神全能者和羔羊為城的殿，也不用日月，因有神的榮耀光照。

22.title: 耶穌必快來
22.context: 天使説這些話是真實可信的；耶穌説「我必快來」，遵守這書上預言的有福了；約翰俯伏要拜天使，天使説不可，你要敬拜神；聖靈和新婦都説「來」，口渴的人可以白白取生命的水喝。

22.title: 不可加添或刪減
22.context: 約翰警告：若有人在這書上的預言加添甚麼，或刪去甚麼，必受書上所寫的災禍；那證明這事的説「是了，我必快來」，約翰回應「主耶穌啊，我願你來」；願主耶穌的恩惠常與眾聖徒同在。

1.title: The Creation
1.context: The Bible opens with God creating the heavens and the earth in six days, each closing with “evening and morning.” God sees all he has made and it is very good; on the seventh day he rests from his work, blesses it and makes it holy.

2.title: Man and Woman in the Garden
2.context: Yahweh God forms the man from the dust of the ground and breathes life into his nostrils. He places him in the garden of Eden and later builds the woman from one of the man’s ribs.

3.title: The Serpent’s Deception
3.context: The serpent tempts the woman, and she and her husband eat the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. They hear Yahweh God walking in the garden and hide; God questions them and each blames another.

3.title: The Fate of the Serpent
3.context: God curses the serpent and says the woman’s offspring will strike its head (Gen 3:15). He pronounces what the woman and the man must bear: pain in childbearing, a cursed ground, lifelong toil, and a return to the dust.

3.title: The Expulsion from Paradise
3.context: Yahweh God says the man now knows good and evil and must not reach out to eat from the tree of life and live forever; so he sends him out of Eden to work the ground and places cherubim and a flaming sword east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life.

4.title: Cain and Abel
4.context: Adam and Eve bear Cain and Abel. Yahweh looks with favor on Abel’s offering but not on Cain’s; in anger Cain kills his brother in the field. Yahweh confronts him, curses him, and makes him a restless wanderer.

4.title: The Descendants of Cain
4.context: Cain’s descendants build a city, dwell in tents, keep livestock, play the harp and pipe, and forge bronze and iron; Lamech boasts of his killing.

4.title: Seth and Enosh
4.context: Adam has another son, Seth, and Seth has Enosh; at that time people began to call on the name of Yahweh.

5.title: The Descendants of Adam
5.context: The genealogy from Adam to Noah, ten generations, each ending “and he died”; only Enoch walked with God, and God took him, and he was no more.

6.title: Corruption on the Earth
6.context: People multiply on the earth; God sees that their wickedness is great and every inclination of their hearts is only evil, and he grieves that he made man.

6.title: Noah’s Favor with God
6.context: Noah is righteous and blameless among his people and walks with God. Seeing the earth corrupt, God tells him to build an ark for his family and for pairs of every living creature.

7.title: The Great Flood
7.context: Yahweh tells Noah to enter the ark; the flood comes upon the earth forty days and nights, the windows of heaven open, and every creature that breathes dies, except Noah and those with him.

8.title: The Ark Rests on Ararat
8.context: God remembers Noah and sends a wind; the waters recede and the ark rests on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sends out a raven and a dove, and the dove returns with an olive leaf; then the earth dries.

8.title: Noah Builds an Altar
8.context: Noah builds an altar to Yahweh and offers burnt offerings of the clean animals; Yahweh smells the pleasing aroma and resolves never again to curse the ground or destroy all living creatures.

9.title: The Covenant of the Rainbow
9.context: God blesses Noah and his sons and makes a covenant that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth, with the rainbow as its sign.

9.title: Noah’s Shame and Canaan’s Curse
9.context: Noah plants a vineyard, gets drunk and lies uncovered in his tent; Ham tells his brothers, while Shem and Japheth cover their father. Noah curses Canaan, Ham’s son, and blesses Shem and Japheth.

10.title: The Table of Nations
10.context: The descendants of Noah’s three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, spread out to become the nations after the flood.

11.title: The Tower of Babel
11.context: All the earth has one language; the people settle in Shinar and build a city and a tower reaching the heavens to make a name for themselves. Yahweh confuses their language and scatters them; the city is called Babel.

11.title: Genealogy from Shem to Abram
11.context: The genealogy from Shem down to Terah, who fathers Abram, Nahor and Haran.

11.title: Terah’s Descendants
11.context: Terah’s family: Haran dies in Ur; Abram marries Sarai; Terah sets out with Abram, Sarai and Lot for Canaan, settles in Haran, and dies there.

12.title: The Call of Abram
12.context: Yahweh tells Abram to leave his country and his father’s household for a land he will show him, promising to make him a great nation and to bless all peoples on earth through him. Abram goes.

12.title: Abram and Sarai in Egypt
12.context: Famine drives Abram down to Egypt, where, fearing for his life, he says Sarai is his sister; Pharaoh takes her, Yahweh afflicts Pharaoh’s house, and Pharaoh sends them away.

13.title: Abram and Lot Part Ways
13.context: Abram’s and Lot’s herds grow and their herdsmen quarrel. Abram lets Lot choose; Lot takes the whole plain of the Jordan and pitches his tents near Sodom, while Abram stays in Canaan.

13.title: God Renews the Promise to Abram
13.context: After Lot leaves, Yahweh tells Abram to look in every direction: all the land he sees will be given to him and his offspring forever, as many as the dust of the earth.

14.title: The War of the Kings
14.context: Four kings attack five and carry off Lot with the goods of Sodom; Abram pursues them with 318 trained men, attacks by night, and recovers the people and the possessions.

14.title: Melchizedek Blesses Abram
14.context: On Abram’s return, Melchizedek king of Salem, priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses him; Abram gives him a tenth of everything.

15.title: God’s Covenant with Abram
15.context: Yahweh’s word comes to Abram in a vision; Abram believes Yahweh, and it is credited to him as righteousness. Yahweh makes a covenant, promising that his offspring will be strangers for four hundred years before inheriting the land.

16.title: Hagar and Ishmael
16.context: Sarai is childless and gives her servant Hagar to Abram; Hagar conceives, despises her mistress, and flees. The angel of Yahweh finds her in the wilderness, tells her to return, and names her son Ishmael.

17.title: Abraham to Father Many Nations
17.context: When Abram is ninety-nine, Yahweh appears to him as God Almighty, renames him Abraham, “father of many nations,” makes circumcision the sign of the covenant, and promises that Sarah will bear Isaac within a year.

18.title: The Three Visitors
18.context: Yahweh appears to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre; looking up, Abraham sees three men standing nearby, runs to meet them and offers generous hospitality. They promise Sarah a son within a year, and she laughs to herself.

18.title: Abraham Intercedes for Sodom
18.context: Yahweh says the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great and he will go down and see. Abraham draws near and pleads for the righteous in the city, down to ten.

19.title: Lot Welcomes the Angels
19.context: Two angels reach Sodom at evening and Lot receives them; the men of the city surround the house, and the angels strike them with blindness and urge Lot to leave with his family.

19.title: Lot Flees to Zoar
19.context: The angels urge Lot to flee for his life, not to look back or stop in the plain; Lot asks to go to the small town of Zoar.

19.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
19.context: As the sun rises Yahweh rains burning sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot’s wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.

19.title: Lot and His Daughters
19.context: Afraid to stay in Zoar, Lot lives in a cave with his two daughters, who make him drink wine and lie with him; their sons Moab and Ben-Ammi become the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.

20.title: Abraham, Sarah, and Abimelech
20.context: Abraham lives in Gerar and again calls his wife his sister; Abimelech takes Sarah, God warns him in a dream, and he returns her; Abraham prays and God heals Abimelech’s household.

21.title: The Birth of Isaac
21.context: Yahweh does for Sarah what he promised: when Abraham is a hundred she bears Isaac; he is circumcised on the eighth day, and Sarah says, “God has brought me laughter.”

21.title: Sarah Turns against Hagar
21.context: Sarah sees Hagar’s son mocking Isaac and asks Abraham to send them away; God tells Abraham to listen to her and promises to make Ishmael a nation too. In the wilderness God hears the boy’s cry and shows Hagar a well.

21.title: The Covenant at Beersheba
21.context: Abimelech and Phicol come to Abraham and ask for a treaty; after a dispute over a well, they make a covenant at Beersheba, where Abraham plants a tamarisk and calls on the name of Yahweh, the Eternal God.

22.title: The Offering of Isaac
22.context: God tests Abraham, telling him to offer his only son Isaac; Abraham obeys, binds Isaac on Mount Moriah, and as he raises the knife the angel of Yahweh calls from heaven and provides a ram instead. Yahweh again promises countless offspring and blessing for all nations through them.

22.title: The Sons of Nahor
22.context: Abraham is told that Milcah has borne eight sons to his brother Nahor, among them Bethuel, who is the father of Rebekah.

23.title: The Death and Burial of Sarah
23.context: Sarah dies at 127 in Hebron in Canaan; Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah and its field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place and buries her there.

24.title: A Wife for Isaac
24.context: Abraham sends his senior servant to his own people to find a wife for Isaac. At the well the servant prays, Rebekah comes and answers the sign he asked for; she goes with him, marries Isaac, and he loves her.

25.title: Abraham and Keturah
25.context: Abraham takes another wife, Keturah, and has more sons; he leaves everything to Isaac and sends his other sons away to the east with gifts.

25.title: The Death of Abraham
25.context: Abraham dies at 175, old and full of years, and Isaac and Ishmael bury him in the cave of Machpelah.

25.title: The Descendants of Ishmael
25.context: Ishmael’s twelve sons become twelve tribal rulers according to their settlements and camps; Ishmael lives 137 years.

25.title: Jacob and Esau
25.context: Isaac marries Rebekah at forty, and twenty years later she conceives twins; Yahweh tells her two nations are in her womb and the older will serve the younger. Esau is born first, and Jacob follows, his hand gripping Esau’s heel.

25.title: Esau Sells His Birthright
25.context: Esau becomes a hunter and Jacob is a quiet man; Esau comes in from the field famished and trades his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of red stew.

26.title: God’s Promise to Isaac
26.context: Famine strikes; Yahweh appears to Isaac, tells him not to go to Egypt but to stay in Gerar, and renews the promise made to Abraham. He blesses Isaac, who sows and reaps a hundredfold.

26.title: Isaac’s Covenant with Abimelech
26.context: Abimelech comes with his advisor and army commander, having seen that Yahweh is with Isaac, and asks for a treaty; they swear an oath, and Isaac’s servants find water at Beersheba.

26.title: Esau’s Wives
26.context: At forty Esau marries two Hittite women, who make life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.

27.title: Isaac Blesses Jacob
27.context: Isaac is old and nearly blind and means to bless Esau; Rebekah overhears and helps Jacob disguise himself in Esau’s clothes and goatskins, and Jacob receives the blessing.

27.title: Esau’s Lost Hope
27.context: Esau returns from hunting, learns he has been deceived, and weeps bitterly; Isaac can give him only a lesser blessing, and Esau nurses a grudge and resolves to kill Jacob.

27.title: Isaac Sends Jacob to Laban's House
27.context: Weary of Esau’s Hittite wives, Rebekah tells Isaac that life would not be worth living if Jacob married one too; Isaac calls Jacob and sends him to Laban’s house to find a wife.

28.title: Esau Marries Mahalath
28.context: Seeing that Isaac has blessed Jacob and sent him off with orders not to marry a Canaanite, Esau takes another wife, Mahalath, Ishmael’s daughter.

28.title: Jacob’s Ladder
28.context: Jacob leaves Beersheba for Haran and sleeps with a stone for a pillow; he dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven, with angels ascending and descending and Yahweh above it, renewing the promise. He names the place Bethel and makes a vow.

29.title: Jacob Meets Rachel
29.context: Jacob reaches the land of the eastern peoples and meets Rachel at a well; he kisses her and weeps aloud, and stays with her father Laban.

29.title: Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel
29.context: Jacob offers to serve Laban seven years for Rachel; Laban gives him her older sister Leah instead, and Jacob serves another seven years for Rachel.

29.title: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah
29.context: Yahweh sees that Leah is unloved and opens her womb; she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah, while Rachel is at first childless, until God remembers her and she bears Joseph.

30.title: Jacob Prospers
30.context: After Joseph is born Jacob asks Laban to let him go home; they agree his wages will be the speckled and spotted animals, and Yahweh prospers him greatly in flocks, servants, camels and donkeys.

31.title: Jacob Flees from Laban
31.context: Jacob hears Laban’s sons complaining and sees Laban’s attitude has changed; Yahweh tells him to go back to his own land, and while Laban is shearing sheep Jacob slips away with his family and flocks. Rachel steals her father’s household gods.

31.title: Laban Pursues Jacob
31.context: Laban pursues and overtakes Jacob, but God warns him in a dream not to harm him. Laban searches for his gods, Rachel sits on them and they are not found, and Jacob rebukes Laban angrily.

31.title: Jacob’s Covenant with Laban
31.context: Jacob and Laban make a covenant, setting up a heap of stones and a pillar as witness and swearing not to harm each other; Jacob swears by the Fear of his father Isaac, offers a sacrifice, and shares a meal with his relatives.

32.title: Jacob Prepares to Meet Esau
32.context: Jacob meets angels of God and calls the place Mahanaim; he sends messengers ahead to Esau, and hearing that Esau is coming with four hundred men he is afraid, divides his camp, prays, and prepares gifts for Esau.

32.title: Jacob Wrestles with God
32.context: Alone at the ford of the Jabbok, Jacob wrestles with a man until daybreak; the man touches his hip so that he limps, and renames him Israel, because he has struggled with God and with men and prevailed. Jacob names the place Peniel.

33.title: Jacob Meets Esau
33.context: Esau comes with four hundred men; Jacob bows to the ground seven times, and Esau runs to meet him, embraces him and kisses him, and both weep. Jacob presses his gifts on Esau, and they part; Jacob goes on to Succoth and then to Shechem.

34.title: The Defiling of Dinah
34.context: Shechem defiles Jacob’s daughter Dinah and then wants to marry her; Jacob’s sons deceitfully require the men of the city to be circumcised, and on the third day Simeon and Levi kill all the males and the brothers plunder the city.

35.title: Jacob Returns to Bethel
35.context: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel and build an altar; Jacob has his household put away their foreign gods and purify themselves, and he builds the altar. God again names him Israel and renews the promise.

35.title: Benjamin Born, Rachel Dies
35.context: On the way to Ephrath Rachel goes into hard labor, gives birth to Benjamin and dies; Jacob buries her beside the road to Bethlehem.

35.title: The Sons of Jacob
35.context: While Israel lives in that region Reuben lies with his father’s concubine Bilhah; the twelve sons of Jacob are then listed.

35.title: The Death of Isaac
35.context: Jacob comes to his father Isaac at Mamre; Isaac dies at 180, old and full of years, and his sons Esau and Jacob bury him.

36.title: The Descendants of Esau
36.context: Esau, that is Edom, settles in the hill country of Seir; his descendants become the clans of Edom.

36.title: The Descendants of Seir
36.context: The sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in the land, are listed as the clan chiefs of the Horites.

36.title: The Kings of Edom
36.context: These are the kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king: Bela, Jobab, Husham, and others.

37.title: Joseph’s Dreams
37.context: Jacob loves Joseph more than his other sons and makes him a richly ornamented robe; Joseph has two dreams and tells them, and his brothers hate him all the more.

37.title: Joseph Sold into Egypt
37.context: Sent by his father to check on his brothers, Joseph finds them at Dothan; they plot to kill him, then sell him to Ishmaelite traders who take him to Egypt. They dip his robe in goat’s blood and show it to Jacob, who mourns many days.

38.title: Judah and Tamar
38.context: Judah leaves his brothers, marries a Canaanite woman and has three sons; Tamar’s first two husbands die by Yahweh’s hand, and Judah withholds his youngest son. Disguised as a prostitute she lies with Judah, conceives, and bears Perez and Zerah.

39.title: Joseph and Potiphar’s Wife
39.context: In Potiphar’s house Yahweh is with Joseph and everything he does succeeds; Potiphar’s wife repeatedly tempts him, and when he refuses she accuses him falsely and Potiphar has him put in prison, where Yahweh is still with him and gives him favor.

40.title: The Cupbearer and the Baker
40.context: Pharaoh’s cupbearer and baker offend him and are put in the prison where Joseph is; each has a dream, and Joseph interprets them by God’s help: the cupbearer is restored and the baker hanged, but the cupbearer forgets Joseph.

41.title: The Dreams of Pharaoh
41.context: Two years later Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows and seven lean cows, seven plump ears and seven withered; none of his wise men can interpret them. The cupbearer remembers Joseph, who says God is showing Pharaoh that seven years of plenty will be followed by seven of famine.

41.title: Joseph Given Charge of Egypt
41.context: Pharaoh sets Joseph over all Egypt and gives him an Egyptian name and a wife, Asenath; during the seven years of plenty Joseph stores up grain, and when the famine begins he opens the storehouses.

42.title: Joseph’s Brothers Sent to Egypt
42.context: Jacob hears there is grain in Egypt and sends ten sons to buy it, keeping Benjamin at home; Joseph recognizes his brothers but treats them as strangers, accuses them of spying, and keeps Simeon as a hostage until they bring their youngest brother.

42.title: Joseph’s Brothers Return to Canaan
42.context: Joseph has their sacks filled with grain and each man’s silver put back; on the way home they find the silver and are alarmed; back in Canaan Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go.

43.title: The Return to Egypt with Benjamin
43.context: The famine is severe and the grain runs out; Judah pledges himself for Benjamin, and Jacob reluctantly lets them go again with gifts, double the silver and Benjamin. Joseph sees Benjamin and has a meal prepared for them.

44.title: Benjamin and the Silver Cup
44.context: Joseph orders his silver cup put in Benjamin’s sack; the brothers are barely out of the city when his steward overtakes them and finds it, and they tear their clothes and return to Joseph.

44.title: Judah Pleads for Benjamin
44.context: Judah steps forward and tells Joseph how dearly their father loves Benjamin, offering to stay as a slave in his place so that he will not have to see his father’s anguish.

45.title: Joseph Reveals His Identity
45.context: Joseph can no longer control himself, sends everyone out, and tells his brothers, “I am Joseph,” saying God sent him ahead to preserve their lives; he tells them to bring their father down.

46.title: Jacob’s Journey to Egypt
46.context: Israel sets out with all his family and at Beersheba offers sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac; God tells him in a night vision not to fear going down to Egypt, where he will become a great nation. Seventy of Jacob’s family come to Egypt.

46.title: Jacob Arrives in Egypt
46.context: Jacob sends Judah ahead to Joseph; Joseph hitches his chariot and goes to meet his father, and they weep on each other’s necks. Joseph arranges for them to settle in Goshen.

47.title: The Famine Continues
47.context: The famine grows worse, and the Egyptians exhaust their silver, then their livestock, then their land and themselves to buy grain from Joseph; Pharaoh acquires the land, except the priests’ land.

47.title: The Israelites Prosper in Goshen
47.context: The Israelites settle in Goshen, acquire property and multiply greatly; Jacob lives seventeen years in Egypt and makes Joseph swear to bury him in the family tomb.

48.title: Jacob Blesses Ephraim and Manasseh
48.context: Jacob is ill and Joseph brings his sons Ephraim and Manasseh; Jacob adopts them as his own, crosses his hands, and puts his right hand on the younger, Ephraim, as he blesses them.

49.title: Jacob Blesses His Sons
49.context: Jacob calls his sons together and blesses each of the twelve, foretelling what will become of each tribe; of Judah he says the scepter will not depart from him.

49.title: The Death of Jacob
49.context: Jacob charges his sons to bury him in the cave of Machpelah; then he draws his feet up into the bed, breathes his last, and is gathered to his people. Joseph weeps over him and has him embalmed, and Egypt mourns him seventy days.

50.title: Joseph Comforts His Brothers
50.context: After Jacob dies, the brothers fear Joseph’s revenge and ask forgiveness; Joseph tells them that what they intended for harm God turned to good, to save many lives, and he reassures them.

50.title: The Death of Joseph
50.context: Joseph lives to 110 and sees Ephraim’s children to the third generation; before he dies he tells the Israelites that God will surely come to their aid and bring them up to the land he promised, and he makes them swear to carry his bones with them.

1.title: The Israelites Multiply in Egypt
1.context: Jacob’s descendants multiply in Egypt; a new king who does not know Joseph oppresses them with forced labor and orders the Hebrew midwives to kill the baby boys, but the midwives fear God and spare them.

2.title: The Birth and Adoption of Moses
2.context: A Levite baby is hidden for three months, then set afloat in a papyrus basket among the reeds; Pharaoh’s daughter finds him, hires his own mother to nurse him, and names him Moses, “drawn out of the water.”

2.title: The Rejection and Flight of Moses
2.context: Grown up, Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew and kills him; when it becomes known and Pharaoh seeks his life, he flees to Midian, helps the daughters of the priest Jethro at a well, and marries Zipporah.

3.title: Moses at the Burning Bush
3.context: While tending sheep at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed; the angel of Yahweh appears to him, Yahweh calls from the bush, sends him to deliver Israel, and reveals his name, “I AM WHO I AM.”

4.title: Moses’ Staff
4.context: Moses objects, and Yahweh gives him signs: his staff becomes a snake, his hand turns leprous, and water will become blood. When Moses pleads that he cannot speak well, Yahweh promises to help him and appoints Aaron as his spokesman.

4.title: Moses Leaves for Egypt
4.context: Moses takes leave of Jethro and sets out for Egypt with his wife and sons; on the way Yahweh confronts him, and Zipporah circumcises their son. Aaron meets Moses, and when they gather the elders and perform the signs, the people believe and bow down.

5.title: Pharaoh’s First Refusal
5.context: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh, “Let my people go”; Pharaoh answers that he does not know Yahweh and makes the work harder, withholding straw while demanding the same number of bricks.

5.title: Moses Complains to Yahweh
5.context: Israel’s foremen blame Moses and Aaron, and Moses brings his complaint to Yahweh, asking why he has made things worse for this people and why he sent him.

6.title: God Promises Deliverance
6.context: God tells Moses, “I am Yahweh,” who appeared to the patriarchs as God Almighty; he promises to free Israel from their burdens, to be their God, and to bring them to the land he swore to give. But the people, crushed by their labor, do not listen.

6.title: Genealogies of Moses and Aaron
6.context: The heads of the families of Reuben, Simeon and Levi are listed, with special attention to Levi’s line, from which Moses and Aaron come.

6.title: Yahweh Instructs Moses and Aaron
6.context: In Egypt Yahweh again speaks to Moses and tells him to say to Pharaoh all that Yahweh commands; Moses protests that he speaks poorly and Pharaoh will not listen.

7.title: Aaron’s Staff
7.context: Yahweh has Aaron throw down his staff before Pharaoh, and it becomes a snake; Pharaoh’s magicians do the same with their staffs, but Aaron’s staff swallows theirs. Pharaoh’s heart remains hard.

7.title: The First Plague: Blood
7.context: Yahweh sends Moses to Pharaoh at the river; Moses strikes the Nile with his staff and the water turns to blood, the fish die, the river stinks and the Egyptians cannot drink from it.

8.title: The Second Plague: Frogs
8.context: Yahweh makes frogs come up from the river and cover Egypt; Pharaoh begs Moses to pray and promises to let the people go, but once the frogs are gone he hardens his heart again.

8.title: The Third Plague: Gnats
8.context: Aaron strikes the dust with his staff and it becomes gnats throughout Egypt; the magicians cannot imitate it and say, “This is the finger of God,” but Pharaoh does not listen.

8.title: The Fourth Plague: Flies
8.context: Yahweh sends swarms of flies on the Egyptians but spares Goshen, where Israel lives; Pharaoh agrees to let them sacrifice, but when the flies are gone he again refuses.

9.title: The Fifth Plague: Livestock
9.context: Yahweh’s hand strikes the Egyptians’ livestock with a plague, but none of Israel’s animals die; Pharaoh’s heart stays hard.

9.title: The Sixth Plague: Boils
9.context: Moses tosses handfuls of ash into the air, and festering boils break out on people and animals; the magicians cannot stand before Moses, and Yahweh hardens Pharaoh’s heart.

9.title: The Seventh Plague: Hail
9.context: Yahweh warns Pharaoh of a devastating hailstorm; those who fear his word bring their servants and livestock inside, and the rest suffer. Pharaoh admits “I have sinned,” but when the hail stops he sins again and hardens his heart.

10.title: The Eighth Plague: Locusts
10.context: Locusts cover Egypt and devour whatever the hail left; Pharaoh calls for Moses and Aaron, confesses his sin and asks for prayer, then changes his mind once more.

10.title: The Ninth Plague: Darkness
10.context: At Yahweh’s word Moses stretches out his hand toward the sky, and thick darkness covers Egypt for three days, while the Israelites have light where they live. Pharaoh refuses to let their livestock go and drives Moses away.

11.title: The Plague on the Firstborn Foretold
11.context: Yahweh tells Moses one more plague will bring Pharaoh to let them go, and the Israelites ask their neighbors for silver and gold. Moses warns Pharaoh that at midnight every firstborn in Egypt will die, while not even a dog will bark at the Israelites.

12.title: The First Passover
12.context: Yahweh tells Israel that on the fourteenth day of the first month each household is to slaughter an unblemished year-old lamb, put its blood on the doorposts and lintels, and eat the meat with unleavened bread and bitter herbs; when he sees the blood, he will pass over that house.

12.title: The Feast of Unleavened Bread
12.context: The day is to be kept as a lasting memorial and a feast to Yahweh; for seven days they eat bread without yeast, remove yeast from their houses on the first day, and hold a sacred assembly.

12.title: The Israelites Keep the Passover
12.context: Moses summons Israel’s elders and tells them to slaughter the Passover lamb and apply its blood with hyssop to the doorframes; when their children ask later, they are to explain that Yahweh passed over Israel’s houses. The people bow down in worship.

12.title: The Tenth Plague: Death of the Firstborn
12.context: At midnight Yahweh strikes down every firstborn in Egypt, and there is loud wailing in the land; Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron that night and orders Israel out, and the Egyptians urge them to hurry, giving them silver, gold and clothing.

12.title: The Israelites Leave Egypt
12.context: The Israelites set out from Rameses toward Succoth, about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children, along with a mixed crowd and large herds. They had lived in Egypt 430 years, and on that very day all Yahweh’s divisions left.

12.title: Instructions for the Passover
12.context: The rules for the Passover: no foreigner or hired worker may eat it, a slave may eat after being circumcised, it is eaten inside a single house, and no bone is to be broken; a resident alien who wants to keep it must have all his males circumcised.

13.title: The Dedication of the Firstborn
13.context: Yahweh tells Moses to consecrate to him every firstborn male among the Israelites, of people and of animals.

13.title: The Feast of Unleavened Bread
13.context: Moses tells the people to remember the day they left Egypt, to eat unleavened bread for seven days, and to explain to their children how Yahweh brought them out with a mighty hand, so that it is a sign on the hand and a reminder on the forehead.

13.title: The Firstborn
13.context: After Yahweh brings them into Canaan, the firstborn of livestock belong to him: a donkey is redeemed with a lamb, and every firstborn son is redeemed; when children ask, parents explain how Yahweh killed Egypt’s firstborn.

13.title: The Pillars of Cloud and Fire
13.context: After Pharaoh lets the people go, God does not lead them by the short road through Philistine territory, lest they see war and turn back, but by the desert road toward the Red Sea; Moses takes Joseph’s bones. By day Yahweh goes ahead in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire.

14.title: Pharaoh Pursues the Israelites
14.context: Pharaoh regrets letting Israel go and pursues them to the sea; Moses tells the people to stand firm and watch Yahweh save them. The sea parts, Israel crosses on dry ground, the pursuing army drowns, and the people fear Yahweh and trust Moses.

15.title: The Song at the Sea
15.context: Moses and the Israelites sing to Yahweh, who is their strength, song and salvation; he has hurled Pharaoh’s chariots into the sea and will bring his people to his holy dwelling. “Yahweh will reign forever and ever.”

15.title: Miriam's Song
15.context: Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, leads the women with tambourines and dancing, singing of Yahweh’s great victory.

15.title: The Waters of Marah
15.context: Israel walks three days in the Desert of Shur without water; at Marah the water is bitter and the people grumble. Yahweh shows Moses a piece of wood, which he throws into the water to make it sweet, and says, “I am Yahweh, who heals you.” They then come to Elim.

16.title: Manna and Quail from Heaven
16.context: In the Desert of Sin the people grumble for lack of food; Yahweh promises bread from heaven, quail in the evening and manna in the morning, to be gathered day by day, a double portion on the sixth day and none on the seventh.

17.title: Water from the Rock
17.context: At Rephidim there is no water, and the people quarrel with Moses and test Yahweh; at Yahweh’s word Moses strikes the rock at Horeb with his staff and water flows out. He names the place Massah and Meribah.

17.title: The Defeat of the Amalekites
17.context: The Amalekites attack Israel at Rephidim; Joshua leads the fighting while Moses, Aaron and Hur go up the hill, and as long as Moses holds up his hands Israel prevails. Aaron and Hur support his hands until sunset, and Joshua overcomes Amalek.

18.title: The Visit of Jethro
18.context: Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, priest of Midian, brings Moses’ wife and two sons to him in the wilderness; hearing all Yahweh has done for Israel he rejoices, declares Yahweh greater than all gods, and offers sacrifices, sharing a meal with Aaron and the elders before God.

18.title: Jethro Advises Moses
18.context: The next day Moses sits to judge the people from morning to evening; Jethro advises him to choose capable men who fear God and hate dishonest gain as officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, to judge minor cases while he handles the difficult ones. Moses follows his advice.

19.title: Israel at Mount Sinai
19.context: In the third month Israel camps at Sinai; Yahweh promises that if they keep his covenant they will be his treasured people, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation, and on the third day he descends on the mountain in thunder, cloud and trumpet blast.

20.title: The Ten Commandments
20.context: At Sinai Yahweh gives the Ten Commandments: no other gods, no idols, no misuse of his name, the Sabbath, honoring parents, and no murder, adultery, theft, false testimony or coveting.

20.title: Moses Comforts the People
20.context: Terrified by the thunder and smoking mountain, the people ask Moses to speak to them instead of God; Moses says God has come to test them, so that the fear of him will keep them from sin.

20.title: Idolatry Forbidden
20.context: Yahweh tells Moses to say to the Israelites that they are not to make gods of silver or gold to be alongside him; they are to build him an altar of earth or of uncut stone, and not to climb to it by steps.

21.title: Hebrew Servants
21.context: The laws Moses is to set before Israel: a Hebrew servant serves six years and goes free in the seventh; if he loves his master and wishes to stay, his ear is pierced at the door and he serves for life; the rights of female servants are also set out.

21.title: Personal Injury Laws
21.context: Laws about violence: whoever strikes a person dead is put to death, as are those who strike or curse their parents or kidnap; injuries in a fight require compensation, a slave whose eye or tooth is destroyed goes free, and the law of a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth limits retribution.

21.title: The Owner's Responsibility
21.context: If an ox gores someone to death the ox is stoned and the owner is not liable; if the owner knew it was dangerous and did not restrain it, he is also held accountable, though he may redeem his life by a set price. Rules follow for an ox killing another’s ox or an animal falling into an open pit.

22.title: Property Laws
22.context: Theft of an ox or sheep requires several-fold restitution; a thief breaking in at night may be killed without bloodguilt; the laws also cover damage by grazing and fire, goods entrusted to another, and animals borrowed, hired or lost.

22.title: Laws of Social Responsibility
22.context: Laws on seduction, sorcery, bestiality and sacrificing to other gods; the people must not wrong foreigners, widows or orphans, nor charge interest to the poor, and a cloak taken in pledge is returned by sunset. They are not to blaspheme God or curse a ruler, and the firstfruits and firstborn belong to Yahweh.

23.title: Justice and Mercy
23.context: Israel must not spread false reports, follow the crowd in wrongdoing, show partiality to the poor or pervert justice for them; they are to return an enemy’s straying ox or donkey, and not oppress the foreigner, remembering they were foreigners in Egypt.

23.title: Sabbath Laws
23.context: For six years Israel sows and harvests, but in the seventh the land is left unplowed so that the poor may eat from it; they work six days and rest on the seventh, so that ox, donkey, slave and foreigner may be refreshed.

23.title: The Three Feasts of Pilgrimage
23.context: Three times a year all males are to appear before Yahweh: the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the crops, and the Feast of Ingathering at the year’s end; none are to come empty-handed.

23.title: God’s Angel to Lead
23.context: Yahweh says he is sending an angel ahead to guard Israel on the way and bring them to the place he has prepared; they are to listen to him, for Yahweh’s name is in him. If they obey, Yahweh will be an enemy to their enemies; they are not to serve the gods of the land but to demolish them.

24.title: The Covenant Sealed
24.context: The people promise to do all Yahweh has said; Moses builds an altar, sprinkles them with the blood of the covenant, and he, Aaron and seventy elders go up the mountain, see the God of Israel and eat and drink there.

24.title: Moses on the Mountain
24.context: Yahweh summons Moses up the mountain to receive tablets of stone with the law; Moses goes up with Joshua, the cloud covers the mountain for six days, and on the seventh Yahweh calls him from the cloud, his glory like a consuming fire on the peak. Moses is on the mountain forty days and nights.

25.title: Offerings for the Tabernacle
25.context: Yahweh tells Moses to take offerings from all whose hearts prompt them: gold, silver, bronze, colored yarn, fine linen, skins, acacia wood, oil, spices and gems, so that Israel may make a sanctuary for him and he may dwell among them.

25.title: The Ark of the Covenant
25.context: They are to make an ark of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with rings and poles for carrying it, to hold the tablets of the testimony; on top is a gold atonement cover with two cherubim, and there Yahweh will meet with Moses.

25.title: The Table of Showbread
25.context: A table of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with its dishes, bowls, pitchers and jars, is to hold the bread of the Presence, kept before Yahweh at all times.

25.title: The Lampstand
25.context: A lampstand of pure gold hammered out in one piece, with cups, buds and blossoms and six branches, holding seven lamps; Moses is to make it according to the pattern shown him on the mountain.

26.title: The Ten Curtains for the Tabernacle
26.context: The tabernacle is to be made of ten curtains of fine linen and colored yarn with cherubim worked in, covered with goat-hair curtains and skins, supported by frames of acacia wood on silver bases; a veil separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, where the ark is kept.

27.title: The Bronze Altar
27.context: An altar of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, with horns at its four corners, a bronze grating, rings and carrying poles, hollow and made as shown on the mountain.

27.title: The Courtyard
27.context: The courtyard of the tabernacle is enclosed by fine linen hangings, a hundred cubits long and fifty wide, on bronze bases with silver hooks and rods; its gate is a screen of colored yarn and fine linen.

27.title: The Oil for the Lamps
27.context: Israel is to bring pure oil of pressed olives so the lamp may be kept burning continually; Aaron and his sons are to tend it in the tent of meeting from evening till morning before Yahweh.

28.title: Garments for the Priests
28.context: Aaron and his four sons are set apart as priests, and holy garments are made for them: ephod, breastpiece, robe, tunic, turban and sash, of gold and colored yarn and fine linen; on the shoulder pieces of the ephod are two onyx stones engraved with the names of Israel’s twelve tribes.

28.title: The Breastpiece
28.context: The breastpiece of judgment is woven of gold and colored yarn, square, set with four rows of three gems each, engraved with the twelve tribes’ names; the Urim and Thummim are put in it, and Aaron carries the names of Israel over his heart before Yahweh.

28.title: Additional Priestly Garments
28.context: The robe of the ephod is blue, with pomegranates and gold bells along its hem that sound as Aaron ministers; a gold plate engraved “HOLY TO YAHWEH” is fastened to the turban, and tunics, sashes, headbands and linen undergarments are made for the priests.

29.title: Consecration of the Priests
29.context: The ordination of the priests: Aaron and his sons are washed, clothed, anointed, and consecrated over seven days with sin, burnt and ordination offerings; Yahweh promises to dwell among the Israelites.

29.title: The Daily Offerings
29.context: Every day, morning and evening, two year-old lambs are offered with flour, oil and wine as a regular burnt offering; there at the entrance of the tent of meeting Yahweh will meet Israel and speak with them.

30.title: The Altar of Incense
30.context: An altar of acacia wood overlaid with gold is made for burning incense, set before the veil; Aaron burns fragrant incense on it each morning and evening, and once a year makes atonement on its horns.

30.title: The Census Offering
30.context: When Israel is counted, each man twenty or older gives half a shekel to Yahweh as a ransom for his life, the rich no more and the poor no less, for the service of the tent of meeting.

30.title: The Bronze Basin
30.context: A bronze basin with a bronze stand is made and placed between the tent of meeting and the altar, filled with water; Aaron and his sons wash their hands and feet before entering or approaching the altar, so that they will not die.

30.title: The Anointing Oil
30.context: Holy anointing oil is prepared from myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil, and used to consecrate the tent, the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars and their utensils, and to anoint Aaron and his sons as priests; it is not to be poured on ordinary people or imitated.

30.title: The Incense
30.context: Fragrant spices with pure frankincense are blended into holy incense, part of it placed before the testimony in the tent of meeting; it is holy to Yahweh, and anyone who makes it for himself is cut off from his people.

31.title: Bezalel and Oholiab
31.context: Yahweh calls Bezalel of Judah by name and fills him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability and knowledge in every craft; he appoints Oholiab of Dan to work with him and gives wisdom to all the skilled workers to make everything he has commanded.

31.title: The Sign of the Sabbath
31.context: Yahweh tells Israel to keep his Sabbaths as a sign between him and them for all generations, showing that he makes them holy; then he gives Moses the two tablets of the testimony.

32.title: The Golden Calf
32.context: While Moses delays on the mountain, Aaron casts a golden calf from the people’s earrings and they worship it; Moses intercedes for them, then comes down, breaks the tablets and destroys the calf, the Levites rally to Yahweh, and many die.

33.title: The Command to Leave Sinai
33.context: Yahweh tells Moses to lead the people from Sinai to the land he promised, sending an angel ahead but not going with them himself, since they are stiff-necked; when the people hear this they mourn and put off their ornaments.

33.title: The Tent of Meeting
33.context: Moses pitches the tent of meeting outside the camp, far away; anyone seeking Yahweh goes there. When Moses enters, the pillar of cloud comes down at its entrance, and Yahweh speaks with him face to face, as one speaks with a friend.

33.title: The Promise of God’s Presence
33.context: Moses asks Yahweh to go with them in person and to show him his glory; Yahweh agrees to go and to proclaim his name before him, but no one may see his face, so he shelters Moses in a cleft of the rock as his glory passes.

34.title: New Stone Tablets
34.context: Moses cuts two new stone tablets and goes up the mountain; Yahweh descends and proclaims his name — compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness — and Moses bows in worship and asks for pardon and his presence.

34.title: Yahweh Renews the Covenant
34.context: Yahweh renews the covenant, promising unheard-of wonders; Israel must make no treaty with the land’s inhabitants and worship no other god, and must keep the feasts, the firstborn laws and the seventh-day rest; Moses stays forty days, and the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments, are written on the tablets.

34.title: Moses Comes Down from Sinai
34.context: When Moses comes down from Sinai with the tablets, he does not know his face is radiant from speaking with Yahweh; Aaron and the Israelites are afraid to approach him, so after speaking to them he puts a veil over his face, and removes it when he goes in before Yahweh.

35.title: The Sabbath
35.context: Moses assembles the whole Israelite community and gives Yahweh’s commands: six days are for work, but the seventh is a holy sabbath of rest to Yahweh, and no fire is to be kindled in their homes on it.

35.title: Offerings for the Tabernacle
35.context: Moses tells the community that everyone who is willing may bring an offering to Yahweh: gold, silver, bronze, colored yarn, linen, skins, acacia wood, oil, spices and gems for the tabernacle.

35.title: The Skilled Craftsmen
35.context: All who are skilled are invited to come and make everything Yahweh has commanded: the tabernacle, its covering, the ark, table, lampstand, altars, basin, courtyard and the priestly garments.

35.title: The People Offer Gifts
35.context: The Israelites leave Moses’ presence, and everyone whose heart is stirred brings an offering to Yahweh; men and women bring rings, earrings and gold ornaments, and skilled women spin yarn and linen with their own hands.

35.title: Bezalel and Oholiab
35.context: Moses tells Israel that Yahweh has chosen Bezalel of Judah, filled him with the Spirit of God and given him the ability to teach others, together with Oholiab of Dan.

36.title: The People Bring More than Enough
36.context: Moses calls Bezalel, Oholiab and all the skilled workers to the task; the people keep bringing freewill offerings every morning until the craftsmen report there is more than enough, and Moses has an order sent through the camp that no one bring more.

36.title: The Ten Curtains for the Tabernacle
36.context: The skilled workers make the tabernacle as Yahweh commanded: ten linen curtains, the goat-hair covering, the ram-skin cover, the acacia frames and crossbars, and the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

37.title: Constructing the Ark
37.context: Bezalel makes the ark of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with its rings and poles, and the atonement cover with two cherubim whose wings spread over it.

37.title: The Table of Showbread
37.context: Bezalel makes the table of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with its rim, rings and poles, and the gold utensils for the table.

37.title: The Lampstand
37.context: Bezalel hammers out the lampstand of pure gold with its cups, buds, blossoms and six branches, along with its seven lamps, wick trimmers and trays.

37.title: The Altar of Incense
37.context: Bezalel makes the incense altar of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with horns at its four corners, a gold molding, and gold rings and poles.

37.title: The Holy Oil and Incense
37.context: He also makes the sacred anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, in the way a perfumer does.

38.title: The Bronze Altar
38.context: Bezalel makes the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, with horns at its corners, and all its utensils of bronze.

38.title: The Bronze Basin
38.context: He makes the bronze basin and its stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

38.title: The Courtyard
38.context: He makes the courtyard with hangings of fine linen on the south, north, west and east sides, supported by bronze bases with silver hooks and rods.

38.title: An Inventory of Materials
38.context: The materials used for the tabernacle of the testimony are tallied by the Levites under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest; the gold, silver and bronze donated by the people are recorded as used for the work of the sanctuary.

39.title: The Ephod
39.context: They make the woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, and holy garments for Aaron, as Yahweh commanded Moses, beginning with the ephod made of gold and colored yarn.

39.title: The Breastpiece
39.context: They make the breastpiece of gold and colored yarn, set with four rows of gems engraved with the names of Israel’s twelve tribes like the engravings of a seal.

39.title: Additional Priestly Garments
39.context: They make the robe of the ephod, the tunics, turban, undergarments and sash, and the pure gold plate inscribed “HOLY TO YAHWEH,” as Yahweh commanded Moses.

39.title: Moses Approves the Work
39.context: All the work on the tabernacle is completed; the Israelites do everything just as Yahweh commanded Moses. They bring it and all its furnishings to Moses, who inspects the work, sees that it has been done as Yahweh commanded, and blesses them.

40.title: Setting Up the Tabernacle
40.context: Yahweh tells Moses to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month: place the ark, hang the veil, arrange the table and lampstand, set the altars and basin, put up the courtyard, anoint everything, and wash, clothe and anoint Aaron and his sons as priests. Moses does it all as Yahweh commanded.

40.title: The Cloud and the Glory
40.context: The cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of Yahweh fills the tabernacle, so that Moses cannot enter. Whenever the cloud lifts, the Israelites set out; if it does not, they stay; by day the cloud of Yahweh is over the tabernacle, and by night there is fire in it, in the sight of all Israel.

1.title: Laws for Burnt Offerings
1.context: Yahweh calls to Moses from the tent of meeting and speaks of the burnt offering: an unblemished bull, sheep, goat or bird, with the worshiper laying a hand on its head so that it is accepted on his behalf. The whole animal is burned on the altar as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

2.title: Laws for Grain Offerings
2.context: The grain offering is fine flour with oil and incense; the priest burns a handful as a memorial portion. No yeast or honey is allowed, every offering is seasoned with salt, the salt of the covenant, and firstfruits may also be offered.

3.title: Laws for Peace Offerings
3.context: The fellowship offering may be a bull, lamb or goat without defect; the worshiper lays a hand on it, it is slaughtered at the entrance of the tent, and its fat is burned on the altar. Fat and blood are never to be eaten — a lasting ordinance.

4.title: Laws for Sin Offerings
4.context: When someone sins unintentionally against any of Yahweh’s commands — the anointed priest, the whole community, a leader or an ordinary person — a sin offering is made, with blood sprinkled and applied to the altar’s horns, according to the person’s position, and the sin is forgiven.

5.title: Sins Requiring a Sin Offering
5.context: Those who fail to testify, touch what is unclean, or swear rashly must confess when they realize their guilt and bring a lamb, doves or flour as a sin offering according to their means; unintentional offenses against the holy things or Yahweh’s commands call for a guilt offering.

6.title: The Burnt Offering
6.context: Instructions for the priests: the burnt offering stays on the altar all night, the fire is never to go out, and in the morning the priest in linen garments removes the ashes to a clean place outside the camp.

6.title: The Grain Offering
6.context: Instructions for the grain offering: the priest burns a handful of the flour and oil with incense, and Aaron’s sons eat the rest without yeast in a holy place, for it is most holy.

6.title: The Sin Offering
6.context: Instructions for the sin offering: it is slaughtered where the burnt offering is, most holy, and the priest who offers it eats it in the sacred courtyard; if its blood is brought into the tent of meeting, the meat is burned instead of eaten.

7.title: The Guilt Offering
7.context: Instructions for the guilt offering: it is slaughtered where the burnt offering is, its blood sprinkled on the altar’s sides and its fat burned; the male priests eat the meat, most holy.

7.title: The Peace Offering
7.context: Instructions for the fellowship offering: a thanksgiving offering is eaten the same day, a vow or freewill offering may be eaten the next day, and leftovers on the third day are burned; fat and blood are forbidden, while the breast and right thigh go to the priests.

8.title: Moses Consecrates Aaron and His Sons
8.context: Yahweh has Moses assemble the community and consecrate Aaron and his sons: washing them, clothing them, anointing them with oil, and offering a sin offering, a burnt offering and an ordination offering. For seven days they stay at the entrance of the tent, as Yahweh commanded.

9.title: Aaron’s First Offerings
9.context: On the eighth day Aaron offers a sin offering, burnt offering and fellowship offering for himself and the people, and blesses them. The glory of Yahweh appears, and fire comes out from his presence to consume the offering; the people shout and fall facedown.

10.title: The Sin of Nadab and Abihu
10.context: Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire before Yahweh, which he had not commanded, and fire comes out from Yahweh and consumes them. Aaron is silent as Moses speaks of Yahweh being honored as holy.

10.title: Restrictions for Priests
10.context: Yahweh tells Aaron that neither he nor his sons may drink wine when entering the tent of meeting, so that they can distinguish the holy from the common and the clean from the unclean and teach Israel; Moses then instructs them on how the offerings are to be eaten.

11.title: Clean and Unclean Animals
11.context: Yahweh tells Moses and Aaron which land animals, water creatures, birds and crawling things may be eaten and which are unclean, and says, “Be holy, because I am holy.”

12.title: Purification after Childbirth
12.context: After childbirth a woman is ceremonially unclean for a period, with the boy circumcised on the eighth day; when the days of purification are over she brings a lamb and a dove or pigeon, and the priest makes atonement for her.

13.title: Laws about Skin Diseases
13.context: When someone has a swelling, rash or bright spot on the skin, the priest examines it and pronounces the person clean or unclean; an unclean person lives apart, with torn clothes and covered lips, calling out “Unclean!”

13.title: Laws about Mildew
13.context: When a garment or leather shows a spreading mildew, the priest examines it; if it spreads it is burned, and if it does not, the item is washed and set aside another seven days.

14.title: Cleansing from Skin Diseases
14.context: When someone is healed of a skin disease, the priest goes out of the camp to examine him and performs the cleansing ritual with two live birds, cedar, scarlet yarn and hyssop; on the eighth day offerings are made, with blood and oil applied to the right ear, thumb and big toe.

14.title: Signs of Home Contamination
14.context: If a house has a spreading mildew, the priest inspects it; if it persists, the house is torn down and its materials taken outside the town, but if it is gone, the house is cleansed with birds, cedar and hyssop and declared clean.

15.title: The Uncleanness of Men
15.context: A man with a bodily discharge is unclean, and so is anything he lies on, sits on or touches; he washes and bathes, and after he is healed counts seven days, then on the eighth brings two doves or pigeons for a sin offering and a burnt offering.

16.title: The Day of Atonement
16.context: After the death of Aaron’s two sons, Yahweh warns that Aaron must not enter the Most Holy Place whenever he chooses, or he will die; he comes in with a sin offering for himself and takes two goats from the community, casting lots, one for Yahweh and one for the scapegoat.

16.title: The Scapegoat
16.context: Aaron lays both hands on the live goat, confesses over it all the iniquities and rebellions of Israel, and sends it away into the wilderness by a man appointed; the goat carries their sins to a remote place.

16.title: Keeping the Day of Atonement
16.context: On the tenth day of the seventh month the people are to humble themselves and do no work, for on this day atonement is made to cleanse them from all their sins before Yahweh. It is a lasting ordinance, once a year.

17.title: The Place of Sacrifice
17.context: Yahweh commands that animals for sacrifice be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting rather than offered in the open fields to goat idols; no one may eat blood, for the life of a creature is in the blood, which Yahweh has given on the altar to make atonement.

18.title: Unlawful Sexual Relations
18.context: Yahweh tells Israel not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan: it lists forbidden sexual relations, offering children to Molech, and bestiality, warning that such things defile the land, which will vomit out its inhabitants.

19.title: Commandments for Holiness
19.context: “Be holy, for I, Yahweh, am holy”: holiness is shown in honoring parents, keeping the Sabbath, honesty, refusing to oppress or hate, not taking revenge, loving one’s neighbor as oneself, and care for the poor, the foreigner and the elderly.

20.title: Punishments for Disobedience
20.context: Penalties are set for giving children to Molech, consulting mediums, cursing parents, adultery and incest; Israel must be holy, because Yahweh has set them apart from the nations.

21.title: Holiness Required of Priests
21.context: Priests are not to make themselves unclean for the dead except for close relatives, the high priest not even for them; the priests are to marry within certain limits, and a priest with a physical defect may eat the holy food but not approach the altar.

22.title: Restrictions against the Unclean
22.context: Priests who are unclean may not eat the holy offerings, and neither may outsiders; the animals offered to Yahweh must be without defect, and Yahweh’s holy name is not to be profaned.

23.title: Feasts and Sabbaths
23.context: Yahweh gives Moses the appointed feasts, the sacred assemblies Israel is to proclaim at their set times, beginning with the weekly sabbath, a day of rest and sacred assembly.

23.title: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread
23.context: The Passover of Yahweh begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread follows on the fifteenth for seven days, with sacred assemblies on the first and last days.

23.title: The Feast of Weeks
23.context: Fifty days after the offering of the firstfruits sheaf, Israel presents a new grain offering to Yahweh and holds a sacred assembly; at harvest they are to leave the edges of the field for the poor and the foreigner.

23.title: The Feast of Trumpets
23.context: The first day of the seventh month is a day of rest and a sacred assembly announced with trumpet blasts, with no regular work and an offering made to Yahweh by fire.

23.title: The Day of Atonement
23.context: The tenth day of the seventh month is the Day of Atonement, a sacred assembly when the people humble themselves and do no work; anyone who does not is cut off from his people.

23.title: The Feast of Tabernacles
23.context: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month the Feast of Tabernacles begins, lasting seven days with a sacred assembly on the first and eighth days; the people live in booths so that future generations know Yahweh made Israel live in booths when he brought them out of Egypt.

24.title: The Oil for the Lamps
24.context: Yahweh tells Moses that Israel is to bring pure oil of pressed olives for the lamps so that they burn continually; Aaron tends them before Yahweh from evening till morning.

24.title: The Showbread
24.context: Twelve loaves of fine flour are baked and set in two rows of six on the pure gold table before Yahweh, replaced every sabbath as a lasting covenant; the bread belongs to Aaron and his sons, who eat it in a holy place.

24.title: Punishment for Blasphemy
24.context: The son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father blasphemes the Name in a fight and is held until Yahweh’s will is known; Yahweh orders him taken outside the camp and stoned by the community, and sets down laws on blasphemy, killing and injury that apply equally to native-born and foreigner.

25.title: The Seventh Year
25.context: On Mount Sinai Yahweh tells Moses that when Israel enters the land, they sow and harvest for six years but in the seventh the land is to have a sabbath rest to Yahweh, and whatever grows of itself is food for all.

25.title: The Year of Jubilee
25.context: After seven sabbath years, on the Day of Atonement in the fiftieth year, a trumpet announces the Jubilee: everyone returns to his property and family, land is not sold permanently because it belongs to Yahweh, and no one is to wrong another.

25.title: The Blessing of Obedience
25.context: Yahweh promises that if Israel follows his decrees they will live safely in the land, and in the sixth year he will command such a blessing that the harvest lasts three years.

25.title: The Law of Redemption
25.context: The land must not be sold permanently, for it belongs to Yahweh and Israel are only his tenants; if someone becomes poor and sells his property, a close relative may redeem it, and in any case it returns in the Jubilee.

25.title: Redemption of the Poor
25.context: If a fellow Israelite becomes poor, he is to be supported as a foreigner, with no interest charged on loans or profit on food, because Yahweh brought them out of Egypt to be their God.

25.title: Redemption of Bondmen
25.context: If an Israelite sells himself to you, you are not to make him serve as a slave but as a hired worker, and he and his children go free in the Jubilee, for they are Yahweh’s servants whom he brought out of Egypt; non-Israelite slaves may be held as property, but fellow Israelites are not to be ruled harshly.

26.title: Additional Blessings of Obedience
26.context: Israel is not to make idols or carved images, but to keep Yahweh’s sabbaths and revere his sanctuary; if they follow his decrees, he will send rain in season, give abundant harvests and peace in the land, and walk among them as their God.

26.title: Punishments for Disobedience
26.context: If Israel does not listen and carry out Yahweh’s commands, he warns of terror, disease, defeat and drought, with discipline multiplying sevenfold if they persist; yet if they confess their sin, he will remember his covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham and with the land.

27.title: Rules about Valuations
27.context: Rules for vows to Yahweh and the value set on persons, animals, houses and fields by the sanctuary shekel, according to age and sex; firstborn animals cannot be vowed, what is devoted to destruction cannot be redeemed, and a tenth of the land’s produce and of the herds and flocks belongs to Yahweh.

1.title: The First Census of Israel
1.context: On the first day of the second month of the second year after leaving Egypt, Yahweh tells Moses in the Sinai wilderness to count the men twenty and older who can serve in battle, by tribe and clan: 603,550 in all, with the Levites not counted among them but placed in charge of the tabernacle.

2.title: The Order of the Camps
2.context: Yahweh tells each tribe to camp under its banner around the tent of meeting at a distance: Judah, Issachar and Zebulun to the east, Reuben, Simeon and Gad to the south, Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin to the west, Dan, Asher and Naphtali to the north, with the Levites in the center when they march.

3.title: The Sons of Aaron
3.context: The sons of Aaron are Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar; Nadab and Abihu died childless when they offered unauthorized fire, and Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests under their father.

3.title: The Duties of the Levites
3.context: Yahweh tells Moses to present the tribe of Levi to Aaron the priest to assist him in the work at the tabernacle and care for its furnishings; the Levites are given to Yahweh in place of every firstborn Israelite.

3.title: The Numbering of the Levites
3.context: Yahweh has Moses count all Levite males a month old or more — 22,000 — according to the clans of Gershon, Kohath and Merari, each assigned its camping place and charge.

3.title: The Redemption of the Firstborn
3.context: The Israelite firstborn males number 22,273, which exceeds the Levites by 273; Yahweh has Moses collect five shekels each for the extra and give the money to Aaron and his sons.

4.title: The Duties of the Kohathites
4.context: Kohathites between thirty and fifty serve at the tent of meeting, carrying the most holy things; Aaron and his sons first cover the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altars, and the Kohathites must not touch the holy objects lest they die.

4.title: The Duties of the Gershonites
4.context: The Gershonites between thirty and fifty carry the curtains, coverings and hangings of the tabernacle and the courtyard, under Ithamar son of Aaron.

4.title: The Duties of the Merarites
4.context: The Merarites between thirty and fifty carry the frames, crossbars, posts and bases of the tabernacle and the courtyard’s posts, bases, tent pegs and ropes, also under Ithamar.

4.title: The Numbering of the Levite Clans
4.context: Moses, Aaron and the leaders count the Kohathites, Gershonites and Merarites between thirty and fifty who can serve — 8,580 men in all.

5.title: Cleansing the Camps
5.context: Yahweh commands that those with skin diseases, discharges, or contact with a dead body be sent outside the camp so they do not defile the camp where he dwells.

5.title: Confession and Restitution
5.context: When someone wrongs another and so is unfaithful to Yahweh, he must confess, make full restitution plus a fifth, and give it to the one wronged, or, if there is no relative, to Yahweh for the priest.

5.title: The Adultery Test
5.context: If a husband suspects his wife of unfaithfulness without evidence, he brings her to the priest with a barley offering; she stands before Yahweh and takes an oath and drinks the water, and if she is innocent she is unharmed and will conceive.

6.title: The Nazirite Vow
6.context: A man or woman who takes the special vow of a Nazirite to be set apart to Yahweh abstains from wine, does not cut the hair, and avoids contact with the dead; when the period ends, the Nazirite brings offerings and shaves the head, putting the hair on the fire of the fellowship offering.

6.title: Aaron’s Blessing
6.context: The priestly blessing Aaron and his sons are to speak over Israel asks Yahweh to bless and keep them, make his face shine on them, and give them grace and peace — so placing his name on the people.

7.title: Offerings of Dedication
7.context: After the tabernacle is set up and anointed, the tribal leaders bring wagons and oxen for the Levites and, one leader a day for twelve days, present identical dedication offerings; when Moses enters the tent to speak with Yahweh, he hears the voice speaking to him from above the atonement cover.

8.title: The Lampstand
8.context: Yahweh tells Aaron how to set up the seven lamps so that they light the area in front of the lampstand, and Aaron does so as Yahweh commanded Moses.

8.title: Cleansing the Levites
8.context: Yahweh tells Moses to set the Levites apart from the Israelites and cleanse them with water of purification, shaving and washing, and offerings; the Israelites lay hands on them and Aaron presents them to Yahweh as a wave offering. Levites serve from twenty-five and retire from active duty at fifty.

9.title: The Second Passover
9.context: In the first month of the second year Yahweh tells Israel to keep the Passover at twilight on the fourteenth; some men are unclean from contact with a dead body, and Yahweh allows a second Passover a month later, also open to foreigners who wish to keep it.

9.title: The Cloud above the Tabernacle
9.context: On the day the tabernacle is set up, the cloud covers it, appearing like fire at night; when it lifts, Israel sets out, and wherever it settles they camp — for a day, a month or a year — at Yahweh’s command.

10.title: The Two Silver Trumpets
10.context: Yahweh tells Moses to make two silver trumpets for summoning the community and moving the camps: both blown, the assembly gathers; one blown, only the leaders; an alarm sends the camps out. In war the trumpets bring Yahweh’s remembrance and rescue, and they are also sounded on feast days.

10.title: From Sinai to Paran
10.context: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifts from above the tabernacle and Israel sets out from the Sinai wilderness in the order Yahweh commanded through Moses, and the cloud settles in the Desert of Paran.

10.title: The People and the Ark Move On
10.context: Israel leaves Sinai with the ark going ahead to find them a resting place and the cloud above them by day; Moses prays to Yahweh each time the ark sets out and comes to rest.

11.title: The Complaints of the People
11.context: The people complain and Yahweh’s anger burns among them, with fire consuming the edges of the camp until Moses prays; the place is named Taberah. The rabble craves meat and the Israelites weep for it, and Moses, burdened, tells Yahweh he cannot carry the people alone.

11.title: Moses Appoints Seventy Elders
11.context: Yahweh shares the Spirit that is on Moses with seventy elders so they can help carry the people, and they prophesy; Moses wishes all Yahweh’s people were prophets.

11.title: The Quail and the Plague
11.context: A wind from Yahweh brings quail in from the sea, and the people gather them greedily; while the meat is still between their teeth, Yahweh’s anger flares and he strikes them with a plague. The place is named Kibroth Hattaavah, “graves of craving.”

12.title: The Complaint of Miriam and Aaron
12.context: Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses over his Cushite wife; Yahweh declares that he speaks with Moses face to face, Miriam is struck with leprosy, and after Moses prays she is kept outside the camp seven days.

13.title: The Spies Explore Canaan
13.context: Yahweh tells Moses to send a leader from each tribe to explore Canaan; after forty days they return with grapes, pomegranates and figs, saying the land flows with milk and honey but its people are strong, its cities fortified and the descendants of Anak live there.

14.title: Israel’s Rebellion
14.context: Ten spies’ report makes the community weep and grumble against Moses and Aaron, wanting to choose a leader and return to Egypt; Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes and plead that the land is good, that Yahweh is with them, and that they should not fear the people, but the community talks of stoning them.

14.title: Moses Intercedes for Israel
14.context: Yahweh asks how long they will refuse to trust him and threatens to destroy them; Moses intercedes, appealing to Yahweh’s reputation among the nations and to his declared character, “slow to anger, abounding in love,” and Yahweh pardons them as Moses asked.

14.title: Yahweh Punishes the Complaining People
14.context: Yahweh declares that this wicked community who grumbled will die in the wilderness; everyone twenty and over except Caleb and Joshua will not enter the land, and their children will wander forty years, a year for each day of the exploration. The ten spies who spread the bad report die of a plague.

14.title: The Defeat at Hormah
14.context: The people mourn at these words and in the morning try to go up toward the land anyway; Moses warns them that Yahweh is not with them. They go up without the ark or Moses, and the Amalekites and Canaanites defeat them and drive them back as far as Hormah.

15.title: Laws about Offerings
15.context: Once in the land, offerings are to be accompanied by grain and drink offerings, with the same rules for native-born and foreigner; firstfruits of dough are presented, unintentional sin has provision for a sin offering, but presumptuous sin with a raised fist is cut off from the people.

15.title: A Sabbath-Breaker Stoned
15.context: While Israel is in the wilderness a man is found gathering wood on the sabbath and brought before Moses, Aaron and the community; Yahweh tells Moses that he must be put to death, and the community stones him outside the camp.

15.title: The Law of Tassels
15.context: Yahweh tells Israel to make tassels on the corners of their garments with a blue cord, so that looking at them they remember all Yahweh’s commands and obey them rather than follow their own hearts and eyes, and be consecrated to their God.

16.title: Korah’s Rebellion
16.context: Korah the Levite, with Dathan, Abiram and 250 leaders, challenges Moses and Aaron; Yahweh makes the earth swallow the rebels and fire consume those offering incense.

16.title: The Censers Reserved for Holy Use
16.context: Yahweh tells Eleazar to gather the censers of those who were burned and hammer them into a covering for the altar, as a reminder that no one but Aaron’s descendants may come to burn incense before Yahweh.

16.title: Murmuring and Plague
16.context: The next day the whole community grumbles again, blaming Moses and Aaron for killing Yahweh’s people; Yahweh’s glory appears and a plague begins, and Aaron runs with incense to stand between the living and the dead until the plague stops, though 14,700 have died.

17.title: Aaron’s Staff Buds
17.context: Yahweh has Moses collect a staff from each tribe and lay them before the ark, promising the staff of the man he chooses will sprout; the next day Aaron’s staff for Levi has budded, blossomed and produced almonds. It is kept before the testimony as a sign to the rebels to end their grumbling.

18.title: Duties of Priests and Levites
18.context: Yahweh tells Aaron that he, his sons and the Levites bear responsibility for the sanctuary and the priesthood; the Levites assist but may not touch the sanctuary furnishings or the altar, and the priesthood is given as a gift, so any unauthorized person who approaches is put to death.

18.title: Offerings for Priests and Levites
18.context: Yahweh assigns the priests their portions: the most holy offerings, the wave and contribution offerings, the firstfruits of oil, wine and grain, and the firstborn — though human firstborn and unclean animals are redeemed.

18.title: The Levites' Portion
18.context: The Levites receive no inheritance among the Israelites; instead Yahweh gives them every tithe Israel brings, in return for their service at the tent of meeting, as a lasting ordinance.

18.title: The Levites' Tithe
18.context: Yahweh tells the Levites to present to Yahweh a tenth of the tithe they receive, the best of it, as a contribution for Aaron the priest, so that it is counted as if it were grain from the threshing floor or wine from the winepress.

19.title: The Red Heifer
19.context: Yahweh tells Moses and Aaron to have the Israelites bring a red heifer without defect that has never been yoked; it is slaughtered outside the camp, burned entirely, and its ashes kept in a clean place to be mixed into water for cleansing.

19.title: Purification of the Unclean
19.context: Anyone who touches a dead body is unclean seven days, purified on the third and seventh days with the water of cleansing; whoever does not purify himself defiles Yahweh’s tabernacle and is cut off from Israel. The same applies to those in a tent where someone dies or who touch a bone or grave.

20.title: Water from the Rock
20.context: Miriam dies at Kadesh; when the people quarrel over water, Yahweh tells Moses to speak to the rock, but he strikes it twice and so fails to honor Yahweh as holy, and he and Aaron are barred from leading Israel into the land; the place is called Meribah.

20.title: Edom Refuses Passage
20.context: From Kadesh Moses sends messengers to the king of Edom asking permission to pass through his land on the King’s Highway; Edom refuses and comes out with a large army, so Israel turns away.
