20.title: The Death of Aaron
20.context: The Israelites move on from Kadesh to Mount Hor, where Yahweh tells Moses to take Aaron and Eleazar up; Moses removes Aaron’s priestly garments and puts them on Eleazar, and Aaron dies on the mountain. The whole community mourns him thirty days.

21.title: The Defeat of Arad
21.context: The Canaanite king of Arad in the Negev hears that Israel is coming and attacks, taking some prisoners; Israel vows to Yahweh to destroy their cities if he delivers them, and Yahweh listens, and the place is called Hormah.

21.title: The Bronze Serpent
21.context: Discouraged by the long way, the people speak against God and Moses, and Yahweh sends venomous snakes that kill many. When the people confess, Moses prays, and Yahweh tells him to make a bronze snake and put it on a pole; anyone bitten who looks at it lives.

21.title: The Journey to Moab
21.context: The Israelites move on through Oboth, Iye Abarim, the Zered Valley and the Arnon, and at Beer Yahweh tells Moses to gather the people and he will give them water; they sing the song of the well and travel on toward the heights of Pisgah.

21.title: The Defeat of Sihon
21.context: Israel asks Sihon, king of the Amorites, for permission to pass through; he refuses and attacks, and the Israelites defeat him and take his land. They then defeat Og king of Bashan and settle in the Amorite territory east of the Jordan.

22.title: Balak Summons Balaam
22.context: Israel camps on the plains of Moab; Balak king of Moab, alarmed, sends messengers for Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel. God tells Balaam not to go and not to curse them, for they are blessed; later God allows him to go but only to say what he is told.

22.title: The Angel and Balaam’s Donkey
22.context: Balaam rides his donkey, and the angel of Yahweh stands in the road with a drawn sword; the donkey turns aside three times and Balaam beats it until Yahweh opens its mouth to speak. Yahweh opens Balaam’s eyes to see the angel, and he bows facedown; the angel tells him to speak only what he is told.

22.title: Balak Welcomes Balaam
22.context: When Balak hears that Balaam has come, he goes out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon; he sacrifices cattle and sheep, and the next day takes Balaam up to Bamoth Baal, from where he can see the nearest part of the Israelite camp.

22.title: Balaam's First Oracle
22.context: Balaam has Balak build seven altars and offer a bull and a ram on each; God meets him and gives him a message. Balaam declares that he cannot curse those whom God has not cursed, and that Israel is a people who dwell apart and are not reckoned among the nations.

23.title: Balaam’s Second Oracle
23.context: Balak takes Balaam to the top of Pisgah and again builds seven altars; Balaam again speaks Yahweh’s word, saying that God is not a man that he should lie, nor a son of man that he should change his mind, and that he has blessed Israel and Balaam cannot reverse it.

23.title: Balaam's Third Oracle
23.context: Balak takes Balaam to Peor and once more builds seven altars; the Spirit of God comes on Balaam, and he blesses Israel — “How beautiful are your tents, Jacob” — and says those who bless Israel will be blessed and those who curse them will be cursed.

24.title: Balaam’s Fourth Oracle
24.context: Balaam foretells what Israel will do to Balak’s people in days to come: a star will come out of Jacob and a scepter will rise out of Israel, crushing Moab and overcoming Edom, Amalek and the Kenites. After pronouncing judgments on other nations, Balaam and Balak each go home.

25.title: Moab Seduces Israel
25.context: At Shittim Israelite men are drawn into immorality with Moabite women and the worship of Baal of Peor, and a plague breaks out; Phinehas the priest kills an offending couple, the plague stops, and Yahweh makes a covenant of peace with him.

26.title: The Second Census of Israel
26.context: After the plague Yahweh tells Moses and Eleazar to count the men twenty and older fit for war: 601,730, none of whom had been counted at Sinai except Caleb and Joshua, and the land is to be divided by lot according to these numbers.

27.title: The Daughters of Zelophehad
27.context: The five daughters of Zelophehad, who has no sons, come to Moses and ask for an inheritance among their father’s relatives; Moses brings their case to Yahweh, who says they are right and gives a law that an inheritance without a son passes to the daughters.

27.title: Moses Requests a Successor
27.context: Yahweh tells Moses to view the promised land from the Abarim mountains; Moses asks for a successor so the people will not be like sheep without a shepherd, and Yahweh appoints Joshua, whom Moses commissions publicly.

28.title: The Daily Offerings
28.context: Yahweh tells Moses to instruct Israel to present at the appointed time the food offerings made by fire: two year-old male lambs without defect each day, one in the morning and one at twilight, with flour, oil and wine as a regular burnt offering.

28.title: The Sabbath Offerings
28.context: On the sabbath day two year-old male lambs without defect are offered, with flour, oil and a drink offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering.

28.title: The Monthly Offerings
28.context: At the beginning of each month, Israel presents two young bulls, a ram and seven lambs as a burnt offering with their grain and drink offerings, and a male goat as a sin offering.

28.title: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread
28.context: The fourteenth day of the first month is Yahweh’s Passover, the fifteenth begins a festival, and for seven days unleavened bread is eaten with a sacred assembly on the first and last days; the daily offerings for each day are prescribed.

28.title: The Feast of Weeks
28.context: On the day of firstfruits at the Feast of Weeks Israel holds a sacred assembly and does no regular work, offering two young bulls, a ram and seven lambs with a grain offering, and a goat to make atonement.

29.title: The Feast of Trumpets
29.context: On the first day of the seventh month there is a sacred assembly and a day of trumpet blasts, with the prescribed burnt offering of a bull, a ram and seven lambs, and a goat as a sin offering.

29.title: The Day of Atonement
29.context: On the tenth day of the seventh month there is a sacred assembly: Israel humbles itself and does no work, bringing the prescribed burnt offerings and a goat as a sin offering.

29.title: The Feast of Tabernacles
29.context: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month there is a sacred assembly, and for seven days the festival to Yahweh is kept, with the daily offerings prescribed — the number of bulls decreasing each day — and a solemn assembly on the eighth.

30.title: Laws about Vows
30.context: Moses tells the tribal leaders that when a man makes a vow or oath to Yahweh he must keep his word; the chapter sets out when a young woman’s or wife’s vow stands or is nullified depending on whether her father or husband objects the day he hears of it, while a widow’s or divorced woman’s vow always stands.

31.title: Vengeance on Midian
31.context: Yahweh tells Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites; a thousand men from each tribe — 12,000 — go out with Phinehas, kill every Midianite man including the five kings and Balaam son of Beor, take the women and children captive, and burn their towns.

31.title: Returning from Battle
31.context: When the army returns, Moses rebukes the officers for sparing the Midianite women who led Israel into sin at Peor and orders how the captives are to be treated; those who killed or touched the dead purify themselves outside the camp seven days.

31.title: Division of the Spoils
31.context: Yahweh tells Moses and Eleazar to divide the plunder in half between the soldiers and the community, with one in five hundred of the soldiers’ share given to Yahweh for the priests and one in fifty of the community’s share to the Levites; the officers also bring gold as an offering to make atonement.

32.title: The Tribes East of the Jordan
32.context: Reuben and Gad ask to settle east of the Jordan; Moses at first is angry, then agrees on condition that their fighting men cross over and fight until all Israel has its land; half of Manasseh also receives land there.

33.title: Forty-Two Journeys of the Israelites
33.context: At Yahweh’s command Moses records the stages of Israel’s journey from Rameses by divisions through forty-two stopping places — Succoth, the sea, Sinai and more — to the plains of Moab by the Jordan; Aaron dies on Mount Hor at 123.

33.title: Instructions for Occupying Canaan
33.context: In the plains of Moab Yahweh tells Moses that when Israel crosses the Jordan they are to drive out the inhabitants, destroy their carved images and high places, and take possession of the land by lot; if they leave any, those will become thorns in their sides.

34.title: The Boundaries of Canaan
34.context: Yahweh gives Moses the boundaries of Canaan: the southern border from the Dead Sea past Kadesh Barnea, the Mediterranean as the west, the northern line to Mount Hor and Lebo Hamath, and the eastern border down to the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan.

34.title: Leaders to Divide the Land
34.context: Yahweh names the men to assign the land: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and one leader from each tribe, the ten tribal leaders being listed by name, with Caleb among them.

35.title: Forty-Eight Cities for the Levites
35.context: On the plains of Moab Yahweh tells Moses that Israel is to give the Levites towns to live in from their inheritance, forty-eight towns with their pasturelands, six of them cities of refuge.

35.title: Six Cities of Refuge
35.context: Cities of refuge are set up so that someone who kills another accidentally can flee there and not be killed by the avenger before standing trial; a murderer is put to death on the testimony of more than one witness, and no ransom may be taken for a murderer’s life.

36.title: Zelophehad’s Daughters Marry
36.context: Leaders from Gilead’s clans appeal to Moses that if Zelophehad’s daughters marry outside their tribe, their inheritance will pass to another tribe; at Yahweh’s command they may marry whom they please, but only within their own tribal clan so no inheritance moves between tribes, and they do so.

1.title: The Command to Leave Horeb
1.context: In the fortieth year, on the east side of the Jordan, Moses begins to speak to Israel all that Yahweh commanded him; he recalls how Yahweh told them at Horeb to leave and go up to the hill country and take the land he swore to give their fathers.

1.title: Moses Appoints Leaders
1.context: Moses recalls that he could not bear the burden of the people alone, so wise, understanding and respected men were chosen from each tribe as leaders and judges, charged to judge fairly and show no partiality, “for judgment belongs to God.”

1.title: Twelve Spies Sent Out
1.context: Moses recalls the journey from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea and the twelve spies sent into the land; they reported it was good, yet the people refused to go up, rebelled against Yahweh’s command, and grumbled in their tents that he hated them.

1.title: Israel’s Penalty
1.context: Yahweh hears their words and swears that none of that evil generation will see the good land except Caleb and Joshua; Moses too is told he will not enter on their account. When the people try to go up anyway, the Amorites defeat them and Yahweh does not listen to their weeping.

2.title: Wanderings in the Wilderness
2.context: Israel circles the hill country of Seir for many days; Yahweh tells them not to provoke the descendants of Esau, Moab or Ammon, since he has given those lands to them, and by the time they cross the Zered Valley thirty-eight years have passed and the whole generation of fighting men has died.

2.title: The Defeat of Sihon
2.context: From the desert of Kedemoth Moses sends peaceful terms to Sihon king of Heshbon, but Yahweh makes his heart stubborn; Israel defeats Sihon at Jahaz and takes all his towns, though not the land of the Ammonites.

3.title: The Defeat of Og
3.context: Og king of Bashan marches out with his whole army to meet Israel at Edrei; Yahweh tells Moses not to fear him and delivers Og and his people into Israel’s hand, and Israel captures sixty cities, the whole region of Argob in Bashan.

3.title: Land Division East of the Jordan
3.context: Moses assigns the land east of the Jordan to the Reubenites, Gadites and half of Manasseh, and charges their fighting men to cross over armed ahead of their brothers until Yahweh gives them rest, and then return.

3.title: Moses Forbidden to Cross the Jordan
3.context: Moses pleads with Yahweh to let him cross and see the good land beyond the Jordan; Yahweh is angry with him on account of the people and refuses, telling him instead to go up to Pisgah to look and to commission and encourage Joshua.

4.title: An Exhortation to Obedience
4.context: Moses urges Israel to listen to the decrees and laws Yahweh teaches them, adding nothing and taking nothing away; this is their wisdom before the nations, who will ask what other nation has a god so near, or laws so righteous.

4.title: A Warning against Idolatry
4.context: At Horeb Yahweh spoke to them from the fire but they saw no form, so they are to make no idol in any shape; Yahweh is a consuming fire, a jealous God, and if they become corrupt and make idols they will be scattered among the nations — yet if they seek him with all their heart he will not forget his covenant.

4.title: Cities of Refuge
4.context: Moses sets aside three cities east of the Jordan for someone who kills a person unintentionally: Bezer for Reuben, Ramoth for Gad and Golan for Manasseh.

4.title: Introduction to the Law
4.context: This is the law Moses set before the Israelites, with its testimonies, decrees and laws, as they came out of Egypt, spoken in the valley near Beth Peor in the land once held by Sihon, whom Moses and Israel defeated.

5.title: The Covenant at Horeb
5.context: Moses summons all Israel to hear the decrees and laws, saying Yahweh made the covenant at Horeb not just with their fathers but with all of them alive today. He repeats the Ten Commandments, tying the day of rest to the memory of slavery in Egypt.

5.title: Moses Intercedes for the People
5.context: Frightened by the fire and the voice from the darkness, the people ask Moses to listen to Yahweh and tell them what he says; Yahweh approves and wishes they would always fear him and keep his commands, and tells Moses to stand by him to receive the whole law.

6.title: The Greatest Commandment
6.context: The Shema: Israel is to hear that Yahweh their God is one, love him with all their heart, soul and strength, and teach these words to their children in every part of daily life.

6.title: A Warning Not to Rebel against God
6.context: When Yahweh brings Israel into the land with houses, cisterns and vineyards they did not build, they are to take care not to forget him; they must fear Yahweh, serve him only, swear by his name, and not test him as they did at Massah.

7.title: Drive Out the Nations
7.context: When Yahweh brings Israel into the land and drives out seven stronger nations, they are not to make treaties with them or intermarry, but to destroy their altars, for Israel is a holy people chosen by Yahweh from all peoples.

7.title: The Promises of God
7.context: Yahweh chose Israel not because they were numerous but because he loved them and kept his oath; he is the faithful God who keeps his covenant of love to a thousand generations of those who love him. If they obey, he will bless them above all peoples and drive out the nations little by little.

8.title: Remember Yahweh Your God
8.context: Moses tells Israel to remember how Yahweh led them forty years in the wilderness to humble and test them; he fed them with manna so they would learn that man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of Yahweh.

8.title: A Warning Not to Forget Yahweh
8.context: Moses warns that when Israel has eaten and is satisfied, built fine houses and prospered, they must not become proud and forget Yahweh or say their own power made them wealthy; it is Yahweh who gives power to gain wealth, and forgetting him will mean destruction.

9.title: Assurance of Victory
9.context: Yahweh will go ahead of Israel like a consuming fire against stronger nations, but not because of Israel’s righteousness — because of those nations’ wickedness; Moses reminds them how stubborn they have been, as at the golden calf at Horeb.

10.title: New Stone Tablets
10.context: Yahweh tells Moses to cut two stone tablets and make a wooden ark; he writes the Ten Commandments on the tablets, which Moses puts in the ark. The tribe of Levi is set apart to carry the ark and serve Yahweh, and Yahweh remains Levi’s inheritance.

10.title: A Call to Obedience
10.context: What does Yahweh require of Israel? To fear him, walk in his ways, love him, serve him with all the heart and soul, and keep his commands; circumcise your hearts and stop being stiff-necked, for Yahweh your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, who defends the fatherless and widow and loves the foreigner.

11.title: Obedience and Discipline
11.context: Love Yahweh your God and keep his requirements always; Moses reminds them that it is they, not their children, who saw his discipline and his great works in Egypt, in the wilderness and in the judgment on Dathan and Abiram.

11.title: God’s Great Blessings
11.context: The promised land, unlike Egypt, depends on rain from heaven under Yahweh’s constant care; obedience brings rain in season, but turning to other gods will shut the heavens; Moses sets blessing and curse before them.

12.title: One Place for Worship
12.context: In the land they are to demolish every pagan worship site and seek the place Yahweh chooses for his Name; there they bring their burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes and freewill offerings and rejoice before him, never eating blood but pouring it out like water.

12.title: A Warning against Idolatry
12.context: Moses warns Israel that after Yahweh drives out the nations they must not ask how those nations served their gods, for they even burn their sons and daughters in the fire; Israel is to observe everything Yahweh commands, adding nothing and taking nothing away.

14.title: Children of Yahweh
14.context: Israel are children of Yahweh their God; they must not gash themselves or shave their foreheads for the dead, for they are a people holy to Yahweh, his treasured possession from among all peoples.

14.title: Clean and Unclean Animals
14.context: The animals Israel may eat include ox, sheep, goat and deer — those with a split hoof that chew the cud — and fish with fins and scales and clean birds; the unclean animals, swarming insects and anything found dead are not to be eaten, nor a young goat boiled in its mother’s milk.

14.title: Giving Tithes
14.context: Each year Israel sets aside a tenth of its produce and eats it before Yahweh in the place he chooses, or sells it and buys what they desire there; every third year the tithe is stored in the towns for the Levites, foreigners, orphans and widows, so Yahweh may bless all their work.

15.title: The Seventh Year
15.context: At the end of every seven years debts are to be canceled and not collected from a fellow Israelite; if Israel fully obeys there should be no poor among them. They are not to be hard-hearted or tightfisted toward the needy but openhanded, lending freely without a grudging heart.

15.title: Hebrew Servants
15.context: A fellow Hebrew sold into service is to go free in the seventh year and be sent off with generous gifts, for Israel was once enslaved in Egypt; one who chooses to stay may serve for life.

15.title: Firstborn Animals
15.context: Every firstborn male of the herd and flock is consecrated to Yahweh, not worked or shorn, but eaten each year with one’s household at the place Yahweh chooses; one with a defect is not offered but eaten at home, though its blood is poured out and never eaten.

16.title: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread
16.context: In the month of Aviv Israel keeps the Passover to Yahweh, sacrificing at the place he chooses, and for seven days eats unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, so as to remember all their lives the day they left Egypt.

16.title: The Feast of Weeks
16.context: Seven weeks from when the sickle is first put to the standing grain, Israel keeps the Feast of Weeks to Yahweh with a freewill offering in proportion to his blessing, rejoicing at the chosen place with their households, the Levites, foreigners, orphans and widows.

16.title: The Feast of Tabernacles
16.context: After gathering the produce of threshing floor and winepress Israel keeps the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days, rejoicing before Yahweh; three times a year all males appear before him at the place he chooses, each giving as he has been blessed.

16.title: Judges and Justice
16.context: Israel is to appoint judges and officials in every town, who must judge fairly without partiality or taking bribes, for bribes blind the wise; justice and only justice they are to pursue, and they must set up no wooden pole or sacred stone beside Yahweh’s altar.

17.title: Guidelines for a King
17.context: If Israel wants a king, he must be a fellow Israelite chosen by Yahweh; he must not multiply horses, wives or wealth, but copy out the law and read it all his life, learning to fear Yahweh and not exalt himself.

18.title: Provision for Priests and Levites
18.context: Levites have no inheritance among the tribes because Yahweh himself is their inheritance, and they live on the offerings made to him; priests receive the shoulder, jowls and stomach of sacrifices and the firstfruits of grain, wine, oil and wool, and a Levite from any town may come to serve at the chosen place.

18.title: Sorcery Forbidden
18.context: When Israel enters the land they must not imitate the detestable practices of the nations — sacrificing children in fire, divination, sorcery, interpreting omens, casting spells, consulting mediums or the dead — for these are why Yahweh is driving those nations out; Israel is to be blameless before Yahweh.

18.title: A Prophet Like Moses
18.context: Yahweh promises to raise up from among Israel a prophet like Moses and put his words in his mouth, and the people must listen to him; the New Testament applies this to Jesus (Acts 3:22–23); prophets who speak falsely in Yahweh’s name will be judged.

19.title: Cities of Refuge
19.context: When Yahweh gives Israel the land, they are to set aside three cities of refuge and build roads to them, so that a person who kills another unintentionally can flee there; a murderer who flees to a refuge city is handed over to the avenger of blood, and three more cities are added if Yahweh enlarges the territory.

19.title: The Old Boundary
19.context: Israel is not to move a neighbor’s boundary stone, set up by those who went before.

19.title: The Testimony of Two or Three Witnesses
19.context: Any accusation must be established by two or three witnesses; if a malicious witness accuses someone falsely, both parties stand before Yahweh and the judges investigate, and the false witness suffers what he planned for his brother, so that others will hear and be afraid.

20.title: Laws of Warfare
20.context: Rules for war: do not fear a larger army, for Yahweh is with them; men with a new house, vineyard or fiancée, or who are afraid, may go home; distant cities are first offered peace, and fruit trees are not cut down during a siege.

21.title: Atonement for an Unsolved Murder
21.context: If a body is found in the open country and the killer is unknown, the elders of the nearest town take a heifer to an unplowed valley with a flowing stream and break its neck, wash their hands and declare their innocence, praying Yahweh to forgive his people so innocent blood is not left on them.

21.title: Marrying a Captive Woman
21.context: A captive woman taken as a wife must first be allowed a month to mourn her parents; if later the husband no longer wants her, he must let her go free and may not sell or mistreat her.

21.title: Inheritance Rights of the Firstborn
21.context: If a man has two wives, one loved and one unloved, and the firstborn is the unloved wife’s son, he may not give the loved wife’s son the firstborn’s rights, but must acknowledge the firstborn and give him a double share of the estate.

21.title: A Rebellious Son
21.context: If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his parents even when disciplined, his parents bring him to the town elders at the gate to say he is a glutton and drunkard, and the men of the town stone him, so that Israel will hear and be afraid and the evil be purged from among them.

21.title: Cursed Is Anyone Hung on a Tree
21.context: If someone guilty of a capital offense is put to death and his body is hung on a tree, it must not remain there overnight but be buried that day, because anyone hung on a tree is under God’s curse; so Israel must not desecrate the land Yahweh is giving them.

22.title: Marriage Violations
22.context: Laws on marriage cases: a man who falsely accuses his bride of unchastity is punished and may never divorce her; adultery is a capital offense; the law distinguishes rape in the countryside from consent in town, and forbids marrying a father’s wife.

23.title: Exclusion from the Congregation
23.context: Those with crushed or severed private parts, those born of forbidden unions, and Ammonites and Moabites to the tenth generation may not enter the assembly of Yahweh; Edomites and Egyptians may enter in the third generation.

23.title: Uncleanness in the Camp
23.context: When the army goes out against its enemies it must keep away from everything impure; a man unclean from a nocturnal emission stays outside the camp until evening, bathes and returns at sunset, and a designated place with a trowel is provided outside for human waste, because Yahweh walks in the camp.

23.title: Miscellaneous Laws
23.context: A slave who escapes to Israel is not to be returned and not oppressed; there are laws against shrine prostitution, against charging a fellow Israelite interest, and for keeping vows promptly; a neighbor’s vineyard or grain may be eaten from while passing through, but not carried away.

24.title: Marriage and Divorce Laws
24.context: On divorce: a man may not remarry a former wife after she has married another; a newly married man is exempt from war and public duty for a year so he can bring joy to his wife.

24.title: Additional Laws
24.context: Laws protecting the vulnerable: no millstone may be taken as a pledge, kidnapping is a capital crime, a poor man’s cloak is returned by sunset, wages are paid the same day, each person dies for their own sin, and gleanings are left for foreigners, orphans and widows.

25.title: Widowhood and Marriage
25.context: When brothers live together and one dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up a son for the dead man’s name; if he refuses, she may pull off his sandal and spit in his face before the elders, and he is known in Israel as the man whose sandal was pulled off.

25.title: Standard Weights and Measures
25.context: Israel must not carry two sets of weights or measures, one heavy and one light, but use accurate and honest ones so that their days may be long in the land; Yahweh detests anyone who deals dishonestly.

25.title: Revenge on the Amalekites
25.context: Israel is to remember what the Amalekites did on the way out of Egypt: attacking the stragglers when they were weary, with no fear of God; when Yahweh gives rest from all their enemies in the land, they are to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.

26.title: Offering Firstfruits and Tithes
26.context: In the land, Israel is to bring the firstfruits to the chosen place and recite their story — their ancestor was a wandering Aramean, and Yahweh brought them out of Egypt into this good land; the third-year tithe goes to the Levites and the poor.

26.title: Obey Yahweh’s Commands
26.context: Moses says that today Yahweh commands Israel to follow these decrees; they have declared that Yahweh is their God and will walk in his ways, and Yahweh has declared that they are his treasured possession, to be set high above all nations in praise, fame and honor, a people holy to him.

27.title: The Altar on Mount Ebal
27.context: Moses and the elders command that when Israel crosses the Jordan they set up large stones on Mount Ebal, coat them with plaster and write all the words of the law on them, and build an altar of uncut stones to Yahweh, offering burnt and fellowship offerings and rejoicing before him.

27.title: Curses Pronounced from Ebal
27.context: Moses commands that after crossing the Jordan six tribes stand on Mount Gerizim to bless and six on Mount Ebal to pronounce the curses; the Levites call out twelve curses on idolatry, dishonoring parents, moving boundaries, injustice, immorality, murder and bribery, and all the people answer “Amen.”

28.title: The Blessings of Obedience
28.context: If Israel fully obeys Yahweh and carefully follows all his commands, he will set them high above all the nations; blessing will come on their town and field, children and crops, flocks and storehouses, coming and going, and enemies who attack from one direction will flee in seven.

28.title: The Curses of Disobedience
28.context: But if Israel does not obey Yahweh or follow his commands, all these curses will fall on them: disease, drought, defeat, siege, famine, exile, madness and the loss of everything they have, because they did not serve Yahweh joyfully and gladly in the time of abundance.

29.title: The Covenant in Moab
29.context: Besides the covenant at Horeb, Moses renews the covenant in Moab; he recalls Yahweh’s deeds in Egypt and the wilderness and warns that anyone who turns his heart to other gods brings ruin on the land.

30.title: The Promise of Restoration
30.context: Moses foretells that when Israel, scattered among the nations, returns to Yahweh, he will gather them and circumcise their hearts so they love him; he sets life and death before them and urges them to choose life.

31.title: Joshua to Succeed Moses
31.context: Moses says that at 120 he can no longer lead them and that Yahweh has said he will not cross the Jordan; Yahweh himself will go before them, and Joshua will lead, so they are to be strong and courageous, since Yahweh goes with them and will never leave nor forsake them. He charges Joshua before all Israel.

31.title: The Reading of the Law
31.context: Moses writes down the law and gives it to the Levitical priests who carry the ark and to the elders, commanding that every seventh year at the Feast of Tabernacles it be read aloud to the whole assembly, so that men, women, children and foreigners may hear it, learn to fear Yahweh, and follow it faithfully.

31.title: God Commissions Joshua
31.context: Yahweh tells Moses to bring Joshua to the tent of meeting, where he appears in the pillar of cloud, commissions Joshua, and warns that after Moses dies the people will prostitute themselves to foreign gods and break the covenant; he instructs Moses to write down a song as a witness against them.

31.title: Moses Begins His Song
31.context: Moses recites the words of this song from beginning to end in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel.

32.title: Moses’ Death Foretold
32.context: Moses urges the people to keep every word of the law, for it is their life; that day Yahweh sends him up Mount Nebo to view Canaan and die there, because at Meribah he did not honor Yahweh as holy.

33.title: Moses Blesses the Twelve Tribes
33.context: Before his death Moses blesses the tribes one by one, beginning with Yahweh coming from Sinai and ending by calling Israel blessed, a people saved by Yahweh.

34.title: The Death of Moses
34.context: Moses climbs Mount Nebo and Yahweh shows him the whole promised land; he dies in Moab and Yahweh buries him in an unknown grave; Joshua succeeds him, and no later prophet knew Yahweh face to face as Moses did.

1.title: God Instructs Joshua
1.context: After Moses’ death Yahweh tells Joshua to cross the Jordan into the land he promised, assuring him he will be with him as he was with Moses, and charging him to be strong and courageous and to meditate on the Book of the Law day and night so that he will prosper.

1.title: Joshua Takes Charge
1.context: Joshua tells the officers to have the people prepare supplies to cross the Jordan in three days, and reminds the eastern tribes of their promise to Moses to fight alongside their brothers; they answer that they will do whatever he commands, and will obey as they obeyed Moses.

2.title: Rahab Welcomes the Spies
2.context: Joshua secretly sends two spies from Shittim to Jericho, where they stay with a prostitute named Rahab; she hides them under stalks of flax, misleads the king’s men, and confesses that Yahweh has given them the land. She asks that her family be spared, and they agree if she ties a scarlet cord in her window.

3.title: Crossing the Jordan
3.context: Early in the morning Joshua leads Israel to the Jordan; when the priests carrying the ark step into the water, the river stops flowing and piles up in a heap far upstream, and all the people cross on dry ground while the priests stand firm in the middle of the riverbed.

4.title: Twelve Stones from the Jordan
4.context: Twelve men, one per tribe, carry stones from the riverbed and set them up at Gilgal, so that when children ask, Israel will tell how the Jordan stopped before the ark.

5.title: The Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
5.context: Yahweh tells Joshua to make flint knives and circumcise the Israelite men born in the wilderness, saying he has rolled away the reproach of Egypt; they keep the Passover at Gilgal on the fourteenth day, eat the produce of the land the next day, and the manna stops.

5.title: The Commander of Yahweh’s Army
5.context: Near Jericho Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword who says he has come as commander of Yahweh’s army; Joshua falls facedown and is told to remove his sandals, for the ground is holy.

6.title: The Walls of Jericho
6.context: At Yahweh’s command Israel marches around Jericho once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh; at the trumpet blast and shout the walls collapse, the city is destroyed, and only Rahab’s family is spared.

7.title: The Defeat at Ai
7.context: Achan secretly keeps plunder from Jericho that was devoted to Yahweh, and Israel is defeated at Ai; lots expose him, he confesses and is put to death, and Yahweh’s anger turns away.

8.title: The Conquest of Ai
8.context: Yahweh tells Joshua not to be afraid and to take the whole army against Ai, promising to deliver it, and allowing plunder this time; Joshua sets an ambush and draws the men of Ai out, and the ambush takes and burns the city. Its king is hung on a tree until evening, then buried at the city gate under a heap of stones.

8.title: Joshua Renews the Covenant
8.context: Joshua builds an altar to Yahweh on Mount Ebal and offers burnt and fellowship offerings; there he copies the law of Moses on stones. All Israel, half facing Mount Gerizim and half Mount Ebal, with the ark in the middle, hears Joshua read the blessings and curses as Moses had commanded, with the foreigners among them.

9.title: The Deceit of the Gibeonites
9.context: The kings west of the Jordan unite to fight Israel, but the people of Gibeon pretend to be from a distant land, with worn-out sacks and moldy bread, and trick Joshua into a treaty without asking Yahweh. When the deceit is discovered, Israel keeps its oath but makes them woodcutters and water carriers.

10.title: The Day the Sun Stood Still
10.context: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon, and Joshua marches all night to its aid; Yahweh throws hailstones on the enemy, and at Joshua’s prayer the sun stands still until Israel has won.

10.title: The Victory at Makkedah
10.context: The five kings hide in a cave at Makkedah, and Joshua has it sealed with boulders until the pursuit is finished; then he brings the kings out, has his commanders place their feet on their necks, and puts them to death, hanging them on trees until evening.

10.title: Conquest of the Southern Cities
10.context: Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron and Debir in turn, devoting each city and its king to destruction, and conquers the entire southern region from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza, because Yahweh, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

11.title: Conquest of the Northern Cities
11.context: Jabin king of Hazor gathers the northern kings with a huge force of horses and chariots; Yahweh tells Joshua not to fear, Israel strikes suddenly at the waters of Merom, and Hazor is burned.

11.title: Joshua Takes the Whole Land
11.context: Joshua takes the whole land — the hills, the Negev, Goshen, the Arabah and the mountains of Israel — after fighting many kings over a long time, and apart from Gibeon no city made peace with Israel, for Yahweh hardened their hearts. The Anakites are cut off from the hill country, and the land has rest from war.

12.title: The Kings Defeated East of the Jordan
12.context: The kings Israel defeated east of the Jordan, Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, whose land Moses gave as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh.

12.title: The Kings Defeated West of the Jordan
12.context: The thirty-one kings Joshua and Israel defeated west of the Jordan are listed, from Baal Gad in Lebanon to Mount Halak, including those of Jericho, Ai, Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Bethel, and Joshua gives their land to the tribes as an inheritance.

13.title: Lands Yet Unconquered
13.context: Joshua is old and Yahweh tells him much land remains to be taken: the Philistine and Geshurite regions, the Canaanite coast and Lebanon; Yahweh himself will drive them out, and Joshua is to allot the land to the nine and a half tribes.

13.title: The Inheritance East of the Jordan
13.context: Moses had already assigned the land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, from Aroer on the Arnon over the plateau of Medeba and the kingdom of Og in Bashan; but to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance, since the offerings made to Yahweh are their inheritance.

13.title: Reuben’s Inheritance
13.context: Moses’ allotment to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan: the territory from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge across the plateau to Heshbon, with its towns and villages.

13.title: Gad’s Inheritance
13.context: Moses’ allotment to the tribe of Gad: Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, half of the Ammonite country as far as Aroer near Rabbah, and the Jordan valley up to the Sea of Galilee.

13.title: Manasseh’s Eastern Inheritance
13.context: Moses gives half the tribe of Manasseh their inheritance: the land from Mahanaim through all Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og including Havvoth Jair’s sixty towns, given to half the descendants of Makir son of Manasseh.

14.title: Land Division West of the Jordan
14.context: These are the inheritances the Israelites receive in Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the tribal heads distribute by lot, as Yahweh had commanded through Moses, to the nine and a half tribes; the Levites receive no share but only towns and pastures.

14.title: Caleb Requests Hebron
14.context: The men of Judah come to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb, now eighty-five and as strong as ever, reminds him of Moses’ promise and asks for the hill country of Hebron, where the Anakites live; Joshua blesses him and gives him Hebron as an inheritance because he followed Yahweh wholeheartedly.

15.title: Judah’s Inheritance
15.context: The lot for the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, extends south to the border of Edom and the Desert of Zin, with its boundary running from the Dead Sea through Kadesh Barnea to the Wadi of Egypt and the Mediterranean.

15.title: Caleb’s Portion and Conquest
15.context: Caleb takes Hebron and drives out the Anakites; he promises his daughter Aksah to whoever captures Debir, Othniel takes it and marries her, and she asks her father for springs of water.

15.title: The Cities of Judah
15.context: The towns of the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, are listed by region — the Negev, the western foothills, the hill country and the desert — but the people of Judah are unable to dislodge the Jebusites in Jerusalem, who live there with them to this day.

16.title: Ephraim’s Inheritance
16.context: The lot for Joseph’s descendants extends from the Jordan near Jericho, up through the hill country to Bethel and westward to the sea; Ephraim and Manasseh each receive their inheritance.

16.title: The Tribe of Ephraim
16.context: The territory of Ephraim, clan by clan, runs from Ataroth Addar in the east to Upper Beth Horon and on to the sea, including towns set apart within Manasseh’s land; but they do not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, who are put to forced labor.

17.title: Manasseh’s Western Inheritance
17.context: Manasseh receives land on both sides of the Jordan, and Zelophehad’s daughters receive their inheritance as Moses had commanded.

17.title: The Descendants of Joseph Ask for More Land
17.context: The descendants of Joseph complain to Joshua that one allotment is too small for so numerous a people; Joshua answers that if they are so many they should clear the forested hill country for themselves, and that they are powerful enough to drive out the Canaanites even though they have iron chariots.

18.title: The Remainder Divided
18.context: The assembly sets up the tent of meeting at Shiloh; for the seven tribes still without land, Joshua sends men to survey and divide the territory into seven parts, which he allots by lot before Yahweh.

18.title: Benjamin’s Inheritance
18.context: The lot for Benjamin, clan by clan, falls between Judah and Joseph, with its boundaries described on the north, west, south and east; its towns include Jericho, Bethel, Gibeon, Mizpah and Jebus, that is Jerusalem.

19.title: Simeon’s Inheritance
19.context: The second lot comes out for Simeon, clan by clan, whose inheritance lies within the territory of Judah because Judah’s share was more than they needed, and includes Beersheba, Moladah and other towns.

19.title: Zebulun’s Inheritance
19.context: The third lot falls to Zebulun, clan by clan, with its boundary running from Sarid through Daberath to Japhia, Gath Hepher and Rimmon, including twelve towns.

19.title: Issachar’s Inheritance
19.context: The fourth lot comes out for Issachar, clan by clan, with towns including Jezreel, Kesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion and En Gannim, and boundaries reaching to the Jordan.

19.title: Asher’s Inheritance
19.context: The fifth lot falls to Asher, clan by clan, with towns including Helkath, Hali, Beten and Akshaph, reaching to Mount Carmel and the sea in the west and toward Sidon and Tyre in the north.

19.title: Naphtali’s Inheritance
19.context: The sixth lot comes out for Naphtali, clan by clan, extending from Heleph toward Mount Tabor and the Jordan, with fortified towns including Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath and Kinnereth, nineteen towns in all.

19.title: Dan’s Inheritance
19.context: The seventh lot falls to Dan, clan by clan, with towns including Zorah, Eshtaol and Ir Shemesh; when the Danites find their territory too small, they attack Leshem, take it, settle there and rename it Dan after their ancestor.

19.title: Joshua’s Inheritance
19.context: When the allotments are completed, the Israelites give Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them, as Yahweh commanded: the town he asked for, Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, which he rebuilds and settles in.

20.title: Six Cities of Refuge
20.context: Yahweh tells Joshua to have Israel designate the cities of refuge Moses spoke of, where someone who kills another unintentionally may flee from the avenger of blood; they set apart Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem in Ephraim and Hebron in Judah on the west, and Bezer, Ramoth and Golan on the east.

21.title: Forty-Eight Cities for the Levites
21.context: As Moses had commanded, the Levites receive forty-eight towns with pasturelands from the other tribes, including the cities of refuge.

21.title: Israel Takes the Land as an Inheritance
21.context: So Yahweh gives Israel all the land he swore to give their ancestors, and they take possession and settle there; he gives them rest on every side as he had promised, and none of their enemies can stand against them. Not one of all the good promises Yahweh made to the house of Israel fails; every one is fulfilled.

22.title: The Eastern Tribes Return Home
22.context: Joshua commends the eastern tribes for fighting alongside their brothers and sends them home, urging them to love Yahweh and walk in his ways.

22.title: The Altar of Witness
22.context: The eastern tribes build a large altar by the Jordan, and the others prepare for war, thinking it rebellion; when Phinehas inquires, they explain it is a witness that they too belong to Yahweh, and peace is restored.

23.title: Joshua’s Charge to Leaders
23.context: In old age Joshua gathers Israel’s leaders, reminds them that Yahweh fought for them, and urges them to keep the law, hold fast to Yahweh, and not intermarry with the remaining nations or serve their gods.

24.title: Joshua Reviews Israel’s History
24.context: At Shechem Joshua reviews Israel’s history from Abraham to the conquest and calls the people to choose whom they will serve, declaring that he and his household will serve Yahweh; the people make a covenant, and he sets up a stone as witness.

24.title: Joshua’s Death and Burial
24.context: Joshua son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, dies at 110 and is buried at Timnath Serah; Israel serves Yahweh throughout Joshua’s lifetime and that of the elders who outlive him. Joseph’s bones, brought up from Egypt, are buried at Shechem, and Eleazar son of Aaron dies and is buried in the hill country of Ephraim.

1.title: The Conquest of Canaan Proceeds
1.context: After Joshua’s death the Israelites ask Yahweh who should go up first against the Canaanites; he answers that Judah is to go, and Judah and Simeon fight together, with Yahweh giving the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands.

1.title: The Capture of Jerusalem and Hebron
1.context: Judah attacks Jerusalem, puts it to the sword and sets it on fire, then fights the Canaanites of the hill country, the Negev and the western foothills, and takes Hebron, defeating the clans of Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.

1.title: Othniel Captures Debir
1.context: Judah goes on to Debir, where Caleb promises his daughter Aksah to whoever takes the town; Othniel son of Kenaz takes it and marries her, and at her request Caleb also gives her springs of water.

1.title: The Victories of Judah
1.context: Judah and Simeon take several towns, and Yahweh is with Judah, but they cannot drive out the plains people with iron chariots, and Benjamin fails to dislodge the Jebusites from Jerusalem.

1.title: Ephraim and Manasseh Capture Bethel
1.context: The house of Joseph attacks Bethel, and Yahweh is with them; their spies learn from a man leaving the city how to enter, and they put the city to the sword but spare the man and his family, who go to the land of the Hittites and build another city also called Luz.

1.title: The Failure to Complete the Conquest
1.context: Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali and Dan do not drive out the Canaanites in their territories; they live among them and put them to forced labor, and the Amorites push the Danites into the hill country.

2.title: Israel Rebuked at Bochim
2.context: The angel of Yahweh at Bokim rebukes Israel for making treaties with the land’s people and not tearing down their altars, so Yahweh will no longer drive them out; the people weep aloud.

2.title: Joshua’s Death and Burial
2.context: Joshua dismisses the people to take possession of their land, and they serve Yahweh throughout his lifetime and that of the elders who had seen what he did; Joshua dies at 110 and is buried at Timnath Heres, and that whole generation is gathered to its ancestors.

2.title: Israel’s Unfaithfulness
2.context: A new generation grows up that does not know Yahweh or what he did for Israel; they forsake him to serve the Baals and Ashtoreths, and his anger burns against them. Yahweh raises up judges to save them, but whenever a judge dies they return to worse ways than their ancestors.

3.title: Nations Left to Test Israel
3.context: Yahweh leaves several nations in the land to test the Israelites, to see if they will obey the commands he gave their ancestors through Moses, and to teach war to a generation that has not known it; yet Israel intermarries with them and serves their gods.

3.title: Othniel
3.context: Israel does evil by serving the Baals, and Yahweh sells them into the hands of Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram Naharaim for eight years; when they cry out, he raises up Othniel son of Kenaz, on whom the Spirit of Yahweh comes, who defeats Cushan and gives the land peace for forty years.

3.title: Ehud
3.context: Israel again does evil, and Yahweh gives Eglon king of Moab power over them for eighteen years. Yahweh raises up Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, who delivers tribute to Eglon and kills him with a hidden double-edged sword; then he rallies Israel, who defeat Moab and enjoy peace for eighty years.

3.title: Shamgar
3.context: Shamgar son of Anath strikes down six hundred Philistines with an ox goad, and he too saves Israel.

4.title: Deborah and Barak
4.context: Sisera, commander of King Jabin of Canaan with nine hundred iron chariots, oppresses Israel twenty years; the prophetess Deborah summons Barak to battle, Sisera flees and is killed by Jael in her tent.

5.title: The Song of Deborah and Barak
5.context: The victory song of Deborah and Barak praises Yahweh for the battle, honors the tribes who volunteered and rebukes those who stayed home, celebrates Jael’s deed, and ends wishing that those who love Yahweh may rise like the sun.

6.title: Midian Oppresses Israel
6.context: Midianites and Amalekites ravage Israel like locusts for seven years; the angel of Yahweh appears to Gideon threshing wheat in a winepress and calls him to save Israel; Gideon tears down his father’s altar to Baal and later tests God with a fleece.

7.title: Gideon’s Army of Three Hundred
7.context: Yahweh reduces Gideon’s army from 32,000 to 300 so Israel cannot boast; at night the three hundred blow trumpets, smash jars and raise torches, and the Midianite camp turns on itself and flees.

8.title: Gideon Defeats Zebah and Zalmunna
8.context: The Ephraimites quarrel with Gideon for not calling them earlier, and he calms them with a humble answer; he pursues Zebah and Zalmunna, punishes the men of Succoth and Peniel who refused to help, and executes the two Midianite kings.

8.title: Forty Years of Peace
8.context: Israel asks Gideon to rule, but he says Yahweh will rule them; yet the ephod he makes from their gold earrings becomes an object of idolatry, and after his death Israel returns to the Baals.

9.title: Abimelech’s Conspiracy
9.context: Gideon’s son Abimelech kills seventy brothers and is made king at Shechem; Jotham warns with the fable of the trees; after three years conflict breaks out, and at Thebez a woman drops a millstone on Abimelech, who dies.

10.title: Tola
10.context: After Abimelech, Tola of Issachar rises to save Israel and judges for twenty-three years, then dies and is buried at Shamir.

10.title: Jair
10.context: After Tola, Jair of Gilead judges Israel twenty-two years; he has thirty sons who ride thirty donkeys and control thirty towns, and he dies and is buried at Kamon.

10.title: Oppression by the Philistines and Ammonites
10.context: Israel abandons Yahweh for the gods of the nations and is oppressed by the Philistines and Ammonites for eighteen years; when they confess and put away foreign gods, Yahweh can no longer bear their misery.

11.title: Jephthah's Daughter
11.context: When Jephthah returns, his only daughter is the first to meet him; he is devastated, but she asks him to keep his vow, requesting only two months to mourn with her friends that she will never marry; Israel’s young women commemorate her four days each year.

12.title: Jephthah Defeats Ephraim
12.context: The men of Ephraim complain that Jephthah did not call them to fight the Ammonites and threaten to burn his house; Jephthah’s Gileadites defeat them and seize the fords of the Jordan, killing any fugitive who says “Sibboleth” instead of “Shibboleth,” and 42,000 Ephraimites fall.

12.title: Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon
12.context: After Jephthah, Ibzan of Bethlehem judges Israel seven years, Elon of Zebulun ten years, and Abdon son of Hillel from Pirathon eight years, each succeeded by the next and then buried in his hometown.

13.title: The Birth of Samson
13.context: Under forty years of Philistine oppression, the angel of Yahweh appears to Manoah’s barren wife and promises a son set apart as a Nazirite to begin rescuing Israel; the boy is Samson, and the Spirit of Yahweh begins to stir him.

14.title: Samson’s Marriage
14.context: Samson wants to marry a Philistine woman of Timnah and tears apart a lion on the way; at the wedding feast the guests force his bride to learn his riddle’s answer, and in anger he kills thirty men of Ashkelon, and his bride is given to another.

15.title: Samson Defeats the Philistines
15.context: Samson burns the Philistines’ grain and a cycle of revenge follows; men of Judah hand him over bound, but the Spirit of Yahweh comes on him, the ropes fall away, he kills a thousand men with a donkey’s jawbone, and God provides water for him.

16.title: Samson Escapes Gaza
16.context: Samson goes to Gaza and spends the night with a prostitute; the men of Gaza lie in wait to kill him, but at midnight he pulls up the city gate with its posts and carries it to the top of a hill facing Hebron.

16.title: Samson and Delilah
16.context: The Philistine rulers bribe Delilah to discover the secret of Samson’s strength; after three false answers he tells her he is a Nazirite whose hair has never been cut; his hair is shaved, his strength leaves him, and he is blinded and set to grinding grain in prison.

16.title: Samson’s Vengeance and Death
16.context: At a feast in Dagon’s temple the Philistines bring out Samson to mock him; his hair has begun to grow, he asks Yahweh for strength once more, pushes down the pillars and dies with the Philistines, killing more at his death than in his life.

17.title: Micah’s Idolatry
17.context: Micah of Ephraim makes idols from silver, sets up a shrine and hires a wandering Levite as his priest — a sign of the days when Israel had no king and each did as he saw fit.

18.title: The Danites Settle in Laish
18.context: The tribe of Dan looks for a place to settle and sends five men to spy out the land; at Micah’s house they recognize the Levite, and they report that Laish is a peaceful, unsuspecting city. Six hundred armed Danites take Micah’s idols and priest, destroy Laish, rebuild it as Dan, and set up the idols there.

19.title: The Crime of the Benjamites
19.context: A Levite traveling home with his concubine stops at Gibeah in Benjamin, where wicked men surround the house and abuse her until she dies; he cuts her body into twelve parts and sends them throughout Israel.

20.title: The Decree of the Assembly
20.context: Israelites from Dan to Beersheba and from Gilead gather as one at Mizpah, with 400,000 swordsmen; the Levite tells what happened, and the assembly resolves not to go home until Gibeah is punished. They demand that the Benjamites hand over the guilty men, but the Benjamites refuse.

20.title: Civil War against Benjamin
20.context: The tribes resolve to punish Gibeah, but Benjamin defends it; after two heavy defeats Israel weeps, fasts and inquires at Bethel, and Yahweh promises victory the third time.

20.title: Israel Wins the Battle
20.context: Israel sets an ambush and feigns retreat to draw the Benjamites away from Gibeah; the ambush rises up and sets the city ablaze, and the Benjamites are routed, with 25,100 killed and only 600 escaping to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites then burn Benjamin’s towns.

21.title: Wives for the Benjamites
21.context: Having sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin, Israel grieves that a tribe may vanish and resorts to violent means to provide wives for the surviving Benjamites; the book closes: in those days Israel had no king, and everyone did as he saw fit.

1.title: Naomi Becomes a Widow
1.context: In the days when the judges ruled, famine drives Elimelech of Bethlehem with his wife Naomi and two sons to live in Moab; Elimelech dies, the sons marry the Moabite women Orpah and Ruth, and after about ten years both sons also die, leaving Naomi bereaved and alone.

1.title: Ruth’s Loyalty to Naomi
1.context: Naomi decides to return to Bethlehem and urges her daughters-in-law to go home; Orpah leaves, but Ruth clings to her, saying Naomi’s people will be her people and Naomi’s God her God.

2.title: Boaz Meets Ruth
2.context: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz, who has heard of her loyalty to Naomi and treats her with kindness and protection; Naomi tells her that Boaz is one of their family’s kinsman-redeemers.

3.title: Ruth’s Redemption Assured
3.context: Naomi sends Ruth to the threshing floor at night to lie at Boaz’s feet; Ruth asks him to act as kinsman-redeemer, and he praises her as a woman of noble character but says a closer relative must be asked first.

4.title: Boaz Redeems Ruth
4.context: At the town gate before the elders, the nearer relative declines to marry Ruth and removes his sandal to confirm it; Boaz publicly announces that he will buy Elimelech’s property and take Ruth as his wife.

4.title: Boaz Marries Ruth
4.context: Ruth bears a son, Obed; the women of the town praise Yahweh with Naomi for giving her a redeemer, and Obed becomes the father of Jesse, the father of David.

1.title: Elkanah and His Wives
1.context: Elkanah of the hill country of Ephraim has two wives, Hannah, who has no children, and Peninnah, who has children and provokes her; each year he goes up to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to Yahweh of hosts, where Eli’s sons Hophni and Phinehas are priests.

1.title: Hannah Prays for a Son
1.context: In the sanctuary at Shiloh Hannah prays in anguish, vowing to give a son to Yahweh for life; Eli the priest at first thinks she is drunk, then blesses her.

1.title: The Birth of Samuel
1.context: Yahweh remembers Hannah; she conceives and bears a son whom she names Samuel, “because I asked Yahweh for him.” When he is weaned she brings him to Shiloh and gives him to Yahweh for as long as he lives.

2.title: Hannah’s Prayer of Thanksgiving
2.context: Hannah’s prayer rejoices in Yahweh, the incomparable Holy One who brings low and lifts up, raising the poor from the dust; it closes by saying he will strengthen his king and exalt his anointed.

2.title: Eli’s Wicked Sons
2.context: Eli’s sons are scoundrels who have no regard for Yahweh; they take for themselves whatever the fork brings up from the worshipers’ pot, demand raw meat before the fat is burned, and thereby treat Yahweh’s offering with contempt, so their sin is very great in his sight.

2.title: Samuel at Shiloh
2.context: The boy Samuel ministers before Yahweh in a linen ephod; each year his mother brings him a little robe when she comes up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. Eli blesses Elkanah and Hannah, Yahweh gives Hannah three more sons and two daughters, and Samuel grows up in Yahweh’s presence.

2.title: Eli and His Sons
2.context: The aged Eli hears of his sons’ wickedness and rebukes them for sinning against Yahweh, but they do not listen.

2.title: A Prophecy against the House of Eli
2.context: A man of God tells Eli that because he honored his sons above Yahweh, his house will decline, his two sons will die on the same day, and Yahweh will raise up a faithful priest.

3.title: Yahweh Calls Samuel
3.context: At a time when Yahweh’s word is rare, he calls the boy Samuel at night; Eli teaches him to answer, “Speak, your servant is listening,” and Yahweh announces judgment on Eli’s house. As Samuel grows, all Israel recognizes him as a prophet of Yahweh.

4.title: The Philistines Capture the Ark
4.context: Israel goes out to fight the Philistines at Ebenezer and loses about four thousand men; the elders have the ark of the covenant brought from Shiloh, and the camp roars, but the Philistines fight harder and slaughter thirty thousand of Israel’s foot soldiers, capture the ark, and kill Hophni and Phinehas.

4.title: The Death of Eli
4.context: A Benjamite runs from the battle to Shiloh with torn clothes and dust on his head; Eli, anxious for the ark of God, sits by the road watching, and when the messenger reports that the ark has been captured, Eli falls backward from his chair, breaks his neck and dies, having judged Israel forty years.

4.title: The Death of Phinehas's Widow
4.context: Phinehas’ wife, heavily pregnant, hears that the ark has been captured and her father-in-law and husband are dead, goes into labor, and dies after giving birth, naming her son Ichabod, “the glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God was taken.

5.title: The Ark Afflicts the Philistines
5.context: The Philistines place the ark in Dagon’s temple, and twice the idol falls on its face before it; wherever the ark is taken, plague breaks out, and the Philistines are terrified.

6.title: The Ark Returned to Israel
6.context: After seven months the Philistines send the ark back on a cart pulled by two cows, with gold guilt offerings, and the cows head straight for Beth Shemesh in Israel.

6.title: The Ark at Kiriath-jearim
6.context: The people of Beth Shemesh rejoice to see the ark, but Yahweh strikes down some who look into it; they ask who can stand in the presence of Yahweh, this holy God, and send to Kiriath Jearim to have it taken. The men there bring it to Abinadab’s house on the hill and consecrate his son Eleazar to guard it.

7.title: Samuel Subdues the Philistines
7.context: After the ark has been at Kiriath Jearim twenty years, Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods and serve Yahweh only; at Mizpah Yahweh routs the Philistines with thunder, and Samuel sets up a stone named Ebenezer, “thus far Yahweh has helped us.”

8.title: Israel Demands a King
8.context: Samuel’s sons take bribes, and the elders demand a king like the nations; Yahweh says they are rejecting him, not Samuel, as king; Samuel warns them what a king will take from them, but they insist.

9.title: Saul Chosen as King
9.context: Saul, a tall and impressive Benjamite, goes looking for lost donkeys and comes to Samuel, whom Yahweh has told that this is the man to anoint.

9.title: Samuel Anoints Saul King
9.context: Samuel privately anoints Saul as leader of Israel and gives him three signs; Saul meets a band of prophets, the Spirit of God comes on him, and he prophesies.

10.title: Saul Proclaimed King
10.context: Samuel gathers the people at Mizpah, where Saul is chosen by lot; found hiding among the baggage, he is presented to the people, who shout, “Long live the king!”

11.title: Saul Defeats the Ammonites
11.context: When the Ammonites besiege Jabesh Gilead, the Spirit of God comes on Saul, he rallies Israel and rescues the city, and the people reaffirm him as king at Gilgal.

12.title: Samuel’s Farewell Address
12.context: In his farewell Samuel asks the people to confirm his honesty, recalls Yahweh’s saving acts, and says asking for a king was wrong; yet if they and their king follow Yahweh all will be well, and he promises never to stop praying for them.

13.title: War with the Philistines
13.context: War breaks out with the Philistines and Israel’s troops scatter in fear; Saul, impatient for Samuel, offers the burnt offering himself; Samuel tells him that for disobeying Yahweh his kingdom will not last, and Yahweh has sought a man after his own heart.

14.title: Jonathan’s Victory over the Philistines
14.context: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb up to a Philistine outpost, trusting that Yahweh can save by many or by few; they kill about twenty men and panic spreads through the Philistine camp.

14.title: The Philistines Retreat
14.context: Saul’s lookouts see the Philistine army melting away; Saul counts his troops and finds Jonathan missing, then joins the battle, where the Philistines are striking each other with their swords, and Israelites who had hidden or defected join the pursuit. So Yahweh saves Israel that day.

14.title: Jonathan Eats the Honey
14.context: Saul binds the army with an oath not to eat until evening; Jonathan, unaware, tastes some honey, and when Saul wants to put him to death, the people rescue him, since he brought about the victory.

14.title: Saul’s Victories
14.context: Having taken the throne, Saul fights against Israel’s enemies on every side — Moab, Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah and the Philistines — and wherever he turns he inflicts punishment; he gallantly defeats the Amalekites and rescues Israel. The passage names Saul’s family and his commander Abner.

15.title: Saul’s Disobedience
15.context: Samuel brings Yahweh’s command to Saul: strike Amalek, who ambushed Israel on the way from Egypt, and devote all they have to destruction; Saul attacks but spares King Agag and keeps the best of the sheep, cattle and lambs, destroying only what is despised and weak.

15.title: Samuel Denounces Saul
15.context: Yahweh regrets making Saul king; Samuel rebukes Saul for keeping the Amalekite livestock, saying that obedience is better than sacrifice and that since Saul rejected Yahweh’s word, Yahweh has rejected him as king.

15.title: Saul’s Confession
15.context: Saul confesses that he gave in to the people out of fear; as Samuel turns away, Saul tears his robe, and Samuel says Yahweh has torn the kingdom from him and given it to someone better; Samuel never sees Saul again.

16.title: Samuel Anoints David
16.context: Yahweh sends Samuel to Jesse in Bethlehem to anoint a new king; none of seven sons is chosen, for people look at outward appearance but Yahweh looks at the heart; the youngest, the shepherd David, is anointed, and the Spirit of Yahweh comes on him from that day.

16.title: David Serves Saul
16.context: The Spirit of Yahweh departs from Saul and a tormenting spirit troubles him; his servants bring David, a skilled harpist, into his service, and his playing brings Saul relief.

17.title: Goliath’s Challenge
17.context: The Philistines assemble at Socoh and the Israelites at the Valley of Elah; the Philistine champion Goliath of Gath, over nine feet tall and armored in bronze, comes out morning and evening for forty days, challenging Israel to send a man to fight him. Saul and all Israel are dismayed and terrified.

17.title: David Accepts the Challenge
17.context: Sent with food for his brothers, David hears Goliath defy the armies of the living God and volunteers to fight him, telling Saul that Yahweh who rescued him from lion and bear will rescue him from this Philistine.

17.title: David Kills Goliath
17.context: David goes out without armor, with his staff, sling and five stones, saying he comes in the name of Yahweh of hosts, for the battle is Yahweh’s; one stone fells Goliath, and the Philistines flee.

17.title: David Is Brought before Saul
17.context: Saul asks whose son the young man is, and David, holding Goliath’s head, tells him he is the son of Jesse of Bethlehem.

18.title: Saul Envies David
18.context: Women sing that Saul has slain thousands and David tens of thousands, and from then on Saul is jealous; twice he throws his spear at David, and he fears David more because Yahweh is with him.

18.title: David Marries Michal
18.context: Saul hopes the Philistines will kill David and demands a hundred Philistine foreskins as the bride price for his daughter Michal; David brings double, marries Michal, and Saul becomes his enemy for life.

19.title: Saul Tries to Kill David
19.context: Saul orders David killed, and Jonathan intercedes; later Saul again throws his spear, Michal helps David escape through a window, and at Ramah with Samuel, Saul’s men and finally Saul himself are overcome by God’s Spirit and prophesy.

20.title: Jonathan Helps David
20.context: David asks Jonathan what he has done wrong; the two make a covenant and agree on a signal with arrows; when Saul’s intent to kill David is confirmed, they part in tears, bound by an oath in Yahweh’s name.

21.title: David Takes the Consecrated Bread
21.context: David flees to Nob, where the priest Ahimelech gives him consecrated bread and Goliath’s sword; then he goes to Gath and escapes only by pretending to be insane before the king.

22.title: David Flees to Adullam and Mizpeh
22.context: David hides in the cave of Adullam, where about four hundred distressed, indebted and discontented men gather to him; Saul, learning that Ahimelech helped David, has eighty-five priests of Nob killed, and only Abiathar escapes to David.

23.title: David Delivers Keilah
23.context: David hears that the Philistines are attacking Keilah and inquires of Yahweh, who tells him to go; David rescues the town. When Saul plans to trap him there, David asks Yahweh again and learns that the men of Keilah would hand him over, so he and his six hundred men leave.

23.title: David in the Hill Country
23.context: Saul searches for David every day, but God does not give him up; Jonathan finds David in the wilderness and strengthens him, saying he will be king; betrayed by the Ziphites, David is nearly caught when news of a Philistine raid forces Saul to turn back.

24.title: David Spares Saul
24.context: In a cave at En Gedi David could kill Saul but only cuts off a corner of his robe, refusing to harm Yahweh’s anointed; Saul weeps and admits that David is more righteous and will surely be king.

25.title: The Death of Samuel
25.context: Samuel dies, and all Israel assembles and mourns for him and buries him at his home in Ramah.

25.title: David, Nabal, and Abigail
25.context: The rich and surly Nabal refuses provisions to David’s men, and David sets out for revenge; Nabal’s wife Abigail meets him with gifts and persuades him not to shed blood himself; soon Yahweh strikes Nabal dead, and David marries Abigail.

26.title: David Again Spares Saul
26.context: David slips into Saul’s camp at night and takes the spear and water jug by his head, again refusing to harm Yahweh’s anointed; Saul admits he has done wrong, and they go their separate ways.

27.title: David and the Philistines
27.context: Fearing he will one day die at Saul’s hand, David goes with six hundred men to Achish king of Gath and settles at Ziklag, raiding Israel’s enemies while concealing it from Achish.

28.title: The Philistines Gather against Israel
28.context: Facing a great Philistine army and receiving no answer from Yahweh, Saul disguises himself and consults a medium at Endor to bring up Samuel, who tells him Yahweh has left him and that tomorrow he and his sons will die.

29.title: The Philistines Reject David
29.context: The Philistines gather their forces at Aphek, and Achish would take David with him, but the Philistine commanders object, fearing David might turn against them in the battle; Achish sends David back, and David and his men return early in the morning to Ziklag.

30.title: The Amalekites Raid Ziklag
30.context: David returns to find Ziklag raided and the families taken; his men talk of stoning him, but he finds strength in Yahweh, pursues the Amalekites, recovers everything, and shares the spoil with those who stayed behind and with Judah’s elders.

31.title: Saul’s Overthrow and Death
31.context: Israel is routed on Mount Gilboa; Saul’s three sons are killed, and the wounded Saul falls on his own sword; the Philistines hang his body on the wall of Beth Shan, and the men of Jabesh Gilead retrieve and bury it by night.

1.title: Saul’s Death Reported to David
1.context: A young Amalekite reaches David at Ziklag with the news that Saul and Jonathan are dead, claiming he finished off the wounded Saul and bringing his crown and armband. David tears his clothes, mourns and fasts, then has the man put to death for raising his hand against Yahweh’s anointed.

1.title: David’s Song for Saul and Jonathan
1.context: David composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan, the Song of the Bow, mourning how the mighty have fallen and grieving especially for Jonathan’s love for him.

2.title: David Anointed King of Judah
2.context: David inquires of Yahweh, who tells him to go up to Hebron; there with his two wives and his men he settles, and the men of Judah anoint him king over the house of Judah. He sends a message of blessing to the men of Jabesh Gilead for burying Saul.

2.title: Ish-bosheth Made King of Israel
2.context: Abner, the commander of Saul’s army, brings Saul’s son Ish-bosheth to Mahanaim and makes him king over Israel, while the house of Judah follows David; David reigns in Hebron seven and a half years.

2.title: The Battle of Gibeon
2.context: At the pool of Gibeon Abner’s men and Joab’s men meet; twelve from each side fight and all fall, and a fierce battle follows in which David’s men prevail. Asahel pursues Abner, who kills him with the butt of his spear, and at sunset Abner calls for a halt and withdraws.

3.title: The House of David Strengthened
3.context: Six sons are born to David at Hebron: Amnon, Kileab, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah and Ithream. The war between Saul’s house and David’s lasts a long time, but David grows stronger and Saul’s house weaker.

3.title: Abner Joins David
3.context: After a quarrel with Ish-bosheth, Abner makes a covenant with David and persuades Israel’s elders to support him; David feasts him and sends him away in peace.

3.title: Joab Murders Abner
3.context: Joab returns from a raid, learns that Abner has been with David, and rebukes the king for letting him go; without David’s knowledge he sends messengers to bring Abner back, then takes him aside at the gate of Hebron and stabs him to avenge his brother Asahel.

3.title: David Mourns for Abner
3.context: David leads public mourning for Abner, walking behind the bier and fasting until sunset, showing he had no part in the killing, and the people are satisfied.

4.title: The Murder of Ish-bosheth
4.context: Two officers murder Ish-bosheth during his midday rest and bring his head to David, who executes them for killing an innocent man and buries the head in Abner’s tomb.

5.title: David Anointed King of All Israel
5.context: All the tribes come to Hebron and anoint David king over all Israel; he is thirty years old and reigns forty years.

5.title: Two Victories over the Philistines
5.context: Twice the Philistines attack, and both times David inquires of Yahweh and wins by following his directions.

6.title: David Fetches the Ark
6.context: David moves the ark on a new cart, Uzzah dies for touching it, and the ark stays at Obed-Edom’s house, which is blessed; three months later David brings it into the City of David with great joy, dancing before Yahweh, though Michal despises him.

7.title: God’s Covenant with David
7.context: David wants to build a house for the ark; through Nathan, Yahweh answers that instead he will build a house for David: a descendant of his will build a temple for Yahweh’s name, his throne will be established forever, and Yahweh will be his father and he will be his son.

7.title: David’s Prayer of Thanksgiving
7.context: David sits before Yahweh in humble thanks, amazed that he and his family should receive such grace, affirms that Yahweh’s words are true, and asks him to bless his house forever as promised.

8.title: David’s Triumphs
8.context: David wins victories on every side — over the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Aram and Edom — dedicating the spoils to Yahweh, and he rules all his people with justice and righteousness.

9.title: David and Mephibosheth
9.context: For Jonathan’s sake David seeks anyone left of Saul’s family, finds the lame Mephibosheth, restores Saul’s land to him, and gives him a place at the king’s table for life.

10.title: David’s Messengers Disgraced
10.context: David sends envoys to console the new Ammonite king, but they are humiliated; the Ammonites hire Aramean troops, and Joab and then David defeat them.

11.title: David and Bathsheba
11.context: Staying in Jerusalem while the army is at war, David sees Bathsheba bathing, sleeps with her and she becomes pregnant; when his cover-up fails, he arranges through Joab for her husband Uriah to die in battle and marries her — and Yahweh is displeased.

12.title: Nathan Rebukes David
12.context: Nathan rebukes David with a parable of a rich man who takes a poor man’s only lamb, and says, “You are the man”; David confesses, and Yahweh forgives him, but the sword will never leave his house, and the child will die.

12.title: David's Son Dies
12.context: David fasts and pleads while the child is ill; when the child dies, he gets up, washes and worships, saying he will go to the child, but the child will not return to him.

12.title: Solomon’s Birth
12.context: David comforts his wife Bathsheba and goes to her; she bears a son whom they name Solomon. Yahweh loves him and sends word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah, “beloved of Yahweh.”

12.title: The Capture of Rabbah
12.context: Joab attacks Rabbah of the Ammonites and captures its royal citadel, then sends for David to complete the conquest lest the city be named after Joab; David gathers the rest of the army, takes Rabbah, removes the king’s crown and great plunder, and sets the people to labor, then returns to Jerusalem.

13.title: Amnon and Tamar
13.context: David’s son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar and then hates her; Absalom takes her in and nurses his hatred, and David, though furious, does not punish Amnon.

13.title: Absalom’s Revenge on Amnon
13.context: Two years later Absalom has Amnon killed at a sheep-shearing feast and flees to his grandfather in Geshur, where he stays three years.

14.title: Absalom’s Return to Jerusalem
14.context: Joab sends a wise woman from Tekoa with a made-up case to move David, who agrees to bring Absalom back but will not let him see his face.

14.title: Absalom Reconciled to David
14.context: After two years in Jerusalem without seeing the king, Absalom sets Joab’s field on fire to force him to intercede, and is finally received by David, who kisses him.

15.title: Absalom’s Conspiracy
15.context: Absalom wins the hearts of the people by intercepting those coming to the king for justice; after four years he declares himself king at Hebron, and David’s counselor Ahithophel joins him.

15.title: David Flees Jerusalem
15.context: Hearing that Israel has gone over to Absalom, David flees Jerusalem with his household; he sends the ark back with the priests, trusting Yahweh to bring him back if he wills, and climbs the Mount of Olives weeping, praying that Ahithophel’s counsel be turned to folly.

16.title: David and Ziba
16.context: Just beyond the summit, Ziba, Mephibosheth’s servant, meets David with donkeys loaded with bread, raisins, fruit and wine, and falsely tells him that his master is staying in Jerusalem hoping to regain his grandfather’s kingdom; David gives Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth.

16.title: Shimei Curses David
