16.context: Shimei, of Saul’s clan, curses David and throws stones at him along the road; Abishai wants to kill him, but David lets him curse, hoping Yahweh will see his distress and repay him with good.

16.title: The Counsel of Ahithophel and Hushai
16.context: Absalom enters Jerusalem, and David’s friend Hushai pretends to join him; Ahithophel advises Absalom to sleep openly with his father’s concubines as a sign of complete break with David.

17.title: Hushai Counters Ahithophel’s Advice
17.context: Ahithophel advises an immediate strike to kill David, but Hushai urges Absalom to gather all Israel first; Absalom prefers Hushai’s plan, for Yahweh had determined to defeat Ahithophel’s good advice.

17.title: Hushai’s Warning Saves David
17.context: Hushai sends word to David by messengers who hide in a well to escape pursuers, and David crosses the Jordan that night; Ahithophel, seeing his advice ignored, goes home and hangs himself.

18.title: Absalom Killed
18.context: David’s army wins a great victory in the forest of Ephraim; Absalom is caught by his head in an oak tree, and Joab, ignoring David’s order to deal gently with him, kills him.

18.title: David Mourns for Absalom
18.context: When the messengers arrive, David asks only whether young Absalom is safe; learning of his death, he goes up to the gate chamber and weeps, wishing he had died instead.

19.title: Joab Reproves David
19.context: David’s grief turns the victory into mourning and the troops slink back ashamed; Joab warns him that he will lose his men unless he encourages them, so David takes his seat at the gate.

19.title: David Restored as King
19.context: The tribes debate bringing David back; he asks Judah’s elders to take the lead and promises Amasa command of the army in place of Joab, and Judah unites to welcome the king home.

19.title: David Forgives Shimei
19.context: Shimei falls at David’s feet at the Jordan and begs forgiveness; Abishai wants him executed, but David says no one should die in Israel that day and swears to spare him.

19.title: Mephibosheth Excused
19.context: Mephibosheth comes out to meet David and says Ziba deceived him; David orders the land divided between them, but Mephibosheth says Ziba can have it all, since the king has come home safely.

19.title: David’s Kindness to Barzillai
19.context: The aged Barzillai, who had supported David, declines the invitation to live in Jerusalem because of his age and asks David to take his servant Kimham instead.

19.title: Contention over the King
19.context: At Gilgal the men of Israel complain that Judah has taken the king for itself, and a sharp quarrel breaks out, with Judah answering more harshly.

20.title: Sheba’s Rebellion
20.context: Sheba the Benjamite leads Israel in revolt against David; when Amasa is slow, Joab kills him and besieges Sheba at Abel, where a wise woman persuades the town to throw Sheba’s head over the wall, ending the rebellion.

21.title: David Avenges the Gibeonites
21.context: A three-year famine comes because Saul killed the Gibeonites; at their demand David hands over seven of Saul’s descendants, Rizpah guards their bodies day and night, and David then gives Saul and Jonathan an honorable burial.

21.title: Four Battles against the Philistines
21.context: In further wars with the Philistines, David is nearly killed by a giant and rescued by Abishai; his warriors kill four descendants of the giants.

22.title: David’s Song of Deliverance
22.context: David’s song after Yahweh delivered him from all his enemies (close to Psalm 18): Yahweh is his rock, fortress and deliverer, who reached down from on high to rescue him.

23.title: David’s Last Song
23.context: David’s last words: the Spirit of Yahweh spoke through him; one who rules justly in the fear of God is like the morning light, and God has made an everlasting covenant with his house.

23.title: David’s Mighty Men
23.context: A roll of David’s mighty men and their exploits, including three who broke through enemy lines to bring him water from Bethlehem’s well, which he poured out to Yahweh; the list ends with Uriah the Hittite.

24.title: David’s Military Census
24.context: After counting the fighting men, David is conscience-stricken and confesses; he chooses to fall into Yahweh’s hands, and a plague strikes Israel until Yahweh stops the angel at Jerusalem; David buys Araunah’s threshing floor, builds an altar, and the plague ends.

1.title: Abishag Cares for David
1.context: David is old and cannot keep warm, so his servants find a young woman, Abishag of Shunem, to care for him; the king has no intimate relations with her.

1.title: Adonijah Usurps the Kingdom
1.context: Adonijah, David’s son, exalts himself and says he will be king; with Joab and Abiathar behind him, he holds a feast at the Stone of Zoheleth, inviting his brothers and the royal officials of Judah but not Nathan, Benaiah or Solomon.

1.title: Nathan and Bathsheba before David
1.context: Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his oath that Solomon would reign; David has Solomon anointed at Gihon amid public rejoicing, and the frightened Adonijah clings to the horns of the altar.

2.title: David Instructs Solomon
2.context: As his death nears, David charges Solomon to be strong, to walk in Yahweh’s ways and keep his decrees, so that Yahweh will keep his promise to David’s line; he also tells Solomon how to deal with Joab and Shimei and to show kindness to Barzillai’s sons.

2.title: David’s Reign and Death
2.context: David rests with his ancestors and is buried in the City of David, having reigned forty years — seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem; Solomon sits on his father’s throne and his rule is firmly established.

2.title: The Execution of Adonijah
2.context: Adonijah asks Bathsheba to ask King Solomon for Abishag as his wife; Solomon sees it as a bid for the throne and has Benaiah put him to death. He also removes Abiathar from the priesthood, fulfilling what Yahweh said at Shiloh about Eli’s house.

2.title: The Execution of Joab
2.context: Joab, hearing what has happened, flees to the tent of Yahweh and takes hold of the horns of the altar; Solomon has Benaiah strike him down there, for the blood he shed in killing Abner and Amasa, and Benaiah replaces Joab as commander and Zadok replaces Abiathar.

2.title: The Execution of Shimei
2.context: Solomon orders Shimei to build a house in Jerusalem and never leave it, on pain of death; three years later Shimei goes to Gath to recover two runaway slaves, and Solomon has Benaiah execute him for breaking his oath, so that the kingdom is firmly established in Solomon’s hands.

3.title: Solomon’s Prayer for Wisdom
3.context: At Gibeon Yahweh appears to Solomon in a dream and invites him to ask for anything; he asks for a discerning heart to govern the people, and Yahweh, pleased, gives him wisdom and also riches and honor.

3.title: Solomon Judges Wisely
3.context: Two women claim the same baby; Solomon orders the child cut in two, the true mother gives up her claim to save his life, and all Israel stands in awe, seeing that he has wisdom from God.

4.title: Solomon’s Princes
4.context: King Solomon rules over all Israel, and his officials include Azariah son of Zadok the priest, the secretaries Elihoreph and Ahijah, Jehoshaphat the recorder, Benaiah over the army, Zabud, Ahishar over the palace, and Adoniram over forced labor.

4.title: Solomon’s Prosperity
4.context: Under Solomon, Judah and Israel are numerous and prosperous, living in safety, and his rule extends from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt, with surrounding kingdoms paying tribute.

4.title: Solomon’s Wisdom
4.context: God gives Solomon wisdom greater than all the wise men of the East and Egypt; he speaks three thousand proverbs and over a thousand songs, and people come from every nation to hear him.

5.title: Preparations for the Temple
5.context: Solomon makes a treaty with Hiram king of Tyre, trading grain and oil for cedar from Lebanon, and conscripts large work crews to prepare for building Yahweh’s temple.

6.title: Temple Construction Begins
6.context: In the 480th year after the exodus, the fourth year of his reign, Solomon begins building Yahweh’s temple, using stone dressed at the quarry so that no hammer or chisel is heard at the site.

6.title: God’s Promise to Solomon
6.context: The word of Yahweh comes to Solomon: if he follows Yahweh’s decrees, keeps his commands and obeys them, Yahweh will fulfill through him the promise he gave to David, and will dwell among the Israelites and not abandon his people Israel.

6.title: The Temple’s Interior
6.context: Solomon completes the temple: the inside walls are paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling and the floor covered with juniper; the inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place, is twenty cubits long and overlaid with pure gold, as is the cedar altar, and the walls are carved with cherubim, palm trees and open flowers.

6.title: The Cherubim
6.context: In the inner sanctuary he makes two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high, with wings of five cubits so that the wingspan of each is ten; their wings touch each other in the middle of the room and reach the walls on either side, and both are overlaid with gold.

6.title: The Doors
6.context: The walls of both rooms are carved all around with cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, and the floors of both are overlaid with gold; the doors of the inner and outer sanctuary are made of olive and juniper wood, carved the same way and overlaid with gold.

7.title: Solomon’s Palace Complex
7.context: Solomon takes thirteen years to complete the building of his own palace; it includes the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon, the Colonnade, the Hall of the Throne for judgment, and a residence for Pharaoh’s daughter, all built of costly stone cut to size.

7.title: The Pillars and Capitals
7.context: King Solomon sends to Tyre for Huram, whose mother is a widow from the tribe of Naphtali and whose father was a Tyrian bronze worker; he is highly skilled and experienced in all kinds of bronze work and comes to Solomon to do all the work assigned to him.

7.title: The Two Bronze Pillars
7.context: Huram casts two bronze pillars, each eighteen cubits high and twelve in circumference, with bronze capitals five cubits high decorated with network and pomegranates; he sets them up at the portico of the temple and names the one on the south Jakin and the one on the north Boaz.

7.title: The Molten Sea
7.context: He makes the Sea, a huge round basin of cast metal ten cubits across, five high and thirty in circumference, with gourd-shaped decorations beneath the rim; it rests on twelve bronze bulls facing outward in groups of three, and holds about two thousand baths.

7.title: The Ten Bronze Stands
7.context: He also makes ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four wide and three high, with panels decorated with lions, bulls and cherubim, each carrying a basin holding forty baths; five are placed on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and the Sea is placed at the southeast corner.

7.title: Completion of the Bronze Works
7.context: The craftsman Huram completes all the bronze work for the temple — the two pillars, the Sea on twelve bulls, the stands and utensils — so much bronze that it could not be weighed.

7.title: The Temple Work Is Finished
7.context: When all the work King Solomon had done for the temple of Yahweh is finished, he brings in the things his father David had dedicated — the silver, the gold and the furnishings — and puts them in the treasuries of Yahweh’s temple.

8.title: The Ark Enters the Temple
8.context: At the Festival of Tabernacles Solomon brings the ark into the new temple and places it under the cherubim in the Most Holy Place; when the priests withdraw, the cloud of Yahweh’s glory fills the temple so they cannot minister.

8.title: Solomon Blesses Yahweh
8.context: Solomon blesses the assembly and praises Yahweh for keeping his promise to David, choosing Jerusalem and having David’s son build the temple for his name.

8.title: Solomon’s Prayer of Dedication
8.context: Before the altar Solomon prays with outstretched hands, confessing that no god is like Yahweh and even the highest heaven cannot contain him; he asks that whenever his people, or even foreigners, pray toward this house in any trouble, Yahweh will hear from heaven and forgive.

8.title: Solomon’s Benediction
8.context: Rising from prayer, Solomon blesses the people, asking Yahweh to be with them and turn their hearts to him, so that all the peoples of the earth may know that Yahweh is God and there is no other.

8.title: Sacrifices of Dedication
8.context: The king and people offer a vast number of sacrifices to dedicate the temple and celebrate for fourteen days, then go home rejoicing in Yahweh’s goodness.

9.title: Yahweh’s Response to Solomon
9.context: After the temple and palace are finished, Yahweh appears to Solomon a second time: he has consecrated the temple; if Solomon walks faithfully his throne will endure, but if Israel turns to other gods it will be cut off and the temple become a byword.

9.title: Solomon’s Additional Achievements
9.context: At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon built the temple and his palace, he gives twenty towns in Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar, juniper and gold; Hiram, when he sees them, is not pleased and calls them the Land of Cabul, though he had sent the king 120 talents of gold.

9.title: Solomon's Other Achievements
9.context: Solomon uses forced labor to build the temple, his palace, Jerusalem’s wall and cities such as Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer, and sends ships with Hiram’s sailors to Ophir for gold.

10.title: The Queen of Sheba
10.context: The queen of Sheba comes with rich gifts to test Solomon with hard questions; seeing his wisdom and splendor, she says she was not told even half, and praises Yahweh for making him king to do justice and righteousness.

10.title: Solomon’s Wealth and Splendor
10.context: Solomon receives 666 talents of gold a year, makes gold shields and an ivory throne, and drinks from gold vessels; he surpasses all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.

10.title: Solomon's Chariots and Horsemen
10.context: Solomon accumulates chariots and horses, importing horses from Egypt and Kue, and makes silver as common as stones in Jerusalem.

11.title: Solomon’s Foreign Wives
11.context: Solomon marries many foreign wives who in his old age turn his heart to other gods, for whom he builds shrines; Yahweh, angry, declares he will tear most of the kingdom from his son, leaving one tribe for David’s sake.

11.title: Hadad’s Return
11.context: Yahweh raises up adversaries against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, who returns from Egypt after Joab’s killing of Edom’s men, and Rezon son of Eliada, who gains control of Damascus and is Israel’s enemy throughout Solomon’s lifetime.

11.title: Jeroboam’s Rebellion
11.context: The prophet Ahijah tears a new cloak into twelve pieces and gives ten to Jeroboam, a sign that Yahweh will give him ten tribes; Solomon tries to kill him, and he flees to Egypt.

11.title: The Death of Solomon
11.context: The other events of Solomon’s reign, all he did and his wisdom, are written in the book of the annals of Solomon; he reigns forty years in Jerusalem over all Israel, then rests with his ancestors and is buried in the city of his father David, and his son Rehoboam succeeds him.

12.title: Rebellion against Rehoboam
12.context: Rehoboam rejects the elders’ advice to lighten the people’s burden and threatens a heavier yoke instead; the ten northern tribes break away and make Jeroboam king, leaving only Judah with the house of David.

12.title: Shemaiah’s Prophecy
12.context: Rehoboam assembles 180,000 chosen warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight against Israel and regain the kingdom, but the word of God comes to Shemaiah, the man of God: do not go up to fight your fellow Israelites, go home, for this is my doing. They obey the word of Yahweh and return.

12.title: Jeroboam’s Idolatry
12.context: Fearing the people will return to Rehoboam if they worship in Jerusalem, Jeroboam sets up two golden calves at Bethel and Dan, presenting them as the gods who brought Israel out of Egypt — a sin that marks the northern kingdom.

12.title: Calf Worship at Bethel Condemned
12.context: Jeroboam establishes a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the festival held in Judah, and offers sacrifices on the altar at Bethel to the calves he made there; he also appoints priests for the high places he had made, and himself goes up to the altar to make offerings.

13.title: The Old Prophet and the Man of God
13.context: A man of God from Judah prophesies against the altar at Bethel; though commanded not to eat there, he is deceived by an old prophet into sharing a meal and is killed by a lion on the way home, showing the seriousness of disobeying Yahweh’s word.

13.title: Jeroboam's Grave Sin
13.context: Even after this, Jeroboam does not change his evil ways, but again appoints priests for the high places from all sorts of people, consecrating anyone who wants to be one; this becomes the sin of the house of Jeroboam that leads to its downfall and destruction from the face of the earth.

14.title: Ahijah’s Prophecy against Jeroboam
14.context: When Jeroboam’s son falls ill, his wife goes in disguise to the prophet Ahijah, who announces that Jeroboam’s house will be cut off, the boy will die, and Israel will one day be uprooted from the land.

14.title: Nadab Succeeds Jeroboam
14.context: Jeroboam reigns twenty-two years, then rests with his ancestors, and his son Nadab succeeds him as king.

14.title: Rehoboam Reigns in Judah
14.context: Rehoboam reigns seventeen years in Judah, where people build high places and idols; Pharaoh Shishak attacks and carries off the treasures of the temple and palace, including Solomon’s gold shields.

15.title: Abijam Reigns in Judah
15.context: Abijam reigns three years in Judah, following his father’s sins, yet for David’s sake Yahweh keeps a lamp burning for him in Jerusalem.

15.title: Asa Reigns in Judah
15.context: Asa reigns forty-one years in Judah and does right in Yahweh’s eyes, removing idols and even deposing his grandmother for idolatry, though in his war with Israel he buys Aram’s help with temple treasures.

15.title: Nadab Reigns in Israel
15.context: Nadab king of Israel reigns two years before Baasha assassinates him and wipes out Jeroboam’s family, fulfilling the prophet’s word.

15.title: Baasha Reigns in Israel
15.context: In the third year of Asa, Baasha son of Ahijah becomes king of Israel in Tirzah and reigns twenty-four years, doing evil in Yahweh’s sight and walking in Jeroboam’s ways; the word of Yahweh comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha (see 16:1–7).

16.title: Elah Reigns in Israel
16.context: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa, Elah son of Baasha becomes king of Israel and reigns two years in Tirzah; while he is drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, his chariot commander Zimri strikes him down and kills Baasha’s whole family, as Yahweh had foretold through Jehu.

16.title: Zimri Reigns in Israel
16.context: Zimri kills Elah and reigns only seven days; the army proclaims its commander Omri king, and Zimri dies in the burning palace.

16.title: Omri Reigns in Israel
16.context: Omri reigns twelve years over Israel, six in Tirzah; he buys the hill of Samaria for two talents of silver, fortifies it, and names the city Samaria after Shemer, the previous owner. He does evil in Yahweh’s sight, more than all before him, and when he dies his son Ahab succeeds him.

16.title: Ahab Reigns in Israel, Marries Jezebel
16.context: Ahab reigns twenty-two years in Israel, marries the Sidonian princess Jezebel, builds a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria, and does more evil than all the kings before him.

17.title: The Ravens Feed Elijah
17.context: Elijah announces that there will be no rain for years; Yahweh sends him to hide by the Kerith brook, where ravens bring him bread and meat morning and evening.

17.title: The Widow of Zarephath
17.context: Elijah stays with a widow in Zarephath whose flour and oil do not run out during the famine; when her son dies, Elijah prays and Yahweh restores the boy to life.

18.title: Elijah’s Message to Ahab
18.context: In the third year of drought Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, asking the people how long they will waver between two opinions; Baal’s prophets cry out all day with no answer, but at Elijah’s prayer fire falls from Yahweh, and the people fall down, confessing that Yahweh is God.

18.title: Yahweh Sends Rain
18.context: Elijah prays on top of Carmel until, on the seventh look, a small cloud rises from the sea and heavy rain follows; the power of Yahweh comes on him and he runs ahead of Ahab’s chariot to Jezreel.

19.title: Elijah Flees from Jezebel
19.context: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees to the wilderness and asks to die; an angel feeds him and he travels to Horeb, where Yahweh is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but speaks in a gentle whisper, sends him back to anoint new kings and Elisha, and tells him seven thousand have not bowed to Baal.

19.title: The Call of Elisha
19.context: Elijah throws his cloak over Elisha as he plows; Elisha slaughters his oxen to feed the people and then follows Elijah as his servant.

20.title: Ben-hadad Attacks Samaria
20.context: Ben-Hadad of Aram besieges Samaria with a coalition and makes ever greater demands; a prophet tells Ahab that Yahweh will hand over the army so that he will know Yahweh is God, and Israel wins a great victory.

20.title: Another War with Ben-hadad
20.context: The Arameans think Israel’s God is only a god of the hills and fight on the plain, but a man of God says Yahweh will prove otherwise and Israel wins again; yet Ahab makes a treaty with Ben-Hadad and lets him go.

20.title: A Prophet Reproves Ahab
20.context: A prophet disguised as a wounded soldier tells Ahab a story that makes the king pronounce his own sentence: because he released the man Yahweh had devoted to destruction, his life will pay for it.

21.title: Naboth’s Vineyard
21.context: Ahab covets Naboth’s vineyard, but Naboth will not sell his inheritance; Jezebel has him falsely accused and stoned; Elijah announces disaster on Ahab’s house, but because Ahab humbles himself, it is delayed until his son’s days.

22.title: Ahab and the False Prophets
22.context: Ahab invites Jehoshaphat of Judah to attack Ramoth Gilead; four hundred prophets promise victory, but Micaiah, Yahweh’s prophet, foresees Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd and a lying spirit in the prophets’ mouths, and Ahab has him imprisoned.

22.title: Ahab’s Defeat and Death
22.context: Ahab goes into battle in disguise but is struck by an arrow shot at random and dies by evening; dogs lick his blood at the pool of Samaria, as Yahweh had said.

22.title: Jehoshaphat Reigns in Judah
22.context: Jehoshaphat reigns twenty-five years in Judah, doing right like his father Asa, though the high places remain; his ships built to sail to Ophir for gold are wrecked at Ezion Geber.

22.title: Ahaziah Reigns in Israel
22.context: Ahab’s son Ahaziah reigns two years in Israel, following the ways of his parents and Jeroboam and serving Baal, provoking Yahweh to anger.

1.title: Elijah Denounces Ahaziah
1.context: Injured in a fall, King Ahaziah sends to consult Baal-Zebub of Ekron; Elijah intercepts the messengers, asking whether there is no God in Israel, and declares the king will die; two companies sent to seize Elijah are consumed by fire, and Ahaziah dies as foretold.

1.title: Jehoram Succeeds Ahaziah
1.context: Because Ahaziah has no son, his brother Joram succeeds him as king of Israel, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.

2.title: Elijah Taken Up to Heaven
2.context: As Elijah is about to be taken up, Elisha refuses to leave him; Elijah parts the Jordan with his cloak and asks what Elisha wants, and Elisha asks for a double portion of his spirit.

2.title: Elijah Taken Up in a Whirlwind
2.context: A chariot and horses of fire separate them and Elijah goes up in a whirlwind; Elisha takes up his cloak, parts the Jordan in the same way, and the prophets say the spirit of Elijah rests on him.

2.title: Elisha Heals the Waters of Jericho
2.context: Elisha heals Jericho’s bad water with salt; on the road to Bethel a crowd of youths mocks him, and two bears come out and maul them.

3.title: Moab’s Rebellion
3.context: When Moab rebels, the kings of Israel, Judah and Edom march against it and run out of water in the desert; for Jehoshaphat’s sake Elisha seeks Yahweh, who promises to fill the valley with water and give Moab into their hands.

3.title: Moab Flees
3.context: The Moabites see the water red in the morning sun, think the allies have killed each other and rush to plunder, but are routed; when the king of Moab sacrifices his firstborn son on the city wall, Israel withdraws.

4.title: The Widow’s Oil
4.context: A prophet’s widow is about to lose her two sons to a creditor; Elisha tells her to borrow empty jars, and her single jar of oil fills them all, so she can pay her debt and live on the rest.

4.title: The Shunammite Woman
4.context: A woman of Shunem regularly hosts Elisha and builds him a room; he promises her a son, and when the boy later dies, Elisha prays and stretches himself on him, and the child comes back to life.

4.title: Elisha Purifies the Poisonous Stew
4.context: During a famine Elisha makes a poisoned stew harmless by adding flour, and feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves, with some left over.

5.title: Naaman Cured of Leprosy
5.context: Naaman, an Aramean commander with leprosy, comes to Elisha at the word of a captive Israelite girl; after washing seven times in the Jordan he is healed and confesses Israel’s God, while Elisha’s greedy servant Gehazi is struck with the disease.

6.title: The Axe Head Floats
6.context: A borrowed axhead falls into the Jordan while the prophets are cutting timber; Elisha throws a stick in, and the iron floats.

6.title: Elisha Captures the Blinded Arameans
6.context: Elisha repeatedly warns Israel’s king of Aramean ambushes; when an army surrounds Dothan to seize him, his servant panics until Yahweh opens his eyes to see hills full of horses and chariots of fire; the Arameans are struck blind, led to Samaria, fed and sent home.

6.title: The Siege and Famine of Samaria
6.context: Ben-Hadad besieges Samaria and famine becomes so terrible that people eat their children; the king blames Elisha and vows to kill him.

7.title: The Arameans Flee
7.context: Four lepers decide to surrender to the Arameans and find their camp deserted, for Yahweh had made them hear the sound of a great army and flee; the city is fed, as Elisha foretold, and the officer who doubted is trampled to death.

8.title: The Shunammite’s Land Restored
8.context: The Shunammite woman, warned by Elisha, escapes a seven-year famine abroad; when she returns to claim her land, the king is just hearing about Elisha’s deeds and restores everything to her.

8.title: Hazael Murders Ben-hadad
8.context: In Damascus Elisha tells Hazael that he will be king of Aram and weeps over the harm he will do Israel; the next day Hazael smothers Ben-Hadad and takes the throne.

8.title: Jehoram Reigns in Judah
8.context: Jehoram reigns in Judah and, married to Ahab’s daughter, follows the ways of Ahab’s house, yet Yahweh does not destroy Judah because of his covenant with David.

8.title: Ahaziah Reigns in Judah
8.context: Ahaziah, son of Ahab’s daughter Athaliah, reigns one year in Judah, following the ways of Ahab’s house, and goes to visit the wounded Joram king of Israel.

9.title: Jehu Anointed King of Israel
9.context: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu king of Israel, commissioned to wipe out Ahab’s house and avenge the blood of the prophets; his fellow officers immediately proclaim him king.

9.title: Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
9.context: Jehu drives to Jezreel and kills Joram with an arrow, throwing his body onto Naboth’s field; Ahaziah king of Judah is pursued and killed as well.

9.title: Ahaziah King of Judah Is Killed
9.context: Seeing this, Ahaziah king of Judah flees, but Jehu pursues and orders his men to shoot him too; wounded, he escapes to Megiddo and dies there. His servants take him by chariot to Jerusalem and bury him with his ancestors in the City of David.

9.title: Jezebel’s Violent Death
9.context: Jezebel, painted and mocking Jehu from a window, is thrown down by her eunuchs and killed, and dogs devour her body, as Elijah had foretold.

10.title: Ahab’s Seventy Sons Killed
10.context: At Jehu’s demand the leaders of Samaria kill Ahab’s seventy sons and send their heads to Jezreel; Jehu then wipes out the rest of Ahab’s house there, fulfilling Yahweh’s word.

10.title: Ahab's Sons Are Killed
10.context: Jehu kills everyone in Jezreel who remains of the house of Ahab, together with all his chief men, close friends and priests, leaving him no survivor.

10.title: Ahaziah's Relatives Are Killed
10.context: On his way to Samaria, Jehu meets forty-two relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah, who say they are going down to greet the families of the king and queen mother; he orders them taken alive and they are killed at the well of Beth Eked, and not one is left.

10.title: The Rest of Ahab's House Is Killed
10.context: Jehu takes Jehonadab son of Rekab into his chariot to see his zeal for Yahweh, and in Samaria kills all who remain of Ahab’s family.

10.title: Jehu Kills the Priests of Baal
10.context: Pretending to be a great devotee of Baal, Jehu gathers all Baal’s prophets and worshipers into his temple, has them killed, and demolishes it, wiping out Baal worship in Israel.

10.title: Jehoahaz Succeeds Jehu in Israel
10.context: Yet Jehu does not turn from Jeroboam’s golden calves, and Yahweh begins to shrink Israel’s territory as Hazael conquers the land east of the Jordan.

11.title: Athaliah and Joash
11.context: When Athaliah, mother of Ahaziah, sees that her son is dead, she moves to destroy the whole royal family; but Jehosheba, Ahaziah’s sister, takes the infant Joash and hides him and his nurse in the temple of Yahweh for six years while Athaliah rules the land.

11.title: Jehoiada Restores the Worship of Yahweh
11.context: The priest Jehoiada crowns Joash, has the usurper Athaliah put to death, leads king and people in a covenant to be Yahweh’s people, and the temple of Baal is torn down.

12.title: Joash Repairs the Temple
12.context: Under Jehoiada’s instruction Joash does right, setting up a collection chest so that the people’s gifts pay for repairs to Yahweh’s temple, carried out by honest workers.

13.title: Jehoahaz Reigns in Israel
13.context: Under Jehoahaz Israel is oppressed by Aram; he seeks Yahweh, who provides a deliverer, yet Israel still clings to the sins of Jeroboam.

13.title: Jehoash Reigns in Israel
13.context: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz becomes king of Israel in Samaria and reigns sixteen years, doing evil in Yahweh’s sight and following the sins of Jeroboam; he fights against Amaziah king of Judah, and when he dies, Jeroboam succeeds him.

13.title: Elisha’s Final Prophecy
13.context: As Elisha lies dying, King Jehoash weeps over him; Elisha has him shoot an arrow and strike the ground, and because he strikes only three times, Israel will defeat Aram only three times; after Elisha’s death, a dead man thrown into his tomb revives on touching his bones.

13.title: Israel at War with Aram
13.context: Yahweh shows Israel compassion because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and Jehoash defeats Aram three times and recovers the lost towns.

14.title: Amaziah Reigns in Judah
14.context: Amaziah of Judah does right, though not like David; proud after defeating Edom, he challenges Israel’s king, is badly beaten, and Jerusalem’s wall is breached and its treasures taken.

14.title: The Death of Amaziah
14.context: Amaziah is later assassinated, and the people make his sixteen-year-old son Azariah (Uzziah) king.

14.title: Jeroboam II Reigns in Israel
14.context: Jeroboam II reigns forty-one years over Israel; though he does evil, Yahweh uses him to restore Israel’s borders, as the prophet Jonah had foretold.

15.title: Azariah Reigns in Judah
15.context: Azariah reigns fifty-two years in Judah and does right, though the high places remain; Yahweh afflicts him with leprosy, and he lives in isolation while his son Jotham governs.

15.title: Zechariah Reigns in Israel
15.context: Israel enters a time of turmoil: Zechariah and Shallum are assassinated in quick succession, fulfilling Yahweh’s word that Jehu’s line would last four generations.

15.title: Shallum Reigns in Israel
15.context: Shallum son of Jabesh reigns a full month in Samaria; then Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah to Samaria, strikes him down and assassinates him, and reigns in his place.

15.title: Menahem Reigns in Israel
15.context: Menahem pays tribute to Pul of Assyria by taxing the wealthy; under his successors Pekahiah and Pekah, Assyria begins deporting Israelites.

15.title: Pekahiah Reigns in Israel
15.context: Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years in Samaria, doing evil in Yahweh’s sight; his chief officer Pekah son of Remaliah conspires against him and kills him in the citadel of the royal palace with fifty men from Gilead, and reigns in his place.

15.title: Pekah Reigns in Israel
15.context: Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years in Samaria, doing evil in Yahweh’s sight; in his time Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria captures Ijon, Abel Beth Maakah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead and Galilee and deports the people to Assyria. Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, assassinates him and succeeds him.

15.title: Jotham Reigns in Judah
15.context: Jotham reigns in Judah, does right and rebuilds the Upper Gate of the temple, while Aram and Israel begin to move against Judah.

16.title: Ahaz Reigns in Judah
16.context: Ahaz of Judah follows the kings of Israel, even sacrificing his son in fire; he buys Assyria’s help with temple treasures and has a copy of a Damascus altar installed in the temple.

17.title: Hoshea the Last King of Israel
17.context: When Hoshea rebels, Assyria besieges Samaria for three years, captures it and deports the Israelites; Scripture explains that this happened because Israel abandoned Yahweh for other gods and ignored the prophets’ warnings.

17.title: Samaria Resettled
17.context: Assyria resettles foreigners in Samaria, who worship Yahweh while also serving their own gods — the background to the later Samaritans.

18.title: Hezekiah Destroys Idolatry in Judah
18.context: Hezekiah of Judah trusts in Yahweh, removes the high places and even breaks up the bronze snake Moses made, which people had been worshiping; there was no king of Judah like him.

18.title: Sennacherib Invades Judah
18.context: Sennacherib of Assyria captures Judah’s fortified cities and sends his field commander to Jerusalem, who mocks Hezekiah’s trust in Yahweh in Hebrew before the people, saying no nation’s god has saved them.

19.title: Isaiah’s Message of Deliverance
19.context: Hezekiah puts on sackcloth, goes to Yahweh’s temple and sends to the prophet Isaiah, who tells him not to fear: Yahweh will send the Assyrian king home to die by the sword.

19.title: Sennacherib’s Blasphemous Letter
19.context: Sennacherib sends a threatening letter; Hezekiah spreads it before Yahweh in the temple and prays, confessing that Yahweh alone is God and asking him to save them so that all kingdoms may know it.

19.title: Sennacherib’s Fall Prophesied
19.context: Isaiah brings Yahweh’s answer that the king of Assyria will not enter the city; that night the angel of Yahweh strikes down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib returns to Nineveh, where his sons later kill him.

20.title: Hezekiah’s Illness and Recovery
20.context: Hezekiah falls mortally ill and prays with tears; Yahweh adds fifteen years to his life, confirming it by making the shadow go back ten steps.

20.title: Hezekiah Shows His Treasures
20.context: Envoys from Babylon visit, and Hezekiah shows them all his treasures; Isaiah foretells that everything will one day be carried off to Babylon.

20.title: Manasseh Succeeds Hezekiah
20.context: Hezekiah’s other deeds, including his might and how he made the pool and tunnel by which he brought water into the city, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah; he rests with his ancestors, and his son Manasseh succeeds him.

21.title: Manasseh Reigns in Judah
21.context: Manasseh reigns fifty-five years, rebuilding the high places, putting idols in the temple, sacrificing his son and practicing sorcery, doing more evil than the nations; Yahweh announces disaster on Jerusalem.

21.title: Amon Reigns in Judah
21.context: Amon follows his father’s evil ways and is assassinated after two years; the people make his son Josiah king.

22.title: Josiah Reigns in Judah
22.context: Josiah is eight years old when he becomes king and reigns thirty-one years in Jerusalem; he does what is right in Yahweh’s eyes and walks in the ways of his father David, not turning aside to the right or to the left.

22.title: Funding the Temple Repairs
22.context: While the temple is being repaired, the high priest Hilkiah finds the Book of the Law; hearing it, Josiah tears his robes and consults the prophetess Huldah, who says disaster will come, but not in his lifetime, because his heart was responsive.

23.title: Josiah Renews the Covenant
23.context: Josiah reads the Book of the Covenant to all the people and renews the covenant before Yahweh, then purges the land of idols, high places and idolatrous priests, even destroying the altar at Bethel as a man of God had foretold.

23.title: Josiah Restores the Passover
23.context: The king commands all the people to celebrate the Passover to Yahweh their God as it is written in the Book of the Covenant; such a Passover had not been observed since the days of the judges who led Israel, nor throughout the days of the kings of Israel and Judah, and it is celebrated in the eighteenth year of Josiah.

23.title: Josiah's Other Reforms
23.context: Josiah also removes mediums and every detestable thing, keeping the law wholeheartedly — no king before or after was like him; yet because of Manasseh’s sins Yahweh’s anger against Judah does not turn away.

23.title: The Death of Josiah
23.context: Pharaoh Necho marches north, and Josiah goes out to meet him and is killed at Megiddo; the people make his son Jehoahaz king.

23.title: Jehoahaz Succeeds Josiah
23.context: Jehoahaz reigns three months before Pharaoh Necho deposes him and takes him to Egypt, installing Jehoiakim and imposing heavy tribute.

23.title: Jehoiakim Reigns in Judah
23.context: Jehoiakim taxes the people to pay Egypt and does evil; when Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon rises, Jehoiakim submits and then rebels, and Yahweh sends raiders against Judah.

24.title: Jehoiachin Reigns in Judah
24.context: Jehoiachin reigns three months; Babylon besieges Jerusalem, he surrenders, and Nebuchadnezzar deports the royal family, officials, fighting men and craftsmen — ten thousand in all — and carries off the temple treasures.

24.title: Zedekiah Reigns in Judah
24.context: Zedekiah is twenty-one when he becomes king and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in Yahweh’s sight, as Jehoiakim had done; it is because of Yahweh’s anger that all this happens to Jerusalem and Judah, and in the end he drives them from his presence. And Zedekiah rebels against the king of Babylon.

25.title: Nebuchadnezzar Besieges Jerusalem
25.context: Zedekiah rebels, Jerusalem is besieged for about two years until the wall is breached, and Zedekiah is captured, sees his sons killed, and is blinded and taken to Babylon.

25.title: The Temple Destroyed
25.context: The Babylonian commander burns Yahweh’s temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem, tears down the walls, and breaks up the bronze furnishings to carry to Babylon.

25.title: Captives Carried to Babylon
25.context: The chief priests and leading men are taken to Riblah and executed; so Judah goes into exile from its land.

25.title: Gedaliah Governs in Judah
25.context: Babylon appoints Gedaliah governor over those left; soon Ishmael of the royal line assassinates him, and the people flee to Egypt for fear of Babylon.

25.title: Jehoiachin Released from Prison
25.context: In the thirty-seventh year of his exile, a new Babylonian king releases Jehoiachin from prison and seats him at the king’s table for life — the kingdom has fallen, but David’s line survives.

1.title: From Adam to Abraham
1.context: Chronicles opens with genealogy: from Adam through Seth and Noah to the descendants of Shem, Ham and Japheth and the nations that spread from them, and down Shem’s line to Abraham.

1.title: The Descendants of Abraham
1.context: Abraham’s sons Isaac and Ishmael, followed by the descendants of Ishmael and of Keturah.

1.title: The Descendants of Esau
1.context: Isaac’s sons Esau and Israel (Jacob), and then Esau’s descendants.

1.title: The Descendants of Seir
1.context: The sons and descendants of Seir the Horite, the clan chiefs who lived in the land of Edom.

1.title: The Kings of Edom
1.context: The kings who reigned in Edom before any Israelite king — Bela, Jobab, Husham and others — and the chiefs of Edom.

2.title: The Sons of Israel
2.context: The twelve sons of Israel, followed by a close look at Judah’s descendants, which is the main focus of the genealogies.

2.title: David's Genealogy
2.context: The sons of Hezron — Ram, Caleb and Jerahmeel — and the line from Ram through Boaz and Jesse to David and his siblings.

2.title: The Descendants of Hezron
2.context: The descendants of Caleb son of Hezron, including the ancestors of the craftsman Bezalel.

2.title: The Descendants of Jerahmeel
2.context: The descendants of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron.

2.title: The Rest of Caleb's Descendants
2.context: More descendants of Caleb, the founders of places such as Ziph, Hebron and Maon.

3.title: The Descendants of David
3.context: The sons born to David in Hebron and in Jerusalem, among them Solomon, and his daughter Tamar.

3.title: The Descendants of Solomon
3.context: Solomon’s descendants, from Rehoboam through the later kings of Judah.

3.title: The Royal Line After the Exile
3.context: The descendants of Jehoiachin in exile, including Zerubbabel and his sons.

4.title: The Descendants of Judah
4.context: More of Judah’s descendants, including the clans of Zorah and other well-known families.

4.title: More Descendants of Judah
4.context: More families of Judah, including the families of Kelub, Kenaz and Othniel.

4.title: The Descendants of Shelah
4.context: The descendants of Shelah son of Judah, including the linen workers and the potters.

4.title: The Descendants of Simeon
4.context: The descendants of Simeon, who lived in the Beersheba region until David’s time.

5.title: The Descendants of Reuben
5.context: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father’s bed the rights of the firstborn passed to Joseph’s sons; his descendants are listed.

5.title: The Descendants of Gad
5.context: The Gadites lived next to the Reubenites in Bashan, as far as Salecah, and their leaders are listed.

5.title: The Armies of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh
5.context: The eastern tribes field 44,760 fighting men; they cry out to God in battle, and he answers them because they trust him, so that they defeat the Hagrites.

5.title: The Half-Tribe of Manasseh
5.context: The half-tribe of Manasseh settles from Bashan toward Mount Hermon and grows numerous; their heads of families are named.

5.title: The Two and a Half Tribes Rebel against God
5.context: The two and a half tribes break faith with the God of their ancestors and prostitute themselves to the gods of the land; God stirs up the king of Assyria, who carries them into exile.

6.title: The Descendants of Levi
6.context: The sons of Levi — Gershon, Kohath and Merari — and the line of Kohath that leads to Aaron, Moses and Miriam.

6.title: The Rest of Levi's Descendants
6.context: The descendants of Levi’s three sons are set out family by family.

6.title: The Temple Musicians
6.context: The singers David puts in charge of music in the house of Yahweh after the ark finds rest: Heman, Asaph and Ethan, who minister before the tabernacle in order.

6.title: The Descendants of Aaron
6.context: Aaron’s descendants serve as priests, offering sacrifices and incense and making atonement for Israel; the line of Zadok follows.

6.title: Territories for the Levites
6.context: The towns and pasturelands that the Levite clans received within the other tribes’ territories.

7.title: The Descendants of Issachar
7.context: The sons of Issachar — Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron — whose descendants number many thousands of warriors.

7.title: The Descendants of Benjamin
7.context: Several lines of Benjamin’s descendants, many of them mighty warriors.

7.title: The Descendants of Naphtali
7.context: The sons of Naphtali, who were Bilhah’s grandsons.

7.title: The Descendants of Manasseh
7.context: The descendants of Manasseh, including Makir and Zelophehad with his daughters.

7.title: The Descendants of Ephraim
7.context: The descendants of Ephraim, including Joshua son of Nun, and their towns around Bethel and Gezer.

7.title: The Descendants of Asher
7.context: The descendants of Asher, who are warriors and chiefs, numbering 26,000 men ready for battle.

8.title: Genealogy from Benjamin to Saul
8.context: The genealogy of Benjamin’s sons, down to Saul’s family.

8.title: The Benjamites at Aijalon
8.context: The Benjamite heads of families in Aijalon, who drove out the inhabitants of Gath.

8.title: The Benjamites in Jerusalem
8.context: Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem, with their family heads.

8.title: The Benjamites in Gibeon and Jerusalem
8.context: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived there, and his descendants also lived in Jerusalem, including Ner, who fathered Kish.

8.title: The Family of Saul
8.context: Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul, who had sons Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab and Esh-Baal; Jonathan’s line is traced.

9.title: The People of Jerusalem
9.context: All Israel was listed in the genealogies written in the book of the kings; Judah was taken captive to Babylon for unfaithfulness. The first to resettle their own towns were Israelites, priests, Levites and temple servants, and some from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.

9.title: The Priests Living in Jerusalem
9.context: The priests who lived in Jerusalem — Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jakin and the chief officer of the house of God.

9.title: The Levites Living in Jerusalem
9.context: The Levites living in Jerusalem, such as Shemaiah and Mattaniah of Asaph’s line.

9.title: The Gatekeepers of the Temple
9.context: The gatekeepers — Shallum, Akkub, Talmon and Ahiman — who guard the King’s Gate on the east and the entrances of the tent; their duties were set by David and Samuel the seer.

9.title: The Remaining Levites
9.context: Other Levites are in charge of the temple articles, flour, wine, oil, incense and spices; some of the priests prepare the spices, and gatekeepers and singers remain at their posts day and night.

9.title: The Descendants of Saul
9.context: The family of Jeiel of Gibeon, and the line from Ner to Saul and Jonathan again.

10.title: Saul’s Overthrow and Death
10.context: Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa (compare 1 Samuel 31); the Chronicler explains that he died for his unfaithfulness to Yahweh and for consulting a medium, so Yahweh turned the kingdom over to David.

11.title: David Anointed King of All Israel
11.context: All Israel gathers at Hebron and anoints David king, in keeping with the word of Yahweh through Samuel; David and his men capture the Jebusite stronghold of Zion, the City of David, and Joab leads the assault and becomes commander. David grows steadily more powerful, because Yahweh Almighty is with him.

11.title: David’s Mighty Men
11.context: David’s chief warriors, who along with all Israel supported his kingship as Yahweh promised — Jashobeam, Eleazar, Abishai, Benaiah and others; when three of them break through the Philistine lines for water from Bethlehem’s well, David will not drink it but pours it out before Yahweh.

12.title: The Mighty Men Join David at Ziklag
12.context: Skilled archers and slingers from Benjamin, Saul’s own tribe, come to David at Ziklag while he is still banned from Saul’s presence; they can shoot arrows or sling stones with either hand.

12.title: The Gadites Who Followed David
12.context: Some Gadites come over to David in the wilderness stronghold: brave warriors, trained for battle, whose faces are like lions and who are as swift as gazelles on the mountains.

12.title: The Benjamites and Judahites Who Followed David
12.context: Men from Benjamin and Judah also join David at the stronghold; the Spirit comes on Amasai, who declares peace and success to David, for his God helps him.

12.title: The Manassites Who Followed David
12.context: Some of Manasseh’s men defect to David when he goes with the Philistines to fight Saul, though in the end the Philistine rulers send him back; as he returns to Ziklag, more Manassite leaders join him and help him against raiding bands.

12.title: David’s Army Grows at Hebron
12.context: The number of armed men from each tribe who come to David at Hebron to turn Saul’s kingdom over to him, as Yahweh had said, is recorded; all these fighting men come to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel, and for three days they celebrate with food prepared by their relatives.

13.title: David Fetches the Ark
13.context: David consults his officers and all Israel about bringing the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim, and they carry it on a new cart; when the oxen stumble, Uzzah reaches out to steady the ark and God strikes him down. David is afraid of God and leaves the ark with Obed-Edom, whose household Yahweh blesses for three months.

14.title: David’s Family Grows
14.context: Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to build David a palace; David takes more wives in Jerusalem and has more children, and knows that Yahweh has established him as king over Israel and exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people.

14.title: Two Victories over the Philistines
14.context: Twice the Philistines attack, and each time David inquires of God and wins by following his direction, so that David’s fame spreads to every land.

15.title: Preparing to Move the Ark
15.context: David prepares a place for the ark and commands that only the Levites carry it, consecrating themselves and moving it as the law prescribes.

15.title: Moving the Ark to Jerusalem
15.context: David and the elders joyfully bring the ark into the City of David with Levite musicians playing; Michal watches David dancing from a window and despises him.

16.title: David’s Psalm of Thanksgiving
16.context: David appoints Asaph and his associates to give thanks before the ark and gives them a psalm of thanks (drawn from Psalms 105, 96 and 106) calling all nations to declare Yahweh’s deeds.

16.title: Worship before the Ark
16.context: David arranges for Asaph and others to minister regularly before the ark, and for Zadok and the priests to offer the daily burnt offerings at the tabernacle in Gibeon.

17.title: God’s Covenant with David
17.context: David wants to build a house for the ark; through Nathan Yahweh promises instead to build a house for David — a descendant will build the temple, his throne will be established forever, and Yahweh will be his father and he Yahweh’s son (compare 2 Samuel 7).

17.title: David’s Prayer of Thanksgiving
17.context: David thanks Yahweh in humility, confessing his unworthiness and praising him as the only God, and asks him to confirm his promise to David’s house forever.

18.title: David’s Triumphs
18.context: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Hadadezer king of Zobah and the Arameans of Damascus; he takes great quantities of bronze, gold and silver, and dedicates all of it to Yahweh. Yahweh gives David victory wherever he goes, and he reigns over all Israel, doing what is just and right for all his people.

19.title: David’s Messengers Disgraced
19.context: David’s envoys are humiliated by the Ammonite king; the Ammonites hire Aramean forces, and Joab and David defeat them (compare 2 Samuel 10).

20.title: The Capture of Rabbah
20.context: In the spring, when kings go off to war, Joab leads out the army and besieges Rabbah while David stays in Jerusalem; Joab attacks and destroys Rabbah, and David takes the crown from their king’s head — it weighs a talent of gold and is set with precious stones — and carries off a great quantity of plunder.

20.title: Battles against the Philistines
20.context: Later there are battles with the Philistines at Gezer, where Sibbekai kills Sippai, one of the descendants of the Rephaites, and Elhanan kills Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite; in another battle at Gath, Jonathan, David’s nephew, kills a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.

21.title: David’s Military Census
21.context: Satan incites David to count Israel despite Joab’s objection; God is displeased and sends a plague; David confesses, builds an altar on Ornan’s threshing floor, and Yahweh answers with fire from heaven and stops the plague — the site later chosen for the temple.

22.title: Preparations for the Temple
22.context: David gathers vast materials for the temple and charges Solomon: Yahweh did not let David build it because he had shed much blood, but promised a son, a man of peace, who would; he urges Solomon to be strong and keep the law, and tells the leaders to help him.

23.title: The Divisions of the Levites
23.context: David counts the Levites and assigns their duties — supervising the temple work, serving as officials and judges, guarding the gates and leading praise with instruments — to assist Aaron’s descendants and give thanks morning and evening.

24.title: Twenty-Four Divisions of Priests
24.context: David, with Zadok and Ahimelech, divides Aaron’s descendants into twenty-four divisions for their service, sixteen from Eleazar’s line and eight from Ithamar’s, by casting lots in the presence of the king and officials.

24.title: The Rest of the Levites
24.context: The heads of the remaining Levite families are listed, and lots are cast for their duties just as for the descendants of Aaron, without distinction between the head of a family and his younger brother.

25.title: Twenty-Four Divisions of Musicians
25.context: David and the army commanders set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for the ministry of prophesying with harps, lyres and cymbals; the number of those trained and skilled in music for Yahweh is 288, and lots are cast for twenty-four divisions of twelve each.

26.title: The Divisions of the Gatekeepers
26.context: The divisions of the gatekeepers, from the Korahites, the family of Meshelemiah, and the family of Obed-Edom, whom God had blessed with many sons; they cast lots, family by family, for the gates, small and great alike, and are capable men with strength for the service.

26.title: The Treasurers, Officers, and Judges
26.context: Other Levites are put in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and of the dedicated things; still others are appointed as officials and judges, in charge of the external affairs of Israel and of everything concerning Yahweh and the king in the regions west of the Jordan.

26.title: The Duties of the Other Levites
26.context: Some Levites are assigned duties away from the temple as officials and judges, handling the affairs of Yahweh and the king on both sides of the Jordan.

27.title: Twelve Captains for Twelve Months
27.context: The army of Israel is organized in twelve divisions of 24,000 men each, serving the king one month at a time; each of twelve commanders, beginning with Jashobeam for the first month, takes a turn.

27.title: The Leaders of the Twelve Tribes
27.context: The leaders of Israel’s tribes are listed; David did not count those under twenty, since Yahweh had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars, and Joab’s census was never finished or recorded.

27.title: David’s Various Overseers
27.context: Officials are named for the royal storehouses, for the farmers, for the vineyards, for the olive and sycamore-fig trees, for the herds, camels, donkeys and flocks.

27.title: The Counselors
27.context: David’s uncle Jonathan, a man of insight and a scribe, serves as counselor along with Jehiel son of Hakmoni, who looks after the king’s sons; Ahithophel is the king’s counselor and Hushai the Arkite is the king’s friend, followed by Jehoiada and Abiathar, and Joab is commander of the royal army.

28.title: David Commissions Solomon
28.context: David assembles Israel’s leaders and announces that Yahweh has chosen Solomon to sit on the throne of Yahweh’s kingdom; he charges Solomon to serve God wholeheartedly and gives him the temple plans the Spirit had put in his mind.

29.title: Offerings for the Temple
29.context: David gives his own gold and silver for the temple, and the leaders and people follow with willing offerings, rejoicing together.

29.title: David’s Prayer of Blessing
29.context: David praises Yahweh before the assembly: greatness, power and glory belong to him, everything comes from him, and what they give is only from his hand; Solomon is then acknowledged king a second time.

29.title: David’s Reign and Death
29.context: David reigns forty years over Israel and dies at a good old age, full of riches and honor, and Solomon succeeds him; his acts are recorded in the writings of Samuel, Nathan and Gad.

1.title: Solomon’s Prayer for Wisdom
1.context: At Gibeon God invites Solomon to ask for anything, and he asks for wisdom and knowledge to lead the people; God grants it and adds wealth and honor (compare 1 Kings 3).

1.title: Solomon’s Riches
1.context: Solomon accumulates chariots and horses, stationing them in the chariot cities and in Jerusalem; the king makes silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and imports horses from Egypt and Kue.

2.title: Preparations for the Temple
2.context: Solomon decides to build a temple for the Name of Yahweh and a palace for himself, and conscripts 70,000 carriers, 80,000 stonecutters and 3,600 supervisors; he asks Hiram king of Tyre for cedar and a skilled craftsman, saying the temple must be great because “our God is greater than all other gods.”

2.title: The Temple Work Begins
2.context: Solomon counts all the foreigners living in Israel — 153,600 — and assigns 70,000 to carry loads, 80,000 to quarry stone in the hills and 3,600 as foremen to see that the people work.

3.title: The Veil and Pillars
3.context: In front of the temple Solomon sets up two pillars thirty-five cubits high, with capitals of five cubits, chains and pomegranates, naming the one on the south Jakin and the one on the north Boaz; he also makes the veil of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it.

4.title: The Bronze Altar and Molten Sea
4.context: Solomon makes a bronze altar twenty cubits square and ten high, the Sea of cast metal resting on twelve bulls, ten basins for washing the burnt offerings, ten gold lampstands, ten tables and a hundred gold sprinkling bowls, and builds the priests’ courtyard and the great courtyard with its doors overlaid with bronze.

5.title: The Ark Enters the Temple
5.context: At the Festival of Tabernacles Solomon brings the ark from the City of David into the temple and places it under the cherubim in the Most Holy Place; it holds only the two tablets.

5.title: The Glory of God
5.context: As the priests and Levite singers praise Yahweh with one voice — he is good, his love endures forever — the temple is filled with a cloud, and the priests cannot continue ministering.

6.title: Solomon Blesses Yahweh
6.context: Solomon praises Yahweh for keeping his promise to David by choosing Jerusalem and having David’s son build the temple for his name.

6.title: Solomon’s Prayer of Dedication
6.context: Kneeling on a bronze platform with hands raised, Solomon confesses that even the highest heaven cannot contain Yahweh, and asks him to hear from heaven and forgive whenever his people, or foreigners, pray toward this house in any trouble.

7.title: Fire from Heaven
7.context: When Solomon finishes praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the sacrifices, and Yahweh’s glory fills the temple; all the people bow down and give thanks that he is good and his love endures forever.

7.title: Yahweh’s Response to Solomon
7.context: Yahweh appears to Solomon at night and promises that if his people humble themselves, pray, seek his face and turn from their wicked ways, he will hear from heaven, forgive their sin and heal their land; but if they forsake him, they will be uprooted.

8.title: Solomon’s Additional Achievements
8.context: Solomon builds towns and store cities, keeps the festivals and offerings as Moses commanded, organizes the priests and Levites as David ordered, and sends ships to Ophir for gold.

9.title: The Queen of Sheba
9.context: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and, seeing his wisdom and splendor, praises Yahweh for making him king out of love for Israel (compare 1 Kings 10).

9.title: Solomon’s Wealth and Splendor
9.context: Solomon’s wealth surpasses all the kings of the earth — gold shields, an ivory throne, vessels of gold — and rulers come from everywhere to hear the wisdom God gave him.

9.title: The Death of Solomon
9.context: The other events of Solomon’s reign, from beginning to end, are written in the records of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite and the visions of Iddo the seer; Solomon reigns over all Israel in Jerusalem forty years, then rests with his ancestors, and his son Rehoboam succeeds him.

10.title: Rebellion against Rehoboam
10.context: Rehoboam refuses to lighten the people’s burden, and the northern tribes break away from David’s house, leaving him only Judah and Benjamin (compare 1 Kings 12).

11.title: Shemaiah’s Prophecy
11.context: Rehoboam musters an army to reclaim Israel, but the prophet Shemaiah brings Yahweh’s word not to fight their brothers, and they obey and go home.

11.title: Rehoboam Fortifies Judah
11.context: Rehoboam lives in Jerusalem and builds up towns for defense in Judah — Bethlehem, Tekoa, Hebron, Lachish and others — fortifying them and putting commanders in them with supplies of food, olive oil and wine, shields and spears; Judah and Benjamin belong to him.

11.title: Jeroboam Forsakes the Priests and Levites
11.context: Priests, Levites and all who sincerely seek Yahweh leave the north for Judah and Jerusalem because Jeroboam has set up calf idols and his own priests, strengthening Judah for three years.

11.title: Rehoboam’s Family
11.context: Rehoboam has many wives and children; he makes Abijah crown prince and wisely disperses his other sons among the fortified cities.

12.title: Shishak Raids Jerusalem
12.context: Once secure, Rehoboam abandons Yahweh’s law, and Shishak of Egypt invades; when the prophet Shemaiah says Yahweh has abandoned them, the king and leaders humble themselves, so Yahweh spares them from destruction, though the temple treasures are taken.

12.title: Rehoboam’s Reign and Death
12.context: Rehoboam reigns seventeen years and does evil because he did not set his heart on seeking Yahweh; there is continual war between him and Jeroboam.

13.title: Abijah Reigns in Judah
13.context: Abijah of Judah faces Jeroboam in battle, declaring from a hilltop that Judah has kept Yahweh and his lawful priests; when surrounded, Judah cries out to Yahweh, and God routs Israel because Judah relied on him.

14.title: Asa Reigns in Judah
14.context: Asa does what is good in Yahweh’s eyes, removing foreign altars and idols, and the land has peace; when a huge Cushite army invades, Asa prays in reliance on Yahweh, and Yahweh routs the Cushites.

15.title: The Prophecy of Azariah
15.context: The prophet Azariah tells Asa that if they seek Yahweh he will be found, but if they forsake him he will forsake them; Asa removes the idols, leads the people in a covenant to seek Yahweh wholeheartedly, and even deposes his idolatrous grandmother.

16.title: War between Asa and Baasha
16.context: When Baasha of Israel fortifies Ramah against Judah, Asa bribes the king of Aram with temple silver and gold to attack Israel, and Baasha abandons the work.

16.title: Hanani’s Message to Asa
16.context: The seer Hanani rebukes Asa for relying on Aram instead of Yahweh, whose eyes range over the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully his; Asa angrily throws the seer into prison.

16.title: The Death and Burial of Asa
16.context: In old age Asa suffers a severe foot disease but seeks help only from physicians, not from Yahweh; he dies and is buried in the City of David.

17.title: Jehoshaphat Reigns in Judah
17.context: Jehoshaphat follows David’s early ways, seeking God rather than the Baals; Yahweh establishes his kingdom, he gains great wealth and honor, and he removes the high places and Asherah poles.

17.title: Jehoshaphat's Achievements
17.context: Jehoshaphat sends officials, Levites and priests through Judah’s towns to teach the people from the Book of the Law, and the fear of Yahweh keeps the surrounding nations from attacking.

18.title: Jehoshaphat Allies with Ahab
18.context: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab by marriage and joins his attack on Ramoth Gilead; the prophets promise victory, but Micaiah foretells Ahab’s defeat and is imprisoned (compare 1 Kings 22).

18.title: Ahab’s Defeat and Death
18.context: Ahab goes into battle disguised but is killed by an arrow; when Jehoshaphat is surrounded, he cries out and God draws the enemy away from him.

19.title: Jehoshaphat Reproved by Jehu
19.context: The seer Jehu rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the wicked and loving those who hate Yahweh, though he commends him for removing the Asherah poles and setting his heart on seeking God.

19.title: Jehoshaphat’s Reforms
19.context: Jehoshaphat travels through the land bringing the people back to Yahweh and appoints judges in every town, charging them that they judge for Yahweh, without partiality or bribes, in the fear of Yahweh.

20.title: War against Jehoshaphat
20.context: When a vast coalition including Moab and Ammon invades, Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast and prays in the temple that they do not know what to do but their eyes are on Yahweh; through a Levite Yahweh says the battle is his; they march out singing praise, the enemies destroy each other, and Judah returns with great plunder.

20.title: Summary of Jehoshaphat’s Reign
20.context: Jehoshaphat reigns twenty-five years and does right, though the high places remain; when he joins Israel’s king in a shipping venture, a prophet foretells its failure, and the ships are wrecked.

21.title: Jehoram Reigns in Judah
21.context: Jehoram kills his brothers when he becomes king and follows Ahab’s ways; Edom revolts, Elijah writes to warn of a terrible disease, and Jehoram dies of it with no one regretting his death.

22.title: Ahaziah Reigns in Judah
22.context: Ahaziah reigns one year under the influence of his mother Athaliah and Ahab’s family, and is killed by Jehu while visiting Joram of Israel.

22.title: Athaliah and Joash
22.context: Athaliah destroys the royal family and seizes the throne, but the infant Joash is hidden in the temple for six years by his aunt Jehosheba.

23.title: Joash Anointed King of Judah
23.context: In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada makes a covenant with the commanders and Levites, and Joash is crowned and anointed in the temple amid shouts of acclamation.

23.title: Jehoiada Restores the Worship of Yahweh
23.context: Athaliah is executed; Jehoiada leads king and people in a covenant to be Yahweh’s people, the temple of Baal is torn down, temple worship is restored, and the city is at peace.

24.title: Joash Repairs the Temple
24.context: While Jehoiada lives, Joash does right and restores the temple with money the people bring gladly.

24.title: Jehoiada’s Death and Burial
24.context: Jehoiada grows old and full of years and dies at the age of 130, and he is buried with the kings in the City of David, because of the good he had done in Israel for God and his temple.

24.title: The Death of Joash
24.context: After Jehoiada’s death, Joash follows the officials into idolatry and has the prophet Zechariah, Jehoiada’s son, stoned for rebuking them; soon Aram invades and Joash is killed by his own servants.

25.title: Amaziah Reigns in Judah
25.context: Amaziah does right but not wholeheartedly; following the law of Moses, he executes his father’s assassins but not their children.

25.title: Amaziah’s Victories
25.context: Following a man of God, Amaziah sends home the Israelite mercenaries and defeats Edom, but then worships the Edomite gods he brought back, and a prophet warns that God has determined to destroy him.

25.title: Jehoash Defeats Amaziah
25.context: Ignoring warnings, Amaziah challenges Israel’s king and is defeated at Beth Shemesh; Jerusalem’s wall is breached and its treasures plundered.

26.title: Uzziah Reigns in Judah
26.context: Uzziah becomes king at sixteen and seeks God under Zechariah’s instruction, and God gives him success — victories, building, cisterns and a strong army — and his fame spreads.

26.title: Uzziah Punished for His Pride
26.context: Grown powerful, Uzziah becomes proud and enters the temple to burn incense; when the priests confront him and he rages, leprosy breaks out on his forehead, and he lives in isolation until his death.

27.title: Jotham Reigns in Judah
27.context: Jotham does right in Yahweh’s eyes, builds up the temple gate and towns and defeats the Ammonites; he grows powerful because he walks steadily before Yahweh.

28.title: Ahaz Reigns in Judah
28.context: Ahaz follows the kings of Israel, making idols for the Baals, burning his children in the Valley of Ben Hinnom and sacrificing at the high places.

28.title: Aram Defeats Judah
28.context: Yahweh gives Ahaz into the hands of Aram and Israel; Judah suffers heavy losses and 200,000 are taken captive to Samaria.

28.title: The Prophet Oded
28.context: The prophet Oded warns the returning Israelite army not to enslave their fellow Judeans, and Ephraim’s leaders clothe and feed the captives and escort them back to Jericho.

28.title: The Idolatry of Ahaz
28.context: When Edom and the Philistines raid Judah, Ahaz appeals to Assyria, which only troubles him further; Yahweh humbles Judah because of Ahaz’s unfaithfulness.

28.title: Ahaz's Sins
28.context: In his distress Ahaz becomes even more unfaithful, sacrificing to the gods of Damascus, shutting the doors of Yahweh’s temple and setting up altars all over Jerusalem.

29.title: Hezekiah Cleanses the Temple
29.context: In the first year of his reign Hezekiah reopens the temple doors and calls the priests and Levites to cleanse it, resolving to make a covenant with Yahweh so that his anger will turn away.

29.title: Cleansing the Temple
29.context: The priests and Levites take sixteen days to purify the temple and restore the articles Ahaz had discarded.

29.title: Hezekiah Restores Temple Worship
29.context: Hezekiah leads the people in sin offerings and burnt offerings while the Levites play and sing as David prescribed; the whole assembly worships, temple worship is restored, and all rejoice.

30.title: Hezekiah Proclaims a Passover
30.context: Hezekiah sends couriers throughout Israel and Judah inviting everyone to Jerusalem to keep the Passover; many in the north scoff, but some humble themselves and come.

30.title: Hezekiah Celebrates the Passover
30.context: A great crowd keeps the Passover in the second month and removes the altars in Jerusalem; some eat without being properly purified, Hezekiah prays for them, and Yahweh heals the people.

30.title: Keeping the Feast Again
30.context: The assembly agrees to celebrate seven more days, and there is joy in Jerusalem unmatched since Solomon; the priests bless the people, and their prayer reaches heaven.

31.title: The Destruction of Idols
31.context: After the festival the people destroy idols and high places across the land; Hezekiah restores the divisions of priests and Levites, and the people bring firstfruits and tithes so generously that they are piled in heaps.

32.title: Sennacherib Invades Judah
32.context: When Sennacherib invades, Hezekiah blocks the water sources, strengthens the walls and encourages the people that the one with them is greater than the one with Assyria; the Assyrians mock Yahweh, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and Yahweh sends an angel who destroys the Assyrian army.

32.title: Hezekiah’s Illness and Recovery
32.context: Hezekiah is healed after prayer but does not respond with gratitude and grows proud; when he later humbles himself, Yahweh’s wrath does not come in his days.

32.title: Hezekiah's Wealth and Honor
32.context: Hezekiah enjoys great wealth and honor and channels the Gihon spring into the City of David; when Babylonian envoys come, God leaves him to test what is in his heart.

32.title: Hezekiah’s Death
32.context: Hezekiah’s acts are recorded in the vision of Isaiah the prophet; he dies honored by all Judah and Jerusalem, and his son Manasseh succeeds him.

33.title: Manasseh Reigns in Judah
33.context: Manasseh reigns fifty-five years, rebuilding high places, setting idols in the temple, sacrificing his children and practicing sorcery, leading Judah into worse evil than the nations; Yahweh warns them, but they do not listen.

33.title: Manasseh’s Repentance and Restoration
33.context: The Assyrians take Manasseh captive to Babylon with hooks; in distress he humbles himself greatly and prays, Yahweh hears him and restores him to his kingdom, and Manasseh then knows that Yahweh is God, removing the idols and restoring Yahweh’s worship.

33.title: Manasseh's Death
33.context: Manasseh’s prayer and God’s answer are recorded in the annals; he dies and is buried in his palace grounds.

33.title: Amon Reigns in Judah
33.context: Amon follows his father’s early evil but, unlike him, never humbles himself, adding to his guilt; after two years he is assassinated, and the people make Josiah king.

34.title: Josiah Reigns in Judah
34.context: Josiah becomes king at eight, begins to seek God at sixteen, and at twenty starts purging idols from Judah, Jerusalem and even the northern territories.

34.title: Josiah Destroys Idolatry
34.context: In his eighth year Josiah begins to seek the God of David, and in his twelfth he purges Judah and Jerusalem of high places, Asherah poles and idols.

34.title: Josiah Repairs the Temple
34.context: While the temple is being repaired, Hilkiah finds the Book of the Law; Josiah tears his robes on hearing it, and the prophetess Huldah says disaster will come, but not in his lifetime, because he humbled himself.

34.title: Josiah Renews the Covenant
34.context: Josiah reads the Book of the Covenant to all the people and renews the covenant before Yahweh, leading everyone to serve Yahweh, and as long as he lives they do not turn away from him.

35.title: Josiah Restores the Passover
35.context: Josiah celebrates the Passover in Jerusalem, organized by priests and Levites according to David’s and Solomon’s directions; no Passover like it had been kept since the days of Samuel.

35.title: The Death of Josiah
35.context: Pharaoh Necho marches north, and Josiah, ignoring Necho’s warning, goes out to fight and is struck by archers at Megiddo; all Judah mourns him, and Jeremiah composes laments for him.

36.title: Jehoahaz Succeeds Josiah
36.context: Jehoahaz reigns three months before Pharaoh deposes him and takes him to Egypt.

36.title: Jehoiakim Reigns in Judah
36.context: Jehoiakim does evil; Nebuchadnezzar attacks, binds him in chains and carries temple articles to Babylon.

36.title: Jehoiachin Reigns in Judah
36.context: Jehoiachin reigns three months and ten days before being taken to Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar makes Zedekiah king.

36.title: Zedekiah Reigns in Judah
36.context: Zedekiah does evil, refuses to humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah and rebels against Babylon, while priests and people follow the detestable practices of the nations and defile Yahweh’s temple.

36.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
36.context: Out of compassion Yahweh sends messengers again and again, but the people mock them, until the Babylonians capture Jerusalem, burn the temple, break down the walls and take the survivors into exile, and the land enjoys its Sabbath rest for seventy years, as Jeremiah had said.

36.title: The Proclamation of Cyrus
36.context: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, Yahweh moves him to decree that the Jews may go up to rebuild Yahweh’s temple in Jerusalem — Chronicles ends on this note of hope.

1.title: The Proclamation of Cyrus
1.context: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, Yahweh moves the king’s heart to decree that the Jews may return to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple, and Cyrus returns the temple articles Nebuchadnezzar had carried off.

2.title: The List of Returning Exiles
2.context: The exiles who return to Jerusalem and Judah under Zerubbabel, Jeshua and others are listed by family, about 42,360 people in all, with their servants and animals.

3.title: Sacrifices Restored
3.context: In the seventh month the people gather in Jerusalem, and Jeshua and Zerubbabel rebuild the altar of the God of Israel on its foundation and offer burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses; they also keep the Festival of Tabernacles.

3.title: Temple Restoration Begins
3.context: In the second month of the second year the temple work begins; when the builders lay the foundation, the people praise Yahweh with trumpets and cymbals, while many of the older priests and Levites who had seen the first temple weep aloud, so that no one can tell the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping.

4.title: Adversaries Hinder the Work
4.context: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin offer to help build, Zerubbabel and the leaders refuse; the people of the land then discourage the builders and frighten them, and hire counselors to frustrate their plans throughout the reigns of Cyrus and into Darius’s time.

4.title: Opposition under Xerxes and Artaxerxes
4.context: Under Xerxes and then Artaxerxes, the adversaries write accusations against the people of Judah and Jerusalem; Artaxerxes orders the rebuilding of the city stopped, and the work is halted by force.

4.title: The Temple Rebuilding Resumes
4.context: In the second year of Darius, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua begin again to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem, with the prophets of God supporting them.

6.title: The Decree of Darius
6.context: Darius orders a search of the archives, and in Ecbatana a scroll is found with Cyrus’s decree: the temple is to be rebuilt, its cost paid from the royal treasury, and its gold and silver articles returned.

6.title: King Darius Orders the Work to Continue
