6.context: King Darius orders the officials not to interfere, to pay the building costs and supply the sacrifices from the royal treasury, and to punish anyone who defies the decree.

6.title: The Temple Completed
6.context: Tattenai and his associates carry out the king’s order diligently, and the Jewish elders continue to build and prosper under the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah; the temple is finished on the third day of Adar in the sixth year of Darius.

6.title: The Returned Exiles Keep the Passover
6.context: The priests, Levites and other returned exiles joyfully dedicate the house of God with sacrifices; on the fourteenth day of the first month they celebrate the Passover, and for seven days they celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread with joy, because Yahweh has filled them with joy.

7.title: Ezra Arrives in Jerusalem
7.context: In the reign of Artaxerxes, Ezra, a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, comes from Babylon to Jerusalem; he has set his heart to study, practice and teach Yahweh’s law, and the hand of Yahweh is on him.

7.title: Artaxerxes’ Letter for Ezra
7.context: Artaxerxes gives Ezra a decree allowing any willing Israelites to go with him, providing silver, gold and sacrifices, and authorizing him to appoint magistrates and teach the law of his God.

7.title: Ezra Blesses God
7.context: Ezra praises Yahweh, the God of his ancestors, who put it into the king’s heart to bring honor to the house of Yahweh in Jerusalem; because the hand of Yahweh his God is on him, Ezra takes courage and gathers leaders from Israel to go up with him.

8.title: The Exiles Who Returned with Ezra
8.context: The heads of families who go up with Ezra from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes are listed by clan, about 1,500 men in all.

8.title: Ezra Sends for the Levites
8.context: Ezra assembles the people at the canal that flows toward Ahava and camps there three days; finding no Levites among them, he sends leaders to Iddo at Casiphia, and because the gracious hand of their God is on them, they bring 38 Levites and 220 temple servants.

8.title: Fasting for Protection
8.context: At the Ahava Canal Ezra proclaims a fast to humble themselves before God and ask him for a safe journey for their children and possessions; he had been ashamed to ask the king for soldiers, having told him that the hand of God is on everyone who looks to him, so they fast and petition God, and he answers their prayer.

8.title: Priests to Guard the Offerings
8.context: Ezra sets apart twelve of the leading priests and weighs out to them the silver, gold and articles offered for the temple, telling them they and the articles are consecrated to Yahweh, and they are to guard them carefully until they are weighed out in Jerusalem.

8.title: Arrival in Jerusalem
8.context: Ezra’s company sets out from the Ahava canal, and God protects them on the way to Jerusalem, where they hand over the silver, gold and vessels and offer sacrifices.

9.title: Intermarriage with Neighboring Peoples
9.context: The leaders report that many, including priests and Levites, have intermarried with the surrounding peoples and adopted their practices; Ezra tears his clothes, pulls out his hair and sits appalled until evening, then kneels and confesses the people’s guilt in shame.

10.title: Shecaniah’s Encouragement
10.context: A large crowd gathers weeping with Ezra; Shecaniah proposes a covenant to send away the foreign wives, and Ezra has the leaders and people swear to do so.

10.title: Those Guilty of Intermarriage
10.context: A list follows of the priests, Levites and others who had married foreign women, who pledge to send them away and offer guilt offerings.

1.title: Nehemiah’s Prayer
1.context: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the king in Susa, hears that Jerusalem’s walls are broken down and its people in disgrace; he weeps, fasts, confesses Israel’s sins and asks God for favor with the king.

2.title: Nehemiah Sent to Jerusalem
2.context: Seeing his sad face, the king asks the reason; after a silent prayer Nehemiah asks to go and rebuild the city, and the king grants it with letters; he inspects the walls by night and rallies the people to build, while Sanballat and others mock.

3.title: The Builders of the Walls
3.context: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests rebuild the Sheep Gate and consecrate it, and the chapter lists, section by section, who repaired the wall and gates — the Fish Gate, Jeshanah Gate, Valley Gate, Dung Gate and others — often each family repairing the section opposite their own house.

3.title: The Levites Who Built the Wall
3.context: After them the Levites repair their sections, beginning with Rehum son of Bani, followed by Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, and their associates.

3.title: The Priests Who Built the Wall
3.context: After them the priests from the surrounding region repair their sections, and Benjamin, Hasshub and others repair the parts opposite or beside their own houses.

3.title: Others Who Built
3.context: Next, the men of Tekoa repair another section, though their nobles refuse to put their shoulders to the work under their supervisors; goldsmiths, perfume makers and merchants complete the sections in between, all the way back to the Sheep Gate.

4.title: The Work Ridiculed
4.context: Sanballat and Tobiah ridicule the builders and plot an attack; Nehemiah prays and posts guards day and night, with workers holding a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other, and the wall quickly rises to half its height.

5.title: Nehemiah Defends the Oppressed
5.context: Poor families have mortgaged their land and even sold their children to survive famine and taxes; Nehemiah angrily rebukes the nobles for charging their own people interest and makes them return the property and interest.

5.title: Nehemiah’s Generosity
5.context: In twelve years as governor Nehemiah never takes the governor’s food allowance or burdens the people, and feeds many at his own expense, out of reverence for God.

6.title: Sanballat’s Conspiracy
6.context: The enemies repeatedly try to lure Nehemiah away, spread rumors that he plans to rebel, and hire a false prophet to frighten him into hiding in the temple; he sees through each scheme and asks God to strengthen his hands.

6.title: Completion of the Wall
6.context: The wall is completed in fifty-two days, and the surrounding enemies lose heart, knowing that this work was done with the help of God.

7.title: The List of Returning Exiles
7.context: The city is large but its population small; Nehemiah prepares to register the people by genealogy and finds the record of the first returnees, family by family.

8.title: Ezra Reads the Law
8.context: The people gather at the Water Gate and ask Ezra to read the Book of the Law; he reads from daybreak to noon while the Levites explain it, and the people weep, but Nehemiah and Ezra say the day is holy and not for mourning, for the joy of Yahweh is their strength.

8.title: The Feast of Tabernacles
8.context: The next day they study the law, discover the command to live in booths in the seventh month, and celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles with great joy, as had not been done since Joshua’s time.

9.title: The People Confess Their Sins
9.context: The people fast in sackcloth with dust on their heads, separate themselves from foreigners, and stand for hours reading the law, confessing their sins and their ancestors’, and worshiping.

9.title: A Prayer of Confession
9.context: The Levites lead a long prayer praising Yahweh as Creator, recounting his faithfulness from Abraham to the land and Israel’s repeated rebellion; in their distress the people make a binding written agreement to keep God’s law.

10.title: Signers of the Covenant
10.context: Those who sign the covenant include Nehemiah the governor, Zedekiah, the priests, the Levites and the leaders of the people, whose names are listed.

10.title: The Vows of the Covenant
10.context: The people swear to keep God’s law: no intermarriage with foreigners, keeping the Sabbath, canceling debts in the seventh year, supporting the temple, and bringing firstfruits and tithes — they will not neglect the house of their God.

11.title: Jerusalem’s New Settlers
11.context: The leaders settle in Jerusalem and the rest cast lots to move one in ten into the holy city, with volunteers commended; the families who live in the city are listed.

11.title: Those Who Lived in Other Towns
11.context: Some of the people of Judah live in Kiriath Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, Beersheba and other towns and villages, and some of Benjamin’s descendants live from Geba onward; some of the divisions of the Levites are assigned to Judah and Benjamin.

12.title: The Priests and Levites Who Returned
12.context: The priests and Levites who return with Zerubbabel and Jeshua are listed — Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra and others among the priests, and Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel and others among the Levites — with the latter responsible for leading the songs of thanksgiving, along with their associates in the divisions.

12.title: The Descendants of Jeshua the High Priest
12.context: Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, Eliashib fathered Joiada, Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.

12.title: The Priests Who Were Family Heads
12.context: In the days of Joiakim the heads of the priestly families are listed: for the family of Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah, Hananiah; for Ezra, Meshullam; and others.

12.title: The Records of the Priests and Levites
12.context: The family heads of the Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua, as well as those of the priests, are recorded in the book until the reign of Darius the Persian.

12.title: The Divisions Serving in the Temple
12.context: The leaders of the Levites — Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel — and their associates stand opposite one another for praise and thanksgiving, division by division, as David the man of God had commanded; the gatekeepers Mattaniah, Bakbukiah and Obadiah keep guard at the storerooms by the gates.

12.title: The Dedication of the Wall
12.context: At the dedication of the wall, Levites and singers are gathered, two great choirs process in opposite directions along the wall and meet at the temple, sacrifices are offered, and Jerusalem’s rejoicing is heard far away.

12.title: Provisions for Temple Worship
12.context: Men are appointed over the storerooms for the priests’ and Levites’ portions, the singers and gatekeepers serve as David prescribed, and all Israel provides for them regularly.

13.title: Foreigners Excluded
13.context: On that day the Book of Moses is read aloud in the hearing of the people, and they find written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever be admitted into the assembly of God; when they hear this law, they exclude from Israel all who are of foreign descent.

13.title: The Temple Cleansed
13.context: Returning after a time in Babylon, Nehemiah finds Tobiah lodged in a temple storeroom, the Levites unpaid, trade on the Sabbath and renewed intermarriage; he corrects each abuse and prays, “Remember me with favor, my God.”

1.title: Xerxes’ Royal Feast
1.context: Xerxes (Ahasuerus) rules 127 provinces from India to Cush; in his third year he holds a banquet in the citadel of Susa for all his nobles and officials for 180 days to display the wealth of his kingdom, followed by a seven-day banquet for all the people in Susa, while Queen Vashti holds a banquet for the women.

2.title: Seeking Vashti’s Successor
2.context: The king seeks a new queen, and beautiful young women are brought to the palace, among them Esther, the cousin Mordecai the Jew had raised, who tells her not to reveal her people.

2.title: Esther Becomes Queen
2.context: The king loves Esther above all and makes her queen; Mordecai uncovers a plot against the king and reports it through Esther, and it is recorded in the royal annals.

3.title: Haman’s Plot against the Jews
3.context: The king promotes Haman, and the king’s servants at the gate must bow to him, but Mordecai refuses; enraged, Haman casts lots (pur) to choose a date and gets a royal decree to destroy all the Jews on the thirteenth of Adar.

4.title: Mordecai Appeals to Esther
4.context: The Jews mourn; Mordecai urges Esther to plead with the king, and when she says approaching uninvited risks death, he asks whether she has not come to royal position for such a time as this; she asks the Jews to fast three days and resolves to go, even if she perishes.

5.title: Esther Approaches the King
5.context: Esther appears before the king in royal robes and he holds out the gold scepter; she invites the king and Haman to a banquet and then to a second banquet the next day.

5.title: Haman’s Plot against Mordecai
5.context: Haman is enraged that Mordecai will not rise for him; after boasting at home of his honors, he follows his wife’s advice and builds a tall gallows to hang Mordecai on.

6.title: Mordecai Is Honored
6.context: Sleepless, the king has the annals read and learns that Mordecai was never rewarded; Haman arrives, is asked how to honor the man the king delights in, assumes it is himself, and ends up leading Mordecai through the streets in honor.

7.title: Esther Pleads for Her People
7.context: At the second banquet Esther asks the king to spare her life and her people’s and names Haman as their enemy; the king is furious, and Haman is hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.

8.title: Esther Appeals for the Jews
8.context: The king gives Haman’s estate to Esther and his signet ring to Mordecai; Esther pleads in tears to revoke the decree, and Mordecai issues a new decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves, bringing joy to Jews everywhere.

9.title: The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
9.context: On the thirteenth of Adar the tables are turned and the Jews overpower those who sought to destroy them, though they take no plunder.

9.title: The Feast of Purim Instituted
9.context: Mordecai writes to Jews everywhere to celebrate the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar each year as Purim, with feasting, gifts to one another and to the poor, remembering how sorrow was turned into joy.

10.title: Tribute to Xerxes and Mordecai
10.context: Mordecai becomes second only to the king, highly esteemed among the Jews because he works for the good of his people.

1.title: Job’s Character and Wealth
1.context: In the land of Uz lives Job, blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil; he is the greatest man in the East and regularly offers burnt offerings in case his children have sinned.

1.title: Job Loses His Children and Possessions
1.context: In one day Job loses his livestock, servants and all his children; he tears his robe and falls down in worship, saying that Yahweh gave and Yahweh has taken away, blessed be his name; he does not sin or blame God.

2.title: Job Loses His Health
2.context: The Accuser challenges Yahweh again and is allowed to strike Job’s body but not take his life; covered with sores, Job rejects his wife’s urging to curse God, saying they must accept trouble from God as well as good.

2.title: Job’s Three Friends
2.context: Three friends — Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar — come to comfort Job; they weep aloud and sit on the ground with him for seven days and nights without saying a word, seeing how great his suffering is.

3.title: Job Laments His Birth
3.context: Job breaks the silence by cursing the day of his birth, asking why life is given to those in misery who long for death; “what I feared has come upon me,” he says.

4.title: Eliphaz: The Innocent Prosper
4.context: Eliphaz opens the first round of speeches between Job and his three friends: he argues that the innocent do not perish and that those who sow trouble reap it, and he recounts a night vision asking whether a mortal can be more righteous than God. This round runs through chapter 14.

15.title: Eliphaz: Job Does Not Fear God
15.context: The second round begins: Eliphaz accuses Job of empty words and says the wicked suffer all their days; this round runs through chapter 21, with Job continuing to protest his innocence.

22.title: Eliphaz: Can a Man Be of Use to God?
22.context: The third round begins: Eliphaz accuses Job of great sins and urges him to return to the Almighty and be restored; this round runs through chapter 31, ending with Job’s long final defense.

28.title: Where Can Wisdom Be Found?
28.context: Job reflects on wisdom: people mine deep in the earth but cannot find it, and no gold can buy it; only God knows where it is, and he tells mankind that the fear of the Lord is wisdom and turning from evil is understanding.

29.title: Job’s Former Blessings
29.context: Job longs for the days when God watched over him and he was honored at the city gate, because he rescued the poor and the fatherless and wore righteousness like a robe.

32.title: Elihu Rebukes Job’s Friends
32.context: When the three friends stop answering, young Elihu, who has waited because they were older, grows angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God and with the friends for failing to refute him, and he says wisdom comes from the spirit in a person, not from age.

38.title: Yahweh Challenges Job
38.context: Yahweh answers Job from the storm with a series of questions about creation and the care of the world — the earth’s foundations, the sea, the stars, the weather and the animals; Job admits he spoke of things he did not understand, saying he had heard of God but now has seen him, and repents in dust and ashes.

42.title: Yahweh Rebukes Job’s Friends
42.context: Yahweh tells Eliphaz that he and his friends have not spoken rightly of him as Job has; Job prays for them, and Yahweh restores his fortunes with twice as much as before, and Job lives another 140 years and dies old and full of years.

1.title: The Two Paths
1.context: The opening of the Psalter, with no title: the person who delights in Yahweh’s law is like a tree by streams of water, while the wicked are like chaff the wind drives away.

2.title: The Triumphant Messiah
2.context: The nations and kings conspire against Yahweh and his anointed, yet he has installed his king on Zion; Acts 4:25–26 and 13:33 apply this psalm to Jesus.

3.title: Deliver Me, O Yahweh!
3.context: A psalm of David when he fled from his son Absalom: surrounded by foes, he lies down and sleeps in peace, for “from Yahweh comes deliverance.”

4.title: Answer Me When I Call!
4.context: A psalm of David for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments: an evening prayer asking Yahweh to answer, and ending in peaceful sleep.

5.title: Give Ear to My Words
5.context: A psalm of David, for flutes: a morning prayer that Yahweh hear his words and lead him in righteousness, and that all who take refuge in him be glad.

6.title: Do Not Rebuke Me in Your Anger
6.context: A psalm of David, on the sheminith: a sick and weary man pleads that Yahweh not rebuke him in anger, for his bones are in agony; in the end Yahweh hears his weeping.

7.title: I Take Refuge in You
7.context: A shiggaion of David sung to Yahweh concerning Cush, a Benjamite: pursued, he takes refuge in Yahweh and asks him to judge him by his righteousness.

8.title: How Majestic Is Your Name!
8.context: A psalm of David: looking at the heavens, he marvels at the majesty of Yahweh’s name and that he has crowned human beings with glory and honor over his works; Hebrews 2:6–9 quotes it.

9.title: I Will Give Thanks to Yahweh
9.context: A psalm of David: thanks to Yahweh who judges the nations in righteousness, a stronghold for the oppressed, who does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.

10.title: The Perils of the Pilgrim
10.context: With no title: the psalmist asks why Yahweh stands far off while the wicked hunt down the weak, and ends sure that Yahweh hears the desire of the afflicted.

11.title: In Yahweh I Take Refuge
11.context: A psalm of David: when friends urge him to flee like a bird to the mountains, he answers, “In Yahweh I take refuge”; Yahweh is in his holy temple and his eyes examine everyone.

12.title: The Godly Are No More
12.context: A psalm of David: the faithful have vanished and everyone lies to his neighbor, but Yahweh promises to arise for the poor, and his words are flawless, like silver refined seven times.

13.title: How Long, O Yahweh?
13.context: A psalm of David asking four times “How long?” and ending with trust in Yahweh’s unfailing love and a song of praise.

14.title: The Fool Says There Is No God
14.context: A psalm of David: the fool says in his heart, “There is no God”; Yahweh looks down from heaven and finds no one who does good (compare Romans 3:10–12), and the psalmist longs for Israel’s salvation to come from Zion.

15.title: Who May Dwell on Your Holy Mountain?
15.context: A psalm of David: who may dwell in Yahweh’s sanctuary? The one whose walk is blameless, who speaks the truth, does no wrong to neighbors and does not lend at interest.

16.title: The Presence of Yahweh
16.context: A miktam of David: Yahweh is his portion and his cup, and he keeps Yahweh always before him; he trusts that Yahweh will not abandon him to the grave (quoted in Acts 2:25–31).

17.title: Hear My Righteous Plea
17.context: A prayer of David: protesting his integrity, he asks Yahweh to keep him as the apple of his eye, and he is satisfied to see Yahweh’s face when he awakes.

18.title: Yahweh Is My Rock
18.context: A psalm of David, servant of Yahweh, sung the day Yahweh delivered him from all his enemies and from Saul (see 2 Samuel 22): Yahweh is his rock, fortress and deliverer.

19.title: The Heavens Declare the Glory of God
19.context: A psalm of David: the heavens declare the glory of God, day after day pouring out speech without words.

19.title: The Law of Yahweh
19.context: The law of Yahweh is perfect, reviving the soul; his precepts and commands are more precious than gold and sweeter than honey, and the psalmist asks to be cleared of hidden faults.

20.title: The Day of Trouble
20.context: A psalm of David: the people pray that Yahweh answer the king in the day of trouble; some trust in chariots and horses, but “we trust in the name of Yahweh our God.”

21.title: After the Battle
21.context: A psalm of David: the king rejoices in Yahweh’s strength, who has given him the desire of his heart and blessed him forever; through the unfailing love of the Most High he will not be shaken.

22.title: The Psalm of the Cross
22.context: A psalm of David that opens with the cry of being forsaken by God; the sufferer endures scorn and agony, yet ends confident that the nations will turn to Yahweh. Jesus quotes its first line on the cross (Matthew 27:46), and the passion accounts echo it often.

23.title: Yahweh Is My Shepherd
23.context: A psalm of David: Yahweh is my shepherd, I lack nothing; he guides me along right paths, and even through the valley of the shadow of death I fear no evil; I will dwell in the house of Yahweh forever.

24.title: The Earth Is Yahweh’s
24.context: A psalm of David: the earth and everything in it belongs to Yahweh; who may ascend his holy hill? The one with clean hands and a pure heart, and the gates are told to lift up their heads for the King of glory.

25.title: To You I Lift Up My Soul
25.context: A psalm of David, an acrostic: “To you, Yahweh, I lift up my soul,” asking to be taught his ways and forgiven; no one who waits for him will be put to shame.

26.title: Vindicate Me, O Yahweh
26.context: A psalm of David: he walks in integrity, asks Yahweh to test his heart and mind, and loves the house where Yahweh dwells.

27.title: Yahweh Is My Salvation
27.context: A psalm of David: with Yahweh as his light and salvation he has nothing to fear; his one desire is to dwell in Yahweh’s house and gaze on his beauty, and he ends by urging patient waiting on Yahweh.

28.title: Yahweh Is My Strength
28.context: A psalm of David: he cries to Yahweh his rock not to be dragged away with the wicked, and then blesses Yahweh because he has heard his cry; Yahweh is his strength and shield.

29.title: Ascribe Glory to Yahweh
29.context: A psalm of David: the voice of Yahweh thunders over the waters and shakes the desert; all are called to ascribe to Yahweh the glory due his name.

30.title: You Turned My Mourning into Dancing
30.context: A psalm of David for the dedication of the house: Yahweh has rescued him from death; his anger lasts a moment but his favor a lifetime, and weeping in the night gives way to joy in the morning.

31.title: Into Your Hands I Commit My Spirit
31.context: A psalm of David: he takes refuge in Yahweh and says, “Into your hands I commit my spirit”; Jesus speaks these words on the cross (Luke 23:46).

32.title: The Joy of Forgiveness
32.context: A maskil of David: blessed is the one whose transgressions are forgiven; while he kept silent his bones wasted away, but when he confessed Yahweh forgave. Paul quotes the opening in Romans 4:6–8.

33.title: Praise to the Creator
33.context: With no title: the righteous are called to sing joyfully to Yahweh, whose word is right; by his word the heavens were made, and his eyes are on those who fear him.

34.title: Taste and See That Yahweh Is Good
34.context: A psalm of David when he pretended to be insane before Abimelek and was driven away, an acrostic: “Taste and see that Yahweh is good”; the righteous have many troubles, but Yahweh delivers them from them all.

35.title: Contend with My Opponents, O Yahweh
35.context: A psalm of David: he asks Yahweh to contend with those who contend with him; though he fasted and mourned for his enemies in their illness, they set a trap for him without cause.

36.title: The Transgression of the Wicked
36.context: A psalm of David, servant of Yahweh: sin whispers to the wicked, who have no fear of God before their eyes.

36.title: The Goodness of God
36.context: Yahweh’s steadfast love reaches the heavens and his faithfulness the skies; people find refuge under his wings, for with him is the fountain of life, and in his light we see light.

37.title: Delight Yourself in Yahweh
37.context: A psalm of David, an acrostic: do not fret because of evildoers; delight yourself in Yahweh, commit your way to him, and the meek will inherit the land.

38.title: Do Not Rebuke Me in Your Anger
38.context: A psalm of David, a petition: his sin weighs him down and his body is ill, friends stand aloof and enemies plot, yet he waits for Yahweh and asks him not to be far.

39.title: I Will Watch My Ways
39.context: A psalm of David for Jeduthun: he has resolved to guard his tongue, then asks Yahweh to show him the measure of his days; life is a mere breath, and his hope is in Yahweh.

40.title: I Waited Patiently for Yahweh
40.context: A psalm of David: “I waited patiently for Yahweh”; he lifted him out of the pit and gave him a new song. Sacrifice and offering he did not desire, but ears opened to obey; Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes these verses.

40.title: A Prayer for Help
40.context: Troubles beyond number surround him and his sins have overtaken him; he asks Yahweh to be quick to help, so that all who seek him will rejoice.

41.title: Victory over Betrayal
41.context: A psalm of David: blessed is the one who has regard for the weak; he is ill and his enemies say he will never rise, even his close friend has lifted his heel against him, yet Yahweh upholds him. Jesus applies the betrayal line to Judas (John 13:18).

42.title: As the Deer Pants for the Water
42.context: A maskil of the sons of Korah: as a deer pants for streams of water, so his soul pants for the living God; downcast, he tells himself to hope in God, for he will yet praise him.

43.title: Send Out Your Light
43.context: With no title and often read with Psalm 42: he asks God to vindicate him, to send his light and truth to lead him to his holy mountain, and ends again telling his soul to hope in God.

44.title: Redeem Us, O God
44.context: A maskil of the sons of Korah recalling how God once drove out the nations for their ancestors; now the nation is defeated and disgraced though it has not forgotten him, and it pleads with God to rise and redeem them for his love’s sake. Paul cites verse 22 in Romans 8:36.

45.title: My Heart Is Stirred by a Noble Theme
45.context: A maskil of the sons of Korah, a wedding song for the king: it praises his grace, righteousness and everlasting throne, and the bride is called to honor him; Hebrews 1:8–9 quotes verses 6–7 concerning the Son.

46.title: God Is Our Refuge and Strength
46.context: A song of the sons of Korah: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble; though the earth gives way, the river of God makes the city glad. “Be still, and know that I am God.”

47.title: Clap Your Hands, All You Peoples
47.context: A psalm of the sons of Korah: all peoples are told to clap and shout to God, for Yahweh Most High is the great King over all the earth, and God reigns over the nations.

48.title: The City of the Great King
48.context: A song of the sons of Korah: Zion is the city of the great King, where God has made himself known as a fortress; the pilgrims walk around it, count its towers and marvel at it.

49.title: The Evanescence of Wealth
49.context: A psalm of the sons of Korah, words of wisdom: no one can redeem the life of another, riches cannot rescue anyone from the grave, but God will redeem the psalmist from the realm of the dead.

50.title: The Mighty One Calls
50.context: A psalm of Asaph: God shines forth from Zion to judge his people, saying he has no need of bulls and goats, but wants a sacrifice of thanksgiving, vows fulfilled to the Most High, and prayer in the day of trouble.

51.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart, O God
51.context: A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him after he had gone to Bathsheba: he asks God to have mercy, blot out his transgressions, create in him a clean heart and renew a steadfast spirit within him.

52.title: Why Do You Boast of Evil?
52.context: A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite told Saul that David had gone to Ahimelek’s house: the one who boasts of evil will be uprooted by God, while the psalmist is like an olive tree flourishing in God’s house.

53.title: The Fool Says There Is No God
53.context: A maskil of David, closely parallel to Psalm 14: the fool says in his heart, “There is no God”; all have turned aside, and no one does good.

54.title: Save Me by Your Name
54.context: A maskil of David, when the Ziphites went to Saul and said David was hiding among them: he asks God to save him by his name, for God is his helper and sustains him.

55.title: Cast Your Burden upon Yahweh
55.context: A maskil of David, grieving a close friend’s betrayal and wishing for wings like a dove to fly away; he ends by urging that burdens be cast on Yahweh, who sustains the righteous.

56.title: Be Merciful to Me, O God
56.context: A miktam of David when the Philistines seized him in Gath: when afraid he trusts in God and praises his word, and so does not fear what mortals can do to him.

57.title: In You My Soul Takes Refuge
57.context: A miktam of David when he hid from Saul in the cave: he takes refuge in the shadow of God’s wings until disaster passes, and with a steadfast heart he will praise the Lord among the nations.

58.title: God Judges the Earth
58.context: A miktam of David: he rebukes unjust rulers and asks God to break the teeth of the wicked; the righteous will be glad when they see vengeance, and people will say there is a God who judges the earth.

59.title: Deliver Me from My Enemies
59.context: A miktam of David, when Saul had sent men to watch his house in order to kill him: he asks God to rescue him from his enemies and sings of God as his strength, fortress and loving God.

60.title: Victory with God
60.context: A miktam of David for teaching, when Joab struck down 12,000 Edomites: after a national defeat he asks God for help, since human help is worthless; “with God we will gain the victory.”

61.title: You Have Heard My Vows
61.context: A psalm of David on stringed instruments: from the ends of the earth he cries to God, asking to be led to the rock higher than he, and longs to dwell in God’s tent forever, sheltered under the shelter of his wings.

62.title: Waiting on God
62.context: A psalm of David: his soul waits in silence for God alone, the source of his salvation and hope; power belongs to God, and steadfast love to the Lord.

63.title: Thirsting for God
63.context: A psalm of David when he was in the Desert of Judah: his soul thirsts for God like dry ground, for God’s love is better than life, and he remembers him on his bed through the watches of the night.

64.title: The Hurtful Tongue
64.context: A psalm of David: he asks God to protect his life from the threat of the enemy; the wicked sharpen their tongues like swords and shoot hidden arrows, but God shoots back, and all will fear and proclaim what he has done.

65.title: Praise Awaits God in Zion
65.context: A psalm of David, a song: praise awaits God in Zion, who answers prayer and atones for transgressions; he waters the earth, crowns the year with bounty, and the meadows and valleys shout for joy.

66.title: Make a Joyful Noise
66.context: With no title: the whole earth is called to shout for joy to God, whose works are awesome; he turned the sea into dry land, tested his people as silver is refined, and brought them to a place of abundance, and the psalmist offers his vows.

67.title: May God Cause His Face to Shine upon Us
67.context: With no title: a prayer that God be gracious and bless us and make his face shine on us, so that his ways be known on earth and his salvation among all nations, and that all the peoples praise him.

68.title: God’s Enemies Are Scattered
68.context: A song of David calling God to arise and scatter his enemies; he is father to the fatherless and defender of widows, who led his people through the desert and ascended his holy mountain. Paul cites verse 18 in Ephesians 4:8.

69.title: The Waters Are up to My Neck
69.context: A psalm of David: the waters have come up to his neck, he sinks in the mire, and is a stranger to his own family because of zeal for God’s house; the New Testament quotes it in John 2:17 and Romans 15:3.

70.title: Hurry, O Yahweh, to Help Me!
70.context: A psalm of David, a petition: “Hasten, Yahweh, to help me,” and may all who seek him rejoice and be glad.

71.title: Be My Rock of Refuge
71.context: With no title, the prayer of an aged believer: he has relied on Yahweh since youth and asks not to be forsaken now that he is old and gray, so that he may proclaim God’s power to the next generation.

72.title: Endow the King with Your Justice
72.context: A psalm of Solomon: a prayer that God give the king his justice, that he judge the people in righteousness and defend the needy, that his name endure forever, and that all nations be blessed through him; it closes the second book of the Psalms.

73.title: Surely God Is Good to Israel
73.context: A psalm of Asaph: God is good to Israel, but seeing the prosperity of the wicked he nearly slipped, until he entered God’s sanctuary and understood their end; “Whom have I in heaven but you?”

74.title: Why Have You Rejected Us Forever?
74.context: A maskil of Asaph: the sanctuary has been burned and the people seem abandoned; he asks, “Why have you rejected us forever, God?” and appeals to God to remember his covenant and his people.

75.title: God’s Righteous Judgment
75.context: A psalm of Asaph: we praise you, God; at the appointed time he judges uprightly, bringing one down and lifting another up, and the wicked must drain the cup of his wrath.

76.title: God’s Name Is Great in Israel
76.context: A song of Asaph: God is known in Judah and his name is great in Israel; in Zion he broke the flashing arrows and the shield, and all the earth’s rulers are to bring gifts to the one to be feared.

77.title: In the Day of Trouble I Sought the Lord
77.context: A psalm of Asaph: in the day of trouble he seeks the Lord, lies awake with his spirit troubled, and then remembers what God did in the past, how he led his people through the sea like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.title: I Will Open My Mouth in Parables
78.context: A maskil of Asaph: a call to tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of Yahweh, recounting history from the exodus to David, Israel’s repeated rebellion, God’s compassion, and his choice of Judah and David to shepherd his people. Matthew 13:35 quotes verse 2.

79.title: A Prayer for Deliverance
79.context: A psalm of Asaph: the nations have invaded God’s inheritance, defiled his temple and left Jerusalem in ruins; the psalmist asks God to help his people for the glory of his name, to forgive their sins, and to avenge his servants.

80.title: Hear Us, O Shepherd of Israel
80.context: A psalm of Asaph calling on the Shepherd of Israel; Israel is the vine God brought out of Egypt, now ravaged, and the refrain repeatedly asks God to restore them and make his face shine so they may be saved.

81.title: Sing for Joy to God Our Strength
81.context: A psalm of Asaph calling for festival joy before God, who reminds Israel that he rescued them from Egypt and longed to satisfy them fully, if only they had listened.

82.title: God Presides in the Divine Assembly
82.context: A psalm of Asaph: God presides in the great assembly and renders judgment among the “gods,” rebuking those who judge unjustly and neglect the weak. Jesus quotes verse 6 in John 10:34–36.

83.title: O God, Be Not Silent
83.context: A song of Asaph: “God, do not remain silent”; nations conspire to wipe out the name of Israel, and the psalmist asks God to deal with them as with Midian, so that they will know that he, whose name is Yahweh, is the Most High over all the earth.

84.title: Better Is One Day in Your Courts
84.context: A psalm of the sons of Korah longing for Yahweh’s dwelling place: one day in his courts is better than a thousand elsewhere, and blessed are those whose strength is in him on the pilgrim way to Zion.

85.title: You Showed Favor to Your Land
85.context: A psalm of the sons of Korah: Yahweh showed favor to his land in the past, and now they ask him to restore them; love and faithfulness meet together, righteousness and peace kiss each other.

86.title: Tried but Trusting
86.context: A prayer of David, poor and needy, asking the Lord to hear; none among the gods is like the Lord, and he asks to be taught his way and given an undivided heart to fear his name.

87.title: Yahweh Loves the Gates of Zion
87.context: A song of the sons of Korah: Yahweh loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob, and people of many nations are recorded as having been born there.

88.title: I Cry Out before You
88.context: A song of the sons of Korah, for Heman the Ezrahite: the darkest psalm, which ends with darkness; he has suffered from youth, cries to Yahweh day and night, and his friends have been taken from him.

89.title: I Will Sing of His Love Forever
89.context: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite singing of Yahweh’s everlasting love and faithfulness, especially his covenant to establish David’s line and throne.

89.title: God's Promise to David
89.context: In a vision Yahweh spoke to his faithful people: he has exalted a young man from the people, anointed David his servant, and will make him the firstborn, the most exalted of the kings of the earth, with his love and covenant secure for him.

89.title: A Lament over the King's Defeat
89.context: But now, the psalmist complains, you have rejected and spurned your anointed one, renounced the covenant with your servant, and defiled his crown in the dust; the king is wearied by shame.

89.title: A Prayer for Deliverance
89.context: The psalmist asks how long Yahweh will hide himself and asks him to remember how short life is; the psalm and the third book of the Psalter close with a blessing of Yahweh forever, Amen and Amen.

90.title: From Everlasting to Everlasting
90.context: A prayer of Moses the man of God: the Lord has been our dwelling place in every generation; to him a thousand years are like yesterday, while human life is like grass, so we ask him to teach us to number our days and gain a wise heart.

91.title: You Are My Refuge and My Fortress
91.context: With no title: whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty; he delivers from the fowler’s snare, and he commands his angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways. Satan quotes verses 11–12 in Matthew 4:6.

92.title: How Great Are Your Works!
92.context: A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: it is good to praise Yahweh; the righteous flourish like a palm tree and grow like a cedar of Lebanon, still bearing fruit in old age.

93.title: Yahweh Reigns!
93.context: With no title: Yahweh reigns, robed in majesty and armed with strength; the world is established and cannot be moved, and his throne was established long ago.

94.title: Yahweh Will Not Forget His People
94.context: With no title: a cry to the God who avenges to rise up and repay the proud; the psalmist says Yahweh will not reject his people, for he who teaches humanity knows the thoughts of man, and his comfort brought joy to the psalmist’s soul.

95.title: Do Not Harden Your Hearts
95.context: Untitled: a call to sing to Yahweh and bow before our Maker, for we are the sheep of his pasture, with a warning not to harden hearts as at Meribah. Hebrews 3–4 expounds this psalm.

96.title: Sing to Yahweh, All the Earth
96.context: With no title: all the earth is called to sing a new song to Yahweh and declare his glory among the nations; the gods of the peoples are idols, but Yahweh made the heavens, and he comes to judge the earth in righteousness. 1 Chronicles 16 uses part of it.

97.title: Let the Earth Rejoice
97.context: With no title: Yahweh reigns, let the earth be glad; clouds and thick darkness surround him, righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne, and the worshipers of idols are put to shame.

98.title: Sing to Yahweh a New Song
98.context: A psalm: sing to Yahweh a new song, for he has done marvelous things; his salvation and righteousness are revealed to the nations, and sea, rivers and mountains sing before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.

99.title: Yahweh Reigns!
99.context: With no title: Yahweh reigns, let the nations tremble; he sits enthroned between the cherubim, and “he is holy.” He spoke to Moses, Aaron and Samuel from the pillar of cloud, and answered them when they called.

100.title: Make a Joyful Noise
100.context: A psalm of thanksgiving: all the earth is called to shout for joy to Yahweh and serve him with gladness; he is God and we are his people, the sheep of his pasture, and “his love endures forever.”

101.title: I Will Set No Worthless Thing before My Eyes
101.context: A psalm of David: he will sing of love and justice, walk with integrity in his house, set no worthless thing before his eyes, and cut off the slanderer and the proud.

102.title: The Prayer of the Afflicted
102.context: The prayer of an afflicted person who has grown weak and pours out a lament before Yahweh: his days vanish like smoke, but Yahweh is enthroned forever and will arise and have compassion on Zion. Hebrews 1:10–12 quotes verses 25–27.

103.title: Bless Yahweh, O My Soul
103.context: A psalm of David: “Praise Yahweh, my soul” — he forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases; he is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his love for those who fear him.

104.title: How Many Are Your Works, O Yahweh!
104.context: With no title: Yahweh is praised for creation — he wraps himself in light, makes the clouds his chariot, sets the earth on its foundations, sends springs into the valleys and feeds every creature; “how many are your works, Yahweh!”

105.title: Tell of His Wonders
105.context: With no title: give thanks to Yahweh and make known his deeds — he remembered his covenant with Abraham, protected the patriarchs, sent Joseph ahead to Egypt, brought Israel out with silver and gold, and gave them the lands of the nations.

106.title: Give Thanks to Yahweh, for He Is Good
106.context: With no title: “Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good”; the psalm confesses Israel’s repeated sins from Egypt and the sea through the wilderness and Canaan, and Yahweh’s repeated compassion, and ends by asking him to gather them from the nations. It closes the fourth book.

107.title: Thanksgiving for Deliverance
107.context: Untitled: let the redeemed of Yahweh give thanks; four groups — wanderers in the desert, prisoners, the sick and sailors in a storm — cry out in trouble and are rescued, each section ending with a call to thank him for his steadfast love.

108.title: Israel’s Kingdom Blessing
108.context: A song of David combining parts of Psalms 57 and 60: “My heart, O God, is steadfast,” and a prayer for victory because human help is worthless — “with God we will gain the victory.”

109.title: The Song of the Slandered
109.context: A psalm of David: surrounded by liars who repay his love with accusation, he turns to prayer and calls on God to deal with the accuser; he asks Yahweh to help him for the sake of his name, since he is poor and needy. Acts 1:20 quotes verse 8.

110.title: God’s Faithful Messiah
110.context: A psalm of David in which Yahweh invites David’s lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are subdued, and declares him a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek. Jesus (Matthew 22:41–46), Peter (Acts 2:34–35) and Hebrews all apply it to the Messiah.

111.title: Majestic Is His Work
111.context: An untitled acrostic praising Yahweh wholeheartedly for his glorious works and his faithfulness to his covenant; the fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom.

112.title: The Blessed Fear of Yahweh
112.context: With no title, an acrostic: blessed are those who fear Yahweh and delight in his commands; their descendants will be mighty, their righteousness endures, and they are generous to the poor.

113.title: Yahweh Exalts the Humble
113.context: With no title: praise Yahweh from now and forever; though he is high above the nations, he stoops to look on heaven and earth, lifts the poor from the dust and the needy from the ash heap, and gives the childless woman a home.

114.title: A Psalm of Exodus
114.context: With no title: when Israel came out of Egypt, the sea fled, the Jordan turned back, and the mountains skipped like rams; the earth is told to tremble before the Lord, who turns rock into a pool.

115.title: To Your Name Be the Glory
115.context: Untitled: glory belongs not to us but to Yahweh’s name; the nations’ idols have mouths but cannot speak and eyes but cannot see, while those who trust in Yahweh have him as help and shield.

116.title: Yahweh Has Heard My Voice
116.context: Untitled: the psalmist loves Yahweh, who heard his cry and rescued him from death; he will lift up the cup of salvation and fulfill his vows before the people, for the death of his faithful ones is precious to Yahweh.

117.title: Extol Him, All You Peoples
117.context: The shortest psalm: all nations and peoples are called to praise Yahweh, for his love toward us is great and his faithfulness endures forever. Romans 15:11 quotes it.

118.title: Yahweh Is on My Side
118.context: Untitled: give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good and his love endures forever; with Yahweh on his side the psalmist fears nothing, and the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. The New Testament quotes it often (Matthew 21:9, 42; Acts 4:11).

119.title: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet
119.context: The longest chapter of the Bible, an acrostic of twenty-two eight-verse stanzas, one for each Hebrew letter, nearly every verse mentioning God’s law, statutes, precepts or commands; the first stanza blesses those who walk blamelessly in Yahweh’s law.

119.title: ב BETH
119.context: Second stanza: a young person keeps his way pure by living according to God’s word, and the psalmist treasures that word in his heart so as not to sin.

119.title: ג GIMEL
119.context: Third stanza: he asks God to open his eyes to see wonders in the law; as a stranger on earth he asks not to be kept from God’s commands.

119.title: ד DALETH
119.context: The fourth stanza, Daleth: his soul clings to the dust, so he asks to be revived according to God’s word; he has chosen the way of faithfulness and runs in the path of his commands.

119.title: ה HE
119.context: The fifth stanza, He: teach me, Yahweh, the way of your decrees; give me understanding to keep your law, turn my heart toward your statutes and not toward selfish gain, and turn my eyes from worthless things.

119.title: ו WAW
119.context: The sixth stanza, Waw: may your unfailing love come to me, Yahweh, so that I may answer those who taunt me; he will speak of your statutes before kings without being ashamed.

119.title: ז ZAYIN
119.context: The seventh stanza, Zayin: remember your word to your servant, for it has given me hope; your promise preserves my life, and in the house of my pilgrimage your decrees are my songs.

119.title: ח HETH
119.context: Eighth stanza: Yahweh is his portion and he has promised to keep his words; he rises at midnight to give thanks and is a companion of all who fear God.

119.title: ט TETH
119.context: Ninth stanza: God has dealt well with his servant; the psalmist says affliction was good for him, teaching him God’s decrees, and the law is worth more than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.

119.title: י YODH
119.context: The tenth stanza, Yodh: your hands made and formed me; give me understanding to learn your commands; his affliction was in faithfulness, and he asks for compassion that he may live.

119.title: כ KAPH
119.context: The eleventh stanza, Kaph: his soul faints for Yahweh’s salvation, his eyes fail looking for his promise; though he is like a wineskin in the smoke, he does not forget his decrees.

119.title: ל LAMEDH
119.context: Twelfth stanza: Yahweh’s word stands firm in heaven forever and his faithfulness lasts through all generations; had the law not been his delight, the psalmist would have perished in his affliction.

119.title: מ MEM
119.context: Thirteenth stanza: he loves God’s law and meditates on it all day; God’s commands make him wiser than his enemies and teachers, and God’s words taste sweeter than honey.

119.title: נ NUN
119.context: Fourteenth stanza: God’s word is a lamp to his feet and a light to his path; he has vowed to keep God’s righteous laws and does not forget them even in affliction.

119.title: ס SAMEKH
119.context: Fifteenth stanza: he hates the double-minded but loves God’s law; God is his hiding place and shield, and he hopes in his word.

119.title: ע AYIN
119.context: The sixteenth stanza, Ayin: he has done what is righteous and just, so he asks not to be left to his oppressors; he asks God to deal with his servant according to his love, since it is time for Yahweh to act, for people have broken his law.

119.title: פ PE
119.context: Seventeenth stanza: God’s testimonies are wonderful, the unfolding of his words gives light and understanding to the simple, and the psalmist weeps because people do not keep the law.

119.title: צ TZADE
119.context: Eighteenth stanza: Yahweh is righteous and his judgments are right, his word thoroughly tested; though small and despised, the psalmist does not forget God’s precepts.

119.title: ק KOPH
119.context: Nineteenth stanza: he calls with his whole heart, rising before dawn to cry for help and staying awake through the night watches to meditate on God’s word; Yahweh is near, and all his commands are true.

119.title: ר RESH
119.context: Twentieth stanza: he asks God to look on his suffering, defend his cause and redeem him; the sum of God’s word is truth, and his righteous judgments endure forever.

119.title: ש SIN and SHIN
119.context: The twenty-first stanza, Sin and Shin: rulers persecute him without cause, but his heart trembles at Yahweh’s word; he rejoices in it like one who finds great spoil, praises God seven times a day, and says that those who love his law have great peace and nothing can make them stumble.

119.title: ת TAW
119.context: Twenty-second stanza, the last: he asks that his cry and plea come before God; he has strayed like a lost sheep and asks God to seek his servant, for he has not forgotten his commands.

120.title: In My Distress I Cried to Yahweh
120.context: The first of the Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120–134, sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem): in distress he called to Yahweh and he answered; he lives among liars and the hostile, and longs for peace.

121.title: I Lift Up My Eyes to the Hills
121.context: A song of ascents: the pilgrim lifts his eyes to the hills and finds his help in Yahweh, Maker of heaven and earth, who never slumbers but watches over his going out and coming in forever.

122.title: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem
122.context: A song of ascents of David: he rejoices when invited to go to Yahweh’s house, and prays for the peace and prosperity of Jerusalem.

123.title: I Lift Up My Eyes to You
123.context: A song of ascents: as servants look to their master’s hand, so the people look to God, asking for mercy because they have endured much contempt.

124.title: Our Help Is in the Name of Yahweh
124.context: A song of ascents of David: had Yahweh not been on their side, enemies would have swallowed them; they have escaped like a bird from the snare, for their help is in the name of Yahweh, Maker of heaven and earth.

125.title: Yahweh Surrounds His People
125.context: A song of ascents: those who trust in Yahweh are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken; as mountains surround Jerusalem, so Yahweh surrounds his people from this time on and forever.

126.title: Zion’s Captives Restored
126.context: A song of ascents: when Yahweh restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who dreamed, and our mouths were filled with laughter; those who sow with tears will reap with songs of joy.

127.title: Children Are a Heritage from Yahweh
127.context: A song of ascents of Solomon: unless Yahweh builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless Yahweh watches over the city, the guards stand watch in vain; children are a heritage from Yahweh, a reward from him.

128.title: The Blessed Fear of Yahweh
128.context: A song of ascents: blessed are all who fear Yahweh and walk in his ways; your wife will be like a fruitful vine and your children like olive shoots around your table, and may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life.

129.title: The Cords of the Wicked
129.context: A song of ascents: Israel has been oppressed from its youth but never overcome, for Yahweh is righteous and has cut the cords of the wicked.

130.title: Out of the Depths
130.context: A song of ascents: “Out of the depths I cry to you, Yahweh”; if you kept a record of sins, who could stand? But with you there is forgiveness, so that we can serve you with reverence; Israel is to put its hope in Yahweh, for with him is unfailing love and full redemption.

131.title: I Have Stilled My Soul
131.context: A song of ascents of David: his heart is not proud, nor his eyes haughty; he has calmed and quieted his soul like a weaned child with its mother, and calls Israel to put its hope in Yahweh from this time on and forever.

132.title: Yahweh Has Chosen Zion
132.context: A song of ascents: remember David and all his hardships — he swore he would find a dwelling for Yahweh; Yahweh swore to David that his descendants would sit on his throne forever, for he has chosen Zion and desired it as his resting place.

133.title: How Pleasant to Live in Harmony!
133.context: A song of ascents of David: how good it is when brothers live in unity, like precious oil on Aaron’s head and the dew of Hermon on Zion, where Yahweh commands his blessing of life forever.

134.title: Bless Yahweh, All You Servants
134.context: The last of the Songs of Ascents: all you servants of Yahweh who minister by night in his house, lift up your hands in the sanctuary and praise Yahweh; may Yahweh, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.

135.title: Give Praise, O Servants of Yahweh
135.context: With no title: servants of Yahweh, praise his name; he chose Jacob and Israel for himself, he does whatever pleases him in heaven and on earth, and the idols of the nations are silver and gold, shaped by human hands, with mouths that cannot speak.

136.title: His Loving Devotion Endures Forever
136.context: With no title, each line ending “His love endures forever”: it praises Yahweh for creation, for striking down Egypt’s firstborn, dividing the sea, leading his people through the wilderness and giving them their land, and for remembering us in our low estate.

137.title: By the Rivers of Babylon
137.context: A psalm of the exile: by the rivers of Babylon the captives weep at the memory of Zion, hang up their harps and vow never to forget Jerusalem; the closing lines voice fierce cries against their enemies.

138.title: A Thankful Heart
138.context: A psalm of David giving wholehearted thanks to Yahweh, who answered his prayer and strengthened him; though exalted, Yahweh regards the lowly and will fulfill his purpose for him.

139.title: You Have Searched Me and Known Me
139.context: A psalm of David: Yahweh has searched and known him, every movement and thought; there is nowhere to flee from God’s Spirit; he was fearfully and wonderfully made; he ends asking God to search his heart and lead him in the everlasting way.

140.title: Rescue Me from Evil Men
140.context: A psalm of David: rescue me from the wicked; they make their tongues sharp as a serpent’s, and the poison of vipers is on their lips. He tells Yahweh, “You are my God,” and trusts that Yahweh secures justice for the poor, so the righteous praise his name. Paul quotes verse 3 in Romans 3:13.

141.title: Come Quickly to Me
141.context: A psalm of David asking that his prayer rise like incense and his raised hands like the evening sacrifice; he asks Yahweh to guard his mouth and keep his heart from evil, and welcomes the correction of the righteous.

142.title: I Lift My Voice to Yahweh
142.context: A maskil of David, a prayer in the cave: he pours out his complaint to Yahweh, with no one caring for his life; Yahweh is his refuge and portion in the land of the living, and he asks to be set free from prison.

143.title: I Stretch Out My Hands to You
143.context: A psalm of David asking Yahweh to hear him and not bring him into judgment, for no one living is righteous before God; he stretches out his hands, thirsting like dry land, and asks God’s good Spirit to lead him on level ground.

144.title: Blessed Be Yahweh, My Rock
144.context: A psalm of David praising Yahweh his rock, who trains his hands for battle, marveling that God cares for mere mortals, and ending with a blessing on the people whose God is Yahweh.

145.title: I Will Exalt You, My God and King
145.context: A psalm of praise of David, an acrostic: “I will exalt you, my God the King”; Yahweh is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in love, and the eyes of all look to him; he opens his hand and satisfies the desires of every living thing, and is near to all who call on him in truth.

146.title: Praise Yahweh, O My Soul
146.context: With no title: “Praise Yahweh, my soul”; he will praise him all his life, not putting trust in princes, who return to the ground. Blessed are those whose help is the God of Jacob, who made heaven and earth; he upholds the oppressed, opens the eyes of the blind, and reigns forever.

147.title: It Is Good to Sing Praises
147.context: With no title: how good it is to sing praises to our God; Yahweh builds up Jerusalem and gathers the exiles of Israel, heals the brokenhearted, determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name, and delights in those who fear him.

148.title: Praise Yahweh from the Heavens
148.context: With no title: let the heavens, the angels, sun and moon, sea creatures, mountains, trees, beasts, birds, kings and all peoples, young and old, praise the name of Yahweh, for his name alone is exalted.

149.title: Sing to Yahweh a New Song
149.context: With no title: sing to Yahweh a new song; let Israel rejoice in their Maker and praise his name with dancing, for Yahweh takes delight in his people and crowns the humble with victory.

150.title: Let Everything That Has Breath Praise Yahweh
150.context: The final psalm: praise God in his sanctuary and in the heavens, with trumpet, harp, tambourine, dance and cymbals — let everything that has breath praise Yahweh.

1.title: The Beginning of Knowledge
1.context: The proverbs of Solomon, written to give wisdom and instruction and understanding; the foundation of the book is that the fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge.

1.title: The Enticement of Sin
1.context: A father urges his son not to join sinners who lie in wait for innocent blood; they are caught in their own trap.

1.title: Wisdom Calls Aloud
1.context: Wisdom cries aloud in the street and rebukes the simple for refusing to listen; when disaster comes they will call and get no answer, because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of Yahweh.

2.title: The Benefits of Wisdom
2.context: The father urges his son to receive his words and seek wisdom like silver, and then he will understand the fear of Yahweh, for Yahweh gives wisdom and will guard him from the way of the wicked and the adulteress.

3.title: Trust in Yahweh with All Your Heart
3.context: A father urges his son not to forget his teaching: trust in Yahweh with all your heart rather than your own understanding, acknowledge him in all your ways and he will direct your paths; honor him with your wealth and do not despise his discipline.

4.title: A Father’s Instruction
4.context: A father recalls the teaching he received as a boy and urges his sons to get wisdom and understanding, to embrace her and she will honor them; the path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining ever brighter.

5.title: Avoiding Immorality
5.context: A warning to keep away from the adulteress, whose lips drip honey but whose end is bitter as gall; drink water from your own cistern and rejoice in the wife of your youth.

6.title: Warnings against Foolishness
6.context: Warnings about surety for a neighbor, laziness, a scoundrel’s deceit, and the seven things Yahweh hates: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that rush to evil, a false witness, and one who stirs up conflict.

6.title: Warnings against Adultery
6.context: The son is to keep his father’s commands and not forsake his mother’s teaching, for they are a lamp and light and keep him from the adulterous woman; no one who sleeps with another man’s wife goes unpunished.

7.title: The Adulteress
7.context: The father looks out of his window and sees a young man without sense, enticed at night by a woman dressed as a prostitute, like an ox going to the slaughter; he warns his sons not to turn aside to her ways.

8.title: The Excellence of Wisdom
8.context: Wisdom calls out at the city gates and in the streets; she was present before God made the world, she loves those who love her, and whoever finds her finds life.

9.title: The Way of Wisdom
9.context: Wisdom builds her house and spreads a feast, inviting the simple to life; Folly also calls out, but her guests end up in the grave; the fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom.

10.title: Solomon’s Proverbs: The Wise Son
10.context: The proverbs of Solomon: short, two-line sayings contrasting the wise and the foolish, the righteous and the wicked, the diligent and the lazy, running to 22:16.

22.title: Thirty Sayings of the Wise — Saying 1
22.context: “The sayings of the wise”: listen to them so that your trust may be in Yahweh; do not exploit the poor or befriend one given to anger. This section resembles ancient Egyptian instruction literature.

24.title: Further Sayings of the Wise
24.context: More sayings of the wise: it is not good to show partiality in judging; an honest answer is like a kiss on the lips; do not testify against your neighbor without cause; and the field of the sluggard is overgrown with thorns.

25.title: More Proverbs of Solomon
25.context: These are also proverbs of Solomon, copied by the men of King Hezekiah of Judah; they cover the honor of kings, relationships and self-control, through chapter 29.

30.title: The Words of Agur
30.context: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh: he confesses his limitations, asks God for neither poverty nor riches, lest he disown God or steal, and lists things too wonderful to understand.

30.title: Other Proverbs
30.context: Further sayings of Agur: four things that are never satisfied, four stately things, four small but wise creatures, and the observation that stirring milk produces butter and stirring anger produces strife.

31.title: The Sayings for King Lemuel
31.context: The sayings of King Lemuel, taught to him by his mother: do not spend your strength on women or wine, but speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, judge fairly and defend the rights of the poor and needy.

31.title: The Virtues of a Noble Woman
31.context: An acrostic poem on the woman of strength and character: industrious, wise, caring for her household and generous to the poor, speaking with kindness and wisdom; a woman who fears Yahweh is to be praised.

1.title: Everything Is Futile
1.context: The Teacher declares that all is utterly meaningless and asks what people gain from their toil under the sun; generations come and go, everything repeats, and there is nothing new under the sun.

1.title: With Wisdom Comes Sorrow
1.context: The Teacher applies his mind to study all that is done under heaven and finds it a chasing after the wind; with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and the more knowledge, the more grief.

3.title: To Everything There Is a Season
3.context: There is a time for everything: a time to be born and a time to die, to weep and to laugh; God has made everything beautiful in its time and set eternity in the human heart, though no one can fathom what he has done.

3.title: From Dust to Dust
3.context: The Teacher sees wickedness in the place of judgment and says God will judge both the righteous and the wicked; humans and animals alike return to dust, and he asks who knows whether the human spirit rises upward while the animal’s goes down to the earth.

5.title: Approaching God with Fear
5.context: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God; go near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools. Do not be quick to speak, keep your vows, and “fear God.”

5.title: The Futility of Wealth
5.context: If you see the poor oppressed, do not be surprised; one official is over another. Whoever loves money never has enough, wealth is meaningless, and as a person comes naked from the womb, so he departs, taking nothing from his toil.

7.title: The Value of Wisdom
7.context: A good name is better than fine perfume; it is better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of feasting, for death is the destiny of everyone; wisdom is as good as an inheritance, and no one can straighten what God has made crooked.

8.title: Obey the King
8.context: Obey the king’s command, in view of your oath to God; the wise heart knows the proper time and procedure, but no one has power over the wind or the day of death.

8.title: Fear God
8.context: The Teacher observes that the wicked are sometimes buried with honor and that sentences for crime are slow to be carried out; yet he knows it will go well with those who fear God, and ill with the wicked who do not. He concludes that nothing is better under the sun than to eat, drink and be glad.

9.title: Wisdom Is Better than Strength
9.context: Wisdom is better than strength, yet the poor man’s wisdom is despised and his words ignored; wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

11.title: Cast Your Bread upon the Waters
11.context: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you may find it again; give portions to seven, even eight, for you do not know what disaster may come. Sow in the morning and evening, not knowing which will succeed.

11.title: Enjoy Your Years
11.context: Young man, be happy while you are young and follow your heart’s desires, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment; banish anxiety from your heart, for youth and the prime of life are fleeting.

12.title: The Whole Duty of Man
12.context: The Teacher taught knowledge and arranged many proverbs, and the words of the wise are like goads and firmly fixed nails; the conclusion of the matter is to fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of everyone, and God will judge every deed.

1.title: The Bride Confesses Her Love
1.context: The Song of Songs, Solomon’s: the bride calls for her beloved, whose love is better than wine, while the daughters of Jerusalem look on; the bridegroom in turn praises her beauty.

2.title: The Second Song
2.context: The bride hears the voice of her beloved, bounding over the mountains, inviting her to come away with him to enjoy the spring; “My beloved is mine and I am his.”

3.title: Solomon Arrives on His Wedding Day
3.context: A wedding procession of King Solomon comes up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, surrounded by sixty warriors, with the king wearing the crown his mother gave him on his wedding day.

5.title: The Bride and Her Beloved
5.context: The bride dreams that her beloved knocks at the door; when she rises to open it he is gone, and the watchmen of the city beat her as she searches. She describes him to the daughters of Jerusalem — his head is purest gold — and says, “This is my beloved, this is my friend.”

6.title: The Fifth Song
6.context: The bridegroom praises his bride again — beautiful as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, majestic as troops with banners — and tells her to turn her eyes away because they overwhelm him; her loveliness is without equal among the queens and concubines.

8.title: The Sixth Song
8.context: The bride leans on her beloved as she comes up from the wilderness and asks him to set her like a seal over his heart, for love is as strong as death and many waters cannot quench it; the song closes with her calling her beloved to hurry, like a gazelle on the mountains.

1.title: Judah’s Rebellion
1.context: Isaiah prophesies from Uzziah to Hezekiah; Yahweh opens with a charge that Judah knows him less than an ox knows its owner, rejects their empty sacrifices, calls them to wash and learn to do good, and promises that sins like scarlet can be made white as snow.

1.title: The Corruption of Zion
1.context: The faithful city has become a prostitute and her silver has become dross; Yahweh will purge away her impurities, restore her judges, and she will again be called the City of Righteousness.

2.title: The Mountain of the House of Yahweh
2.context: In the last days the mountain of Yahweh’s temple will be established as the highest of the mountains, and all nations will stream to it; they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks and not train for war anymore.

2.title: The Day of Reckoning
2.context: Yahweh’s people have abandoned him and are full of idols; a day is coming against everything proud and lofty, when people will hide in caves from the dread of Yahweh and the splendor of his majesty.

3.title: Judgment on Jerusalem and Judah
3.context: The Lord Yahweh is about to take away from Jerusalem and Judah every support — food and water, warrior and judge, prophet and elder — and boys will be their officials.

3.title: Yahweh Judges His People
3.context: Yahweh rises to contend and stands to judge his people; he charges the elders and leaders with ruining his vineyard and crushing the poor.

3.title: A Warning to the Daughters of Zion
3.context: The women of Zion are haughty, walking with outstretched necks; Yahweh will bring sores on their heads, replace perfume with a stench and fine clothes with sackcloth.

4.title: A Remnant in Zion
4.context: In that day the Branch of Yahweh will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride of the survivors in Israel; those left in Zion will be called holy, and Yahweh will create over Mount Zion a canopy of cloud by day and fire by night.

5.title: The Song of the Vineyard
5.context: Isaiah sings a song for his beloved about a vineyard: Yahweh tended it with every care, yet it yielded only bad fruit. The vineyard of Yahweh of hosts is the house of Israel — he looked for justice but saw bloodshed, for righteousness but heard cries of distress.

5.title: Woes to the Wicked
5.context: Six woes follow: on those who add house to house and field to field, who rise early for strong drink, who drag sin along with cords, who call evil good and good evil, who are wise in their own eyes, and who are heroes at drinking wine.

6.title: Isaiah’s Commission
6.context: In the year King Uzziah dies, Isaiah sees the Lord enthroned on high, with seraphim crying out Yahweh’s holiness; a burning coal cleanses his lips, he answers, “Here am I, send me,” and is sent to a people whose hearts are hardened.

7.title: A Message to Ahaz
7.context: When Aram and Israel march against Jerusalem, King Ahaz panics; Isaiah, taking his son, tells him not to fear, for their plan will fail, but warns that unless he stands firm in faith he will not stand at all.

7.title: The Sign of Immanuel
7.context: Yahweh invites Ahaz to ask for a sign, and when he refuses, Yahweh himself gives one: the virgin (or young woman) will conceive and give birth to a son and call him Immanuel, “God with us.” Matthew 1:22–23 quotes this verse about the birth of Jesus.

8.title: Assyrian Invasion Prophesied
8.context: Yahweh tells Isaiah to name his newborn son Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz — “quick to plunder, swift to spoil” — as a sign that before the boy can say “my father,” Assyria will carry off the wealth of Damascus and Samaria.

8.title: The King of Assyria Is Coming
8.context: Because the people reject the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, the Lord will bring the mighty flood of the king of Assyria over Judah, reaching up to the neck; yet the nations are told, “God is with us.”

8.title: A Call to Fear God
8.context: Yahweh warns Isaiah not to follow the people’s way or fear what they fear, but to regard Yahweh of hosts as holy and fear him alone; he will be a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling.

8.title: Do Not Consult the Dead
8.context: Isaiah seals up the testimony among his disciples and waits for Yahweh, who is hiding his face; when people say to consult mediums and spiritists, he asks whether a people should not inquire of their God, and points them to the law and the testimony.

8.title: Darkness and Light
8.context: Distressed and hungry, the people curse their king and their God; whichever way they look, they see only distress and darkness and fearful gloom.

9.title: Unto Us a Child Is Born
9.context: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; a child is born to us who will bear the government and reign on David’s throne with justice and righteousness forever. Readers understand his titles in different ways. Matthew 4:15–16 quotes the opening lines.

9.title: Judgment against Israel’s Pride
9.context: The Lord sends a word against Jacob and it falls on Israel; the people of Ephraim and Samaria say in pride that they will rebuild with dressed stone, but Yahweh strikes them, and because the people do not return to him his hand is still upraised in a refrain through the chapter.

10.title: Judgment on Assyria
10.context: Assyria, the rod of Yahweh’s anger, is sent against a godless nation; but the king boasts of his own strength and wisdom, and Yahweh asks whether an ax can raise itself above the one who swings it, promising to punish Assyria’s arrogance when he has finished his work against Mount Zion.

10.title: A Remnant Shall Return
10.context: In that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of Jacob will no longer rely on him who struck them but truly rely on Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel; a remnant will return to the Mighty God (Paul cites this in Romans 9:27), for destruction has been decreed, overwhelming with righteousness.

10.title: Yahweh Will Punish Assyria
10.context: Yahweh tells his people in Zion not to fear Assyria, for his anger will soon turn against it, as when he struck Midian.

10.title: The Invader Advances
10.context: The invader advances from the north — through Aiath, Migron, Geba and Nob — and shakes his fist at Mount Zion; but the Lord Yahweh of hosts will lop off the boughs with great power, and the lofty trees of Lebanon will fall.

11.title: The Root of Jesse
11.context: A shoot will come from the stump of Jesse; the Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him with wisdom, counsel, might and the fear of Yahweh; he will judge the poor with justice, the wolf will live with the lamb, and the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh.

11.title: The Exiles Return Home
11.context: In that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples, and the nations will rally to him; the Lord will reach out a second time to reclaim the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Cush and the islands of the sea, and Ephraim’s jealousy will vanish.

12.title: Joyful Thanksgiving
12.context: In that day the redeemed will thank Yahweh because his anger has turned away and he comforts them; God is their salvation, and with joy they will draw water from the wells of salvation.

13.title: The Burden against Babylon
13.context: The prophecy concerning Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw: Yahweh’s day is near, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; he will stir up the Medes against Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, and she will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah.

14.title: Restoration for Israel
14.context: Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob and again choose Israel, settling them in their own land; foreigners will join them, and Israel will rule over their captors.

14.title: The Fall of the King of Babylon
14.context: Israel will taunt the fallen king of Babylon, the “morning star” who planned to ascend to heaven and make himself like the Most High, but is brought down to the realm of the dead.

14.title: God Will Destroy Babylon
14.context: “I will rise up against them,” declares Yahweh of hosts, and he will cut off from Babylon her name and survivors, offspring and descendants, making her a place for owls and swamps and sweeping her with the broom of destruction.

14.title: God’s Purpose against Assyria
14.context: Yahweh of hosts swears that what he has planned will happen: he will crush Assyria on his mountains; this is his purpose for the whole world, and no one can thwart it.

14.title: Philistia Will Be Destroyed
14.context: In the year King Ahaz died came this prophecy: Philistines, do not rejoice that the rod that struck you is broken, for out of the root of the snake will spring up a viper; the poor will find pasture, but Yahweh will destroy the Philistine root by famine, and the afflicted of his people will find refuge in Zion.

15.title: The Burden against Moab
15.context: A prophecy against Moab: Ar and Kir of Moab are ruined in a night; the people go up to the temple at Dibon to weep, every head is shaved and every beard cut off, and in the streets they wear sackcloth.

16.title: Moab’s Destruction
16.context: Moabite refugees seek shelter in Judah; the prophet foresees a faithful ruler on David’s throne who will judge justly, and laments Moab’s pride and coming ruin.
