24.context: Jesus tells them to learn from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and leaves appear, summer is near, and when they see all these things they will know he is near; heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will never pass away.

24.title: Readiness at Any Hour
24.context: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father; as in the days of Noah, people will be going about their lives until the Son of Man comes, so keep watch, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.

24.title: The Faithful and the Unfaithful Servant
24.context: Jesus asks who is the faithful and wise servant whom the master finds giving out food at the proper time and puts in charge of all his possessions; but if a wicked servant thinks the master is delayed and beats his fellow servants and drinks with drunkards, the master will return unexpectedly and punish him severely.

25.title: The Parable of the Ten Virgins
25.context: The kingdom is like ten virgins who take lamps to meet the bridegroom, five wise ones bringing oil and five foolish ones without; the bridegroom is delayed, and while the foolish go to buy oil he arrives, the ready ones go in to the feast and the door is shut; so keep watch, for you do not know the day or the hour.

25.title: The Parable of the Talents
25.context: A man going on a journey entrusts his servants with five, two and one talent according to their ability; those with five and two double their money and are praised as good and faithful servants, while the one who buried his talent is called wicked and lazy.

25.title: The Sheep and the Goats
25.context: When the Son of Man comes in glory, he will sit on his throne and separate the nations as a shepherd separates sheep from goats; he tells those on his right that whatever they did for the least of his brothers and sisters — the hungry, thirsty, stranger, naked, sick and imprisoned — they did for him.

26.title: The Plot to Kill Jesus
26.context: Jesus tells his disciples that the Passover is two days away and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified; meanwhile the chief priests and elders gather in the palace of the high priest Caiaphas and scheme to arrest Jesus secretly and kill him, but not during the festival, lest there be a riot.

26.title: Jesus Anointed at Bethany
26.context: At Bethany in the home of Simon the leper, a woman pours a jar of very expensive perfume on Jesus’ head; the disciples call it a waste, but Jesus says she has prepared his body for burial, and wherever the gospel is preached what she did will be told in her memory.

26.title: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus
26.context: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, goes to the chief priests and asks what they will give him to hand Jesus over; they count out thirty pieces of silver, and from then on he watches for an opportunity to betray him.

26.title: Preparing the Passover
26.context: On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread the disciples prepare the Passover as Jesus directs; that evening as they eat, he says one of them will betray him, and each asks, “Surely you don’t mean me, Lord?” When Judas asks, Jesus answers, “You have said so.”

26.title: The Institution of the Lord's Supper
26.context: At the Passover meal Jesus breaks bread and calls it his body, then gives the cup as his blood of the covenant poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. He says he will not drink it again until he drinks it new with them in his Father’s kingdom.

26.title: Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial
26.context: Jesus says the disciples will all fall away that night, as Scripture says the shepherd will be struck and the sheep scattered, but after he is raised he will go ahead of them to Galilee; when Peter insists he never will, Jesus says that before the rooster crows Peter will deny him three times.

26.title: Jesus Prays at Gethsemane
26.context: In Gethsemane Jesus is deeply grieved, asks Peter, James and John to keep watch, and prays facedown: if possible, let this cup pass from him, yet not as he wills but as the Father wills; three times he returns and finds them sleeping, saying the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak.

26.title: The Betrayal of Jesus
26.context: Judas arrives with an armed crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; when a disciple draws a sword, Jesus tells him to put it away, saying his Father could send twelve legions of angels, but Scripture must be fulfilled. The disciples all flee.

26.title: Jesus before the Sanhedrin
26.context: The council seeks false testimony against Jesus; when the high priest puts him under oath to say whether he is the Christ, the Son of God, Jesus affirms it and says they will see the Son of Man at the right hand of Power, coming on the clouds. They condemn him and abuse him.

26.title: Peter Denies Jesus
26.context: Peter is sitting in the courtyard when a servant girl says he was with Jesus of Galilee; he denies it before them all, and twice more, finally calling down curses and swearing, “I don’t know the man!” Immediately a rooster crows, and Peter remembers Jesus’ words and goes outside and weeps bitterly.

27.title: Jesus Delivered to Pilate
27.context: Early in the morning all the chief priests and elders decide to put Jesus to death; they bind him, lead him away and hand him over to Pilate the governor.

27.title: Judas Hangs Himself
27.context: When Judas sees Jesus condemned, he is seized with remorse and returns the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders, confessing he betrayed innocent blood; they dismiss him, so he throws the money into the temple and hangs himself, and the priests use it to buy the potter’s field, called the Field of Blood.

27.title: Jesus before Pilate
27.context: Jesus stands before the governor, who asks, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He replies, “You have said so,” but when accused by the chief priests and elders he gives no answer, not even to a single charge, to the great amazement of the governor.

27.title: The Crowd Chooses Barabbas
27.context: By festival custom Pilate asks whether to release Barabbas or Jesus; stirred by the chief priests, the crowd chooses Barabbas and demands crucifixion. Pilate washes his hands to declare himself innocent and hands Jesus over after flogging him.

27.title: The Soldiers Mock Jesus
27.context: The governor’s soldiers take Jesus into their headquarters, strip him, put a scarlet robe on him, twist together a crown of thorns for his head and a staff in his hand, kneel in mockery hailing him as king of the Jews, spit on him and strike his head.

27.title: The Crucifixion
27.context: Soldiers force Simon of Cyrene to carry Jesus’ cross; at Golgotha they crucify him, cast lots for his clothes and place above his head the charge “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews”; passersby, chief priests and the robbers crucified with him mock him for saving others but not himself.

27.title: The Death of Jesus
27.context: Darkness covers the land from noon to three; Jesus cries out the words of Psalm 22, asking why God has forsaken him, and dies. The temple curtain tears in two, the earth shakes, and the centurion says he truly was the Son of God.

27.title: The Burial of Jesus
27.context: As evening approaches, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, himself a disciple of Jesus, asks Pilate for the body, wraps it in clean linen and places it in his own new tomb cut out of the rock, rolling a big stone in front of the entrance; Mary Magdalene and the other Mary are sitting there opposite the tomb.

27.title: The Guards at the Tomb
27.context: The next day the chief priests and Pharisees go to Pilate, recalling that Jesus said he would rise after three days, and ask that the tomb be secured until then so that the disciples cannot steal the body; Pilate gives them a guard, and they seal the stone and post the guard.

28.title: The Resurrection
28.context: Early on the first day of the week the two Marys come to the tomb, and an angel tells them Jesus has risen as he said; as they hurry to tell the disciples, Jesus meets them and sends word for his brothers to go to Galilee.

28.title: The Report of the Guards
28.context: The guards report everything to the chief priests, who, after consulting the elders, pay the soldiers a large sum to say the disciples stole the body at night, and this story is still told among the Jews to this day.

28.title: The Great Commission
28.context: On a mountain in Galilee the disciples bow down before Jesus; he says all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to him and sends them to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching them to obey his commands, promising to be with them always.

1.title: The Mission of John the Baptist
1.context: Mark opens abruptly, using words from Malachi and Isaiah to introduce John the Baptist, who preaches a baptism of repentance in the wilderness, wears camel hair and eats locusts and wild honey, and says one greater is coming who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.

1.title: Jesus Is Baptized
1.context: Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptized by John; as he comes up from the water he sees heaven torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove, and a voice says he is the beloved Son with whom God is pleased.

1.title: The Temptation and Preaching of Jesus
1.context: At once the Spirit sends Jesus into the wilderness, where he is tempted by Satan for forty days, with the wild animals, and angels attend him.

1.title: Jesus Begins His Ministry in Galilee
1.context: After John is imprisoned, Jesus goes into Galilee proclaiming God’s good news: the time has come, the kingdom of God is near, repent and believe the good news.

1.title: The First Disciples
1.context: By the Sea of Galilee Jesus calls the fishermen Simon and Andrew, promising to make them fishers of people; they immediately leave their nets, and James and John leave their father to follow him too.

1.title: Jesus Expels an Unclean Spirit
1.context: In the Capernaum synagogue Jesus teaches with an authority that amazes people; a man with an unclean spirit cries out that he knows Jesus is the Holy One of God, Jesus orders the spirit out, and his fame spreads through Galilee.

1.title: Jesus Heals at Peter’s House
1.context: Jesus heals Simon’s mother-in-law of a fever; at sunset the whole town gathers at the door, and he heals many and drives out demons, not letting the demons speak because they know who he is.

1.title: Jesus Prays and Preaches
1.context: Very early, while it is still dark, Jesus goes to a solitary place to pray; when the disciples find him, he says they must go on to the nearby villages so he can preach there too, “That is why I have come.”

1.title: The Leper’s Prayer
1.context: A man with leprosy begs Jesus, who, moved with compassion, touches him and says, “I am willing. Be clean!” He tells him to show himself to the priest and say nothing, but the man spreads the news, so Jesus can no longer enter a town openly.

2.title: Jesus Heals a Paralytic
2.context: Four men lower a paralyzed man through the roof; Jesus says, “Son, your sins are forgiven,” and when the scribes object in their hearts, he tells the man to take his mat and go home, so that they may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.

2.title: Jesus Calls Levi
2.context: Jesus calls Levi from his tax booth and Levi follows, then hosts a meal for Jesus with many tax collectors and sinners; when the scribes object, Jesus says he came to call not the righteous but sinners.

2.title: Questions about Fasting
2.context: People ask why Jesus’ disciples do not fast; he answers with the bridegroom, the new patch on an old garment and new wine in old wineskins.

2.title: The Lord of the Sabbath
2.context: When the disciples pick grain on the Sabbath and the Pharisees object, Jesus cites David eating the consecrated bread and says the Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath, so the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.

3.title: Jesus Heals on the Sabbath
3.context: In the synagogue on the Sabbath Jesus heals a man with a shriveled hand, asking whether it is lawful on the Sabbath to do good or evil, to save life or to kill; the Pharisees go out and plot with the Herodians how to kill him.

3.title: Jesus Heals the Multitudes
3.context: Jesus withdraws to the lake, and large crowds follow from Galilee, Judea, Idumea, beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon; he heals many, and whenever impure spirits see him they cry out, “You are the Son of God,” but he orders them not to tell who he is.

3.title: The Twelve Apostles
3.context: Jesus goes up a mountain and appoints twelve to be with him, to be sent out to preach and to have authority to drive out demons; their names are listed.

3.title: A House Divided
3.context: Jesus’ family go to take charge of him, saying he is out of his mind, and teachers of the law from Jerusalem say he is possessed by Beelzebul; Jesus answers that a divided kingdom cannot stand and that whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven.

3.title: Jesus’ Mother and Brothers
3.context: Jesus’ mother and brothers come looking for him; looking at those seated around him, he says that whoever does God’s will is his brother, sister and mother.

4.title: The Parable of the Sower
4.context: Sitting in a boat by the lake, Jesus teaches the parable of the sower: seed falling on the path, on rocky places, among thorns and on good soil.

4.title: The Purpose of Jesus’ Parables
4.context: When the disciples ask about the parables, Jesus says the secret of the kingdom of God has been given to them, but to those outside everything is said in parables, so that they may be ever seeing but never perceiving.

4.title: The Parable of the Sower Explained
4.context: Jesus explains the sower: the farmer sows the word, and the four soils are four ways people hear it.

4.title: The Lesson of the Lamp
4.context: Jesus says a lamp is not put under a basket but on a stand, and nothing hidden will stay hidden; the measure people use will be measured back to them.

4.title: The Seed Growing Secretly
4.context: The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed; night and day it sprouts and grows, though he does not know how, and the soil produces grain all by itself until the harvest.

4.title: The Parable of the Mustard Seed
4.context: The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, which grows into the largest of garden plants, with branches where the birds can perch in its shade.

4.title: Jesus Teaches in Parables
4.context: With many similar parables Jesus speaks the word to them as much as they can understand; he does not speak without a parable, but explains everything privately to his disciples.

4.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
4.context: Crossing the lake, a fierce storm arises while Jesus sleeps on a cushion in the stern; the disciples wake him, he rebukes the wind and waves and the sea grows calm, and he asks why they have no faith. They ask one another who this is, whom even wind and sea obey.

5.title: The Demons and the Pigs
5.context: In the region of the Gerasenes a man living among tombs and possessed by many demons runs to Jesus; the demons, calling themselves Legion, beg to enter a herd of pigs, which rush into the lake and drown. The healed man is sent home to tell what the Lord has done for him.

5.title: The Healing Touch of Jesus
5.context: Jairus, a synagogue leader, begs Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman bleeding for twelve years touches Jesus’ cloak and is healed. Word comes that the girl has died, but Jesus says not to fear, only believe, and takes her hand and raises her up.

6.title: The Rejection at Nazareth
6.context: In his hometown Jesus teaches in the synagogue, and the people take offense: “Isn’t this the carpenter?” He could do no miracles there except heal a few sick people, and he is amazed at their lack of faith.

6.title: The Ministry of the Twelve
6.context: Jesus sends the twelve out two by two with authority over impure spirits, taking nothing for the journey except a staff; they preach repentance, drive out many demons and anoint many sick people with oil and heal them.

6.title: The Beheading of John
6.context: King Herod hears of Jesus and thinks John the Baptist has risen from the dead; the account tells how Herod had John imprisoned on account of Herodias and, bound by his oath at his birthday banquet, had him beheaded.

6.title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
6.context: The apostles return and Jesus takes them to a quiet place to rest, but a large crowd gets there first; he has compassion on them, because they are like sheep without a shepherd, and feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish, with twelve basketfuls left over.

6.title: Jesus Walks on Water
6.context: Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up to pray; at night he walks on the sea toward them as they strain against the wind, tells them to take heart, and the wind stops when he gets in. Their hearts are hardened, and they have not understood about the loaves.

6.title: Jesus Heals at Gennesaret
6.context: At Gennesaret people recognize Jesus and carry the sick on mats wherever he goes, placing them in the marketplaces and begging to touch even the edge of his cloak, and all who touch it are healed.

7.title: The Tradition of the Elders
7.context: The Pharisees ask why the disciples eat without ritually washing as tradition requires; quoting Isaiah, Jesus says they abandon God’s command to hold to human tradition, and that nothing entering from outside defiles a person, only the evil that comes from the heart. Mark notes that he thereby declared all foods clean.

7.title: The Faith of the Gentile Woman
7.context: In the region of Tyre a Greek woman of Syrophoenician birth asks Jesus to drive a demon from her daughter; when he says the children should be fed first, she replies that even the dogs eat the children’s crumbs, and because of that answer he tells her the demon has left her daughter.

7.title: The Deaf and Mute Man
7.context: In the Decapolis people bring a deaf man who can hardly speak; Jesus takes him aside, puts his fingers in his ears, touches his tongue with spittle, looks up to heaven and sighs, saying “Ephphatha” (be opened), and his ears are opened and his tongue released.

8.title: The Feeding of the Four Thousand
8.context: Again a large crowd gathers with nothing to eat; Jesus has compassion on them and with seven loaves and a few small fish feeds about four thousand, with seven basketfuls left over.

8.title: The Demand for a Sign
8.context: The Pharisees demand a sign from heaven to test Jesus; sighing deeply, he says no sign will be given to this generation and leaves them.

8.title: The Leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod
8.context: The disciples have forgotten to bring bread, and Jesus warns them to watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod; they think he means bread, and he reminds them of the two feedings and asks, “Do you still not understand?”

8.title: The Blind Man at Bethsaida
8.context: At Bethsaida some people bring a blind man; Jesus leads him outside the village, spits on his eyes and puts his hands on him, and the man sees people like trees walking around; Jesus lays hands on him again, and his sight is fully restored.

8.title: Peter’s Confession of Christ
8.context: On the road to Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks who people say he is and who the disciples say he is; Peter answers that he is the Christ, and Jesus warns them not to tell anyone.

8.title: Christ’s Passion Foretold
8.context: Jesus plainly teaches that the Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, be killed and rise after three days; when Peter rebukes him, Jesus rebukes Peter and says his followers must deny themselves and take up their cross, for whoever loses their life for him will save it.

9.title: The Transfiguration
9.context: Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain and is transfigured, his clothes dazzling white, as Elijah and Moses talk with him; a voice from the cloud says this is the beloved Son, listen to him, and on the way down Jesus tells them to say nothing until he has risen from the dead.

9.title: The Boy with an Evil Spirit
9.context: A father brings his son with a mute spirit that the disciples could not drive out; when he asks Jesus to help if he can, Jesus says everything is possible for one who believes, and the father cries, “I believe; help my unbelief!” Jesus casts out the spirit and says this kind comes out only by prayer.

9.title: The Second Prediction of the Passion
9.context: Passing through Galilee, Jesus teaches his disciples that the Son of Man will be delivered into human hands, killed, and after three days rise; they do not understand and are afraid to ask him about it.

9.title: The Greatest in the Kingdom
9.context: On the road the disciples argue about who is the greatest; Jesus says anyone who wants to be first must be last and servant of all, and taking a little child in his arms says that whoever welcomes one of these children in his name welcomes him, and whoever welcomes him welcomes the one who sent him.

9.title: Whoever Is Not against Us Is for Us
9.context: John says they stopped someone driving out demons in Jesus’ name because he was not one of them; Jesus says not to stop him, for whoever is not against us is for us, and even someone who gives them a cup of water will be rewarded.

9.title: Temptations and Trespasses
9.context: Jesus warns that causing one of these little ones who believe to stumble is a grave sin; if a hand, foot or eye causes one to sin, it is better to remove it than go to hell; salt that loses its saltiness is useless, so they should be at peace with one another.

10.title: Teachings about Divorce
10.context: Pharisees test Jesus about divorce; he says Moses permitted it because of their hard hearts, but at the beginning of creation God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh, so what God has joined together let no one separate; anyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.

10.title: Jesus Blesses the Children
10.context: People bring children for Jesus to touch, and the disciples rebuke them; Jesus is indignant, says to let the children come, for whoever does not receive God’s kingdom like a child will never enter it, and takes them in his arms and blesses them.

10.title: The Rich Man
10.context: A man asks how to inherit eternal life; Jesus looks at him with love and tells him to sell everything, give to the poor and follow him, and he leaves sad. Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter God’s kingdom, but all things are possible with God.

10.title: The Third Prediction of the Passion
10.context: On the road up to Jerusalem Jesus walks ahead while the disciples are astonished and afraid; for the third time he tells them the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the Gentiles, mocked, flogged and killed, and will rise after three days.

10.title: The Request of James and John
10.context: James and John ask to sit at Jesus’ right and left in his glory; Jesus says that rulers of the nations lord it over others, but among his followers whoever wants to be great must be the servant of all, for the Son of Man came to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.

10.title: Jesus Heals Bartimaeus
10.context: As Jesus leaves Jericho, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus shouts, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” and keeps shouting when rebuked; Jesus calls him and asks what he wants, and he says, “Rabbi, I want to see.” “Go, your faith has healed you,” and immediately he receives his sight and follows Jesus along the road.

11.title: The Triumphal Entry
11.context: Jesus sends disciples for a colt no one has ridden and rides it into Jerusalem; people spread cloaks and branches on the road, shouting hosanna, blessing the one who comes in the Lord’s name and the coming kingdom of David.

11.title: Jesus Curses the Fig Tree
11.context: Hungry, Jesus sees a fig tree in leaf but finds no fruit on it, since it was not the season for figs; he says no one will ever eat fruit from it again, and the disciples hear him.

11.title: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
11.context: Jesus enters the temple, drives out the traders, overturns the money changers’ tables and stops people carrying goods through, saying Scripture calls God’s house a house of prayer for all nations but they have made it a den of robbers; the chief priests and scribes begin looking for a way to kill him.

11.title: The Withered Fig Tree
11.context: The next morning the disciples see the fig tree withered from the roots; Jesus tells them to have faith in God, for whatever they ask in prayer believing they have received it will be theirs, and when they pray they must forgive anyone they hold something against.

11.title: Jesus’ Authority Challenged
11.context: The chief priests, scribes and elders ask by what authority Jesus is doing these things; he asks whether John’s baptism was from heaven or of human origin, and when they reply, “We don’t know,” he refuses to tell them by what authority he acts.

12.title: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
12.context: Jesus tells the parable of tenants who kill the owner’s servants and beloved son, quoting the psalm about the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone; the leaders realize the parable is aimed at them and want to arrest him but fear the crowd.

12.title: Paying Taxes to Caesar
12.context: Pharisees and Herodians try to trap Jesus by asking whether to pay taxes to Caesar; he has them bring a denarius and says to give Caesar what is Caesar’s and God what is God’s, and they are amazed.

12.title: The Sadducees and the Resurrection
12.context: The Sadducees mock the resurrection with a widow married to seven brothers; Jesus says the risen do not marry, and from the burning bush passage shows that God, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, is the God of the living.

12.title: The Greatest Commandment
12.context: A scribe asks which commandment is greatest; Jesus quotes the Shema — the Lord our God is one Lord — and says to love him with all one’s being and one’s neighbor as oneself. The scribe agrees that God is one with no other besides him, and Jesus says he is not far from God’s kingdom.

12.title: Whose Son Is the Christ?
12.context: Teaching in the temple, Jesus asks how the scribes can say the Christ is David’s son when David, speaking by the Spirit in Psalm 110:1, calls him Lord; the large crowd listens to him with delight.

12.title: Beware of the Scribes
12.context: Jesus warns, “Watch out for the scribes,” who like to walk around in flowing robes, be greeted with respect in the marketplaces, and have the most important seats in synagogues and the places of honor at banquets; they devour widows’ houses and for a show make lengthy prayers, and they will be punished most severely.

12.title: The Widow’s Offering
12.context: Jesus watches people putting money into the temple treasury; many rich people give large amounts, but a poor widow puts in two small coins, and he says she has given more than all the others, for they gave from their abundance while she gave all she had to live on.

13.title: Temple Destruction and Other Signs
13.context: A disciple admires the temple’s massive stones and buildings, and Jesus says not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.

13.title: The Beginning of Birth Pains
13.context: Four disciples ask privately when these things will happen; Jesus says wars, earthquakes and famines are only the beginning of birth pains, they will be put on trial, but the gospel must first be preached to all nations, and those who endure will be saved.

13.title: The Abomination of Desolation
13.context: Jesus says that when they see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not, those in Judea must flee to the mountains; those days will bring unequaled distress, and false messiahs and prophets will perform signs to deceive, so they must be on guard.

13.title: The Return of the Son of Man
13.context: After that distress the sun will darken, the moon lose its light and the stars fall; then people will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory, and he will send angels to gather his elect from the four winds.

13.title: The Lesson of the Fig Tree
13.context: Jesus uses the fig tree as a lesson: when its branches grow tender and put out leaves, summer is near, and when these things happen they will know he is near; heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will not.

13.title: Readiness at Any Hour
13.context: No one knows that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven or the Son, but only the Father; so they must stay alert, like servants and a doorkeeper told to watch while their master is away, lest he come suddenly and find them asleep.

14.title: The Plot to Kill Jesus
14.context: Two days before Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the chief priests and scribes look for a cunning way to arrest Jesus and kill him, but not during the festival, for fear of a riot.

14.title: Jesus Anointed at Bethany
14.context: At Bethany a woman breaks an alabaster jar and pours very costly perfume on Jesus’ head; some call it waste, but Jesus says she has anointed his body in advance for burial, and wherever the gospel goes her deed will be told.

14.title: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus
14.context: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, goes to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them; they are delighted and promise him money, and he watches for an opportunity to hand him over.

14.title: Preparing the Passover
14.context: On the first day of Unleavened Bread Jesus sends two disciples into the city, where a man carrying a water jar will lead them to a large furnished upper room to prepare the Passover; during the meal Jesus says one of them will betray him.

14.title: The Institution of the Lord's Supper
14.context: While they eat, Jesus takes bread, blesses and breaks it and says this is his body; then he takes a cup, gives thanks, they all drink, and he says this is his blood of the covenant poured out for many; after singing a hymn they go out to the Mount of Olives.

14.title: Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial
14.context: Jesus says all the disciples will fall away, for it is written that the shepherd will be struck and the sheep scattered, but after he rises he will go ahead of them to Galilee; when Peter insists he will not, Jesus says that before the rooster crows twice that night Peter will deny him three times.

14.title: Jesus Prays at Gethsemane
14.context: In Gethsemane Jesus is deeply distressed and falls to the ground praying: Abba, Father, everything is possible for you, take this cup from me, yet not what I will but what you will; three times he returns and finds the disciples asleep.

14.title: The Betrayal of Jesus
14.context: Judas arrives with men sent by the chief priests and betrays Jesus with a kiss; someone cuts off the high priest’s servant’s ear; Jesus asks why they come against him with swords as if he were a robber when he taught daily in the temple, but the Scriptures must be fulfilled, and all the disciples flee.

14.title: The Young Man Who Fled
14.context: A young man wearing nothing but a linen garment is following Jesus; when they seize him, he flees naked, leaving his garment behind — a detail only Mark records.

14.title: Jesus before the Sanhedrin
14.context: The council seeks testimony to put Jesus to death, but the false witnesses do not agree; when the high priest asks whether he is the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One, Jesus says, “I am,” and that they will see the Son of Man at the right hand of Power, coming with the clouds of heaven, and they all condemn him.

14.title: Peter Denies Jesus
14.context: Warming himself in the courtyard, Peter is recognized by a servant girl and denies it; challenged twice more, he swears with curses that he does not know the man; immediately the rooster crows a second time, Peter remembers Jesus’ words and breaks down weeping.

15.title: Jesus Delivered to Pilate
15.context: Very early in the morning the chief priests, elders, scribes and the whole Sanhedrin reach a decision; they bind Jesus, lead him away and hand him over to Pilate, who asks, “Are you the king of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replies, but he makes no reply to the many accusations, and Pilate is amazed.

15.title: The Crowd Chooses Barabbas
15.context: By festival custom Pilate releases a prisoner, knowing the chief priests handed Jesus over out of envy; they stir up the crowd to ask for Barabbas, and the crowd shouts for Jesus to be crucified; wanting to satisfy them, Pilate releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over to be flogged and crucified.

15.title: The Soldiers Mock Jesus
15.context: The soldiers lead Jesus into the governor’s headquarters, call the whole company together, dress him in purple, put a crown of thorns on him and salute him as king of the Jews, strike his head with a staff, spit on him and kneel in mock homage, then lead him out to crucify him.

15.title: The Crucifixion
15.context: The soldiers force Simon of Cyrene, father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry Jesus’ cross; at Golgotha they offer him wine mixed with myrrh, which he refuses, and crucify him under the charge “The King of the Jews”; passersby and chief priests mock him for saving others but not himself.

15.title: The Death of Jesus
15.context: From noon until three darkness covers the land; Jesus cries out, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” — my God, my God, why have you forsaken me? — then with a loud cry breathes his last, and the temple curtain tears from top to bottom; the centurion says this man was truly the Son of God, while women watch from a distance.

15.title: The Burial of Jesus
15.context: That evening, the Day of Preparation, Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member, boldly asks Pilate for Jesus’ body; after confirming with the centurion that Jesus is dead, Pilate grants it, and Joseph wraps the body in linen, lays it in a tomb cut from rock and rolls a stone against the entrance.

16.title: The Resurrection
16.context: Early after the Sabbath the women find the tomb’s stone rolled away, and a young man in white tells them Jesus has risen and they should tell the disciples and Peter to go to Galilee; afraid, they say nothing. The earliest manuscripts end at verse 8.

16.title: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
16.context: (This and the following sections are not found in the earliest manuscripts.) Early on the first day of the week Jesus first appears to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven seven demons; she tells those who had been with him, but when they hear that he is alive and she has seen him, they do not believe it.

16.title: Jesus Appears to Two Disciples
16.context: Afterward Jesus appears in a different form to two of them while they are walking in the country; they return and report it to the rest, but they do not believe them either.

16.title: The Great Commission
16.context: Jesus appears to the eleven, rebukes their unbelief and sends them into all the world with the gospel: whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, and signs will follow believers. This section (16:9–20) is absent from the earliest manuscripts.

16.title: The Ascension
16.context: After the Lord Jesus has spoken to them, he is taken up into heaven and sits at the right hand of God; the disciples go out and preach everywhere, and the Lord works with them and confirms his word by the signs that accompany it.

1.title: Dedication to Theophilus
1.context: Luke explains that, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, he writes an orderly account for Theophilus so that he may know the certainty of what he has been taught.

1.title: Gabriel Foretells John’s Birth
1.context: The priest Zechariah and his wife Elizabeth are old and childless; while he burns incense in the temple, the angel Gabriel promises them a son named John, and because Zechariah doubts, he is struck mute.

1.title: Gabriel Foretells Jesus’ Birth
1.context: Gabriel is sent to the virgin Mary in Nazareth: the Holy Spirit will come on her and the power of the Most High will overshadow her; she will bear a son named Jesus, called Son of the Most High and Son of God, who will reign on David’s throne. Mary answers, “May your word to me be fulfilled.”

1.title: Mary Visits Elizabeth
1.context: Mary visits Elizabeth; at her greeting the baby leaps in Elizabeth’s womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, calls Mary blessed.

1.title: Mary’s Song
1.context: At Elizabeth’s home Mary magnifies the Lord for regarding her lowliness; she praises God who brings down rulers and lifts up the humble, fills the hungry and remembers his mercy promised to Abraham. She stays about three months.

1.title: The Birth of John the Baptist
1.context: Elizabeth gives birth to a son; when relatives want to name him Zechariah, his father writes, “His name is John,” and his mouth is opened.

1.title: Zechariah’s Song
1.context: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Zechariah praises the God of Israel for raising up a horn of salvation in David’s house, and says his child will be called a prophet of the Most High to prepare the way for the Lord.

2.title: The Birth of Jesus
2.context: When Caesar Augustus orders a census while Quirinius governs Syria, Joseph goes with Mary to Bethlehem, where she gives birth to her firstborn son and lays him in a manger, because there is no guest room.

2.title: The Shepherds and the Angels
2.context: An angel announces to shepherds in the fields that a Savior has been born in the town of David, the Messiah, the Lord; a heavenly host praises God, and the shepherds go and find the baby.

2.title: Jesus Presented at the Temple
2.context: When the days of purification are over, Jesus is presented at the temple; the righteous Simeon and the prophet Anna recognize him, and Simeon praises God for the salvation he has seen, a light for the Gentiles.

2.title: The Return to Nazareth
2.context: Having done everything the law required, Joseph and Mary return to Nazareth; the child grows and becomes strong, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God is on him.

2.title: The Boy Jesus at the Temple
2.context: At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple courts after Passover, listening to the teachers and asking questions; he tells his parents he had to be in his Father’s house, and he grows in wisdom and stature and in favor with God and people.

3.title: The Mission of John the Baptist
3.context: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar, God’s word comes to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness; he preaches a baptism of repentance, calls for fruit in keeping with it, and points to one more powerful who is coming.

3.title: The Baptism of Jesus
3.context: When all the people are baptized, Jesus is baptized too; as he prays, heaven opens, the Holy Spirit descends on him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice says he is the beloved Son with whom God is pleased.

3.title: The Genealogy of Jesus
3.context: Jesus is about thirty when he begins his ministry; Luke traces his genealogy back from Joseph through David and Abraham to Adam, “the son of God.”

4.title: The Temptation of Jesus
4.context: Full of the Holy Spirit, Jesus is led into the wilderness for forty days and tempted by the devil; he answers each time from Deuteronomy, and the devil leaves him until an opportune time.

4.title: Jesus Begins His Ministry
4.context: Jesus returns to Galilee in the power of the Spirit; news about him spreads, and he teaches in their synagogues.

4.title: The Rejection at Nazareth
4.context: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads Isaiah’s words about the Spirit of the Lord anointing him to preach good news to the poor and says they are fulfilled today; when he recalls Elijah and Elisha being sent to foreigners, the people try to throw him off a cliff, but he walks through the crowd.

4.title: Jesus Expels an Unclean Spirit
4.context: In Capernaum his words have authority; he rebukes an impure demon and it comes out of a man, and everyone is amazed.

4.title: Jesus Heals at Peter’s House
4.context: Jesus heals Simon’s mother-in-law of a high fever, and at sunset lays hands on many sick people and drives out many demons.

4.title: Jesus Preaches in Judea
4.context: At daybreak Jesus goes to a solitary place, and when the crowds try to keep him, he says he must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to other towns, for that is why he was sent.

5.title: The First Disciples
5.context: Jesus teaches from Simon’s boat, then tells him to put out into deep water and let down the nets; though they caught nothing all night, Simon obeys and the nets fill with fish. Falling at Jesus’ knees, Simon calls himself a sinner, and Jesus says from now on he will catch people; they leave everything and follow him.

5.title: The Leper’s Prayer
5.context: A man covered with leprosy begs Jesus, who touches him and makes him clean; news about Jesus spreads all the more, but he often withdraws to lonely places to pray.

5.title: Jesus Heals a Paralytic
5.context: Men lower a paralyzed man through the roof; Jesus forgives his sins and then tells him to get up and go home, so they may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, and everyone praises God.

5.title: Jesus Calls Levi
5.context: Jesus calls Levi the tax collector, who leaves everything and holds a great banquet for him; Jesus says he has not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

5.title: Questions about Fasting
5.context: Asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus answers with images of the bridegroom, new cloth on old garments and new wine in old wineskins.

6.title: The Lord of the Sabbath
6.context: When the disciples pick grain on a Sabbath, the Pharisees object; Jesus cites David and declares that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.

6.title: Jesus Heals on the Sabbath
6.context: On another Sabbath Jesus heals a man whose right hand is shriveled, asking whether it is lawful to do good or evil on the Sabbath; the scribes and Pharisees are furious.

6.title: The Twelve Apostles
6.context: Jesus spends the night praying to God on a mountainside, and in the morning chooses twelve of his disciples, whom he designates apostles.

6.title: Jesus Heals the Multitudes
6.context: Jesus comes down and stands on a level place with a great crowd from many regions who have come to hear him and be healed, for power is coming from him and healing them all.

6.title: The Beatitudes
6.context: Looking at his disciples, Jesus says blessed are the poor, the hungry, those who weep and those hated for the Son of Man’s sake; and woe to the rich, the well fed, those who laugh now and those whom everyone praises.

6.title: Love Your Enemies
6.context: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, pray for those who mistreat you; do to others as you would have them do to you, and be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

6.title: Judging Others
6.context: Do not judge and you will not be judged; forgive and you will be forgiven; give, and it will be given to you. A blind man cannot lead the blind; first take the plank out of your own eye.

6.title: A Tree and Its Fruit
6.context: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor a bad tree good fruit; a good person brings good out of the good stored in the heart, for the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.

6.title: The House on the Rock
6.context: Why call me “Lord, Lord” and not do what I say? Whoever hears and obeys is like a man who builds a house on rock; whoever hears and does not obey is like a man who builds without a foundation.

7.title: The Faith of the Centurion
7.context: A centurion in Capernaum, whose servant is ill, sends Jewish elders to ask Jesus’ help and then sends word that he need only say the word; Jesus says he has not found such great faith even in Israel, and the servant is healed.

7.title: Jesus Raises a Widow’s Son
7.context: At the gate of Nain Jesus meets the funeral of a widow’s only son; moved with compassion, he touches the bier and says, “Young man, I say to you, get up!” and the dead man sits up; the people praise God, saying a great prophet has appeared among them.

7.title: John’s Inquiry
7.context: John sends two disciples to ask, “Are you the one who is to come?” Jesus points to the blind seeing, the lame walking, the dead raised and the good news proclaimed to the poor, and praises John as the greatest born of women.

7.title: A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus
7.context: At the home of Simon the Pharisee, a sinful woman wets Jesus’ feet with her tears, wipes them with her hair and pours perfume on them; with a parable of two debtors, Jesus says her many sins are forgiven, as her great love shows.

8.title: Women Minister to Jesus
8.context: Jesus travels from town to town proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God, with the twelve and several women, including Mary Magdalene, Joanna and Susanna, who support them out of their own means.

8.title: The Parable of the Sower
8.context: Jesus tells the parable of the sower: seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil.

8.title: The Purpose of the Parables
8.context: When the disciples ask its meaning, Jesus says the knowledge of the secrets of the kingdom of God has been given to them, but to others he speaks in parables.

8.title: The Parable of the Sower Explained
8.context: Jesus explains: the seed is the word of God, and the four soils are four kinds of hearers; the good soil stands for those who hear the word, retain it with a noble and good heart, and by persevering produce a crop.

8.title: The Lesson of the Lamp
8.context: No one lights a lamp and hides it; it is put on a stand. So consider carefully how you listen, for whoever has will be given more.

8.title: Jesus’ Mother and Brothers
8.context: Jesus’ mother and brothers cannot reach him because of the crowd; when told, he says that his mother and brothers are those who hear God’s word and do it.

8.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
8.context: Crossing the lake, Jesus falls asleep; a squall comes down and the disciples wake him; he rebukes the wind and waves and all is calm, and he asks, “Where is your faith?”

8.title: The Demons and the Pigs
8.context: In the region of the Gerasenes Jesus drives a legion of demons out of a man into a herd of pigs, which rush into the lake; the man, clothed and in his right mind, is sent home to tell how much God has done for him.

8.title: The Healing Touch of Jesus
8.context: Jairus, a synagogue leader, begs Jesus to come to his dying daughter; on the way a woman who has bled for twelve years touches the edge of his cloak and is healed. Word comes that the girl is dead, but Jesus says, “Don’t be afraid; just believe,” takes her hand and raises her.

9.title: The Ministry of the Twelve
9.context: Jesus gives the twelve power and authority to drive out all demons and cure diseases, and sends them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.

9.title: Herod Tries to See Jesus
9.context: Herod the tetrarch is perplexed by reports about Jesus, since some say John has been raised from the dead; “I beheaded John. Who, then, is this?” and he tries to see him.

9.title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
9.context: The apostles return, and Jesus withdraws with them toward Bethsaida; the crowds follow, and he feeds about five thousand men with five loaves and two fish, with twelve basketfuls left over.

9.title: Peter’s Confession of Christ
9.context: While Jesus prays alone with his disciples, he asks who the crowds say he is, and who they say he is; Peter answers, “God’s Messiah.”

9.title: Christ’s Passion Foretold
9.context: Jesus warns them not to tell anyone and says the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected, be killed and on the third day be raised; whoever would follow him must deny themselves, take up their cross daily and follow him.

9.title: The Transfiguration
9.context: Jesus takes three disciples up a mountain to pray; as he prays his face changes and his clothes become dazzling white, and Moses and Elijah appear in glory, speaking of his departure to be fulfilled in Jerusalem. A voice from the cloud says this is the chosen Son; listen to him.

9.title: The Boy with an Evil Spirit
9.context: The next day a man begs Jesus to help his only son, seized by a spirit the disciples could not drive out; Jesus rebukes the impure spirit and heals the boy, and all are amazed at the greatness of God.

9.title: The Second Prediction of the Passion
9.context: Jesus tells his disciples that the Son of Man is going to be delivered into the hands of men, but they do not understand and are afraid to ask.

9.title: The Greatest in the Kingdom
9.context: When the disciples argue about who is greatest, Jesus stands a little child beside him and says that whoever welcomes this child in his name welcomes him, and the one who is least among them is the greatest.

9.title: Whoever Is Not against You Is for You
9.context: John says they stopped someone driving out demons in Jesus’ name because he did not follow with them; Jesus says not to stop him, for whoever is not against them is for them.

9.title: The Samaritans Reject Jesus
9.context: As the time approaches for him to be taken up to heaven, Jesus resolutely sets out for Jerusalem; when a Samaritan village does not welcome him, James and John want to call down fire, but Jesus rebukes them.

9.title: The Cost of Discipleship
9.context: Someone offers to follow Jesus wherever he goes; he answers that the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head, and that no one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for service in the kingdom of God.

10.title: Jesus Sends the Seventy-Two
10.context: Jesus appoints seventy others (some manuscripts say seventy-two) and sends them two by two ahead of him; the harvest is plentiful but workers few, so they should pray for more. They return rejoicing that even demons submit, but Jesus says to rejoice rather that their names are written in heaven.

10.title: Woe to the Unrepentant
10.context: Woe to Chorazin and Bethsaida, for if the miracles done there had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago; and Capernaum will go down to Hades.

10.title: The Joyful Return
10.context: The seventy-two return with joy, saying even the demons submit to them in his name; Jesus says he saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven, but tells them to rejoice not that the spirits submit but that their names are written in heaven.

10.title: Jesus’ Prayer of Thanksgiving
10.context: Full of joy through the Holy Spirit, Jesus thanks the Father for hiding these things from the wise and revealing them to little children; he tells the disciples they are blessed to see what they see, for many prophets and kings longed to see it and did not.

10.title: The Parable of the Good Samaritan
10.context: An expert in the law asks what he must do to inherit eternal life; he sums up the law as loving God wholeheartedly and loving his neighbor as himself, and when he asks, “Who is my neighbor?” Jesus tells the parable of the good Samaritan and says, “Go and do likewise.”

10.title: Martha and Mary
10.context: At Martha’s home Martha is distracted by her serving while her sister Mary sits at Jesus’ feet listening; when Martha complains, Jesus says she is anxious about many things but only one is needed, and Mary has chosen the better part.

11.title: The Lord’s Prayer
11.context: The disciples ask Jesus to teach them to pray, and he teaches them to ask that the Father’s name be holy, his kingdom come, and for daily bread and forgiveness; through the parable of a friend at midnight he says ask, seek and knock, for the Father will surely give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.

11.title: A House Divided
11.context: When Jesus drives out a mute demon, some say he does it by Beelzebul, prince of demons; he replies that a kingdom divided falls, and if he drives out demons by the finger of God, then God’s kingdom has come upon them; whoever is not with him is against him.

11.title: An Unclean Spirit Returns
11.context: When an impure spirit leaves someone and returns with seven spirits more wicked than itself, the final condition is worse than the first.

11.title: True Blessedness
11.context: A woman in the crowd calls out that the womb that bore him and the breasts that nursed him are blessed; Jesus replies that those who hear God’s word and keep it are more blessed still.

11.title: The Sign of Jonah
11.context: This is a wicked generation that asks for a sign, but none will be given except the sign of Jonah; and now something greater than Solomon and Jonah is here.

11.title: The Lamp of the Body
11.context: Your eye is the lamp of your body; when it is healthy your whole body is full of light, so see to it that the light within you is not darkness.

11.title: Woes to Pharisees and Experts in the Law
11.context: A Pharisee who invites Jesus to dinner is surprised that he does not wash before the meal; Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside of the cup while inside they are full of greed and wickedness, and pronounces woes on the Pharisees and experts in the law.

12.title: The Leaven of the Pharisees
12.context: Jesus warns his disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy; nothing covered up will stay hidden, and what is whispered in private will be proclaimed openly.

12.title: Fear God Alone
12.context: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body and can do no more; fear the one who has authority to throw into hell. Five sparrows are sold for two pennies, yet not one is forgotten by God, and you are worth more than many sparrows.

12.title: Confessing Christ
12.context: Whoever acknowledges the Son of Man before others will be acknowledged before the angels of God; when brought before synagogues and authorities, do not worry what to say, for the Holy Spirit will teach them at that time what they should say.

12.title: The Parable of the Rich Fool
12.context: When someone asks Jesus to make his brother divide the inheritance, Jesus warns against all greed, for life does not consist in possessions; he tells of a rich man who plans bigger barns, but God says his life will be demanded that night — so it is with those who store up for themselves but are not rich toward God.

12.title: Do Not Worry
12.context: Jesus tells his disciples not to worry about food or clothing, for God cares for ravens and lilies; seek his kingdom and these things will be added. Little flock, do not be afraid, for the Father is pleased to give them the kingdom; they should sell possessions, give to the poor and store up treasure in heaven.

12.title: Readiness at Any Hour
12.context: Be dressed ready for service and keep your lamps burning, like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet; the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect, and the faithful and wise manager will be put in charge of all his possessions.

12.title: Not Peace but Division
12.context: “I have come to bring fire on the earth”; Jesus has a baptism to undergo and is distressed until it is completed; he has not come to bring peace but division, even within families.

12.title: Interpreting the Present Time
12.context: Jesus says the crowds can read the clouds and the south wind to forecast the weather, so why can they not interpret the present time? He urges them to settle with an opponent on the way rather than be dragged before the judge.

12.title: Reconciling with an Adversary
12.context: Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right? As you go with your adversary to the magistrate, try hard to be reconciled on the way, or you may be dragged before the judge and thrown into prison.

13.title: A Call to Repentance
13.context: Told that Pilate killed some Galileans, Jesus says neither they nor those killed when the tower in Siloam fell were worse sinners than others; unless his hearers repent, they too will perish. He tells of a fruitless fig tree given one more year by the gardener.

13.title: The Parable of the Barren Fig Tree
13.context: A man has a fig tree that has borne no fruit for three years and wants it cut down, but the gardener asks for one more year to dig around it and fertilize it; if it bears fruit, fine, and if not, then cut it down.

13.title: Jesus Heals a Disabled Woman
13.context: On a Sabbath Jesus heals a woman crippled for eighteen years, bent over and unable to straighten up; when the synagogue leader is indignant, Jesus asks whether this daughter of Abraham, bound by Satan for eighteen years, should not be set free on the Sabbath.

13.title: The Parable of the Mustard Seed
13.context: The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed planted in a garden that grows into a tree, and like yeast mixed into a large amount of flour until it works all through the dough.

13.title: The Narrow Door
13.context: Someone asks whether only a few will be saved; Jesus says to strive to enter through the narrow door, for many will try and fail; once the owner shuts the door, those outside who claim they ate with him will be told he does not know them, while people from east, west, north and south will feast in God’s kingdom.

13.title: Lament over Jerusalem
13.context: Some Pharisees warn Jesus that Herod wants to kill him; he tells them to tell that fox he will keep healing today and tomorrow and finish on the third day, for no prophet can die outside Jerusalem. He laments over Jerusalem, longing to gather her children as a hen gathers her chicks.

14.title: Jesus Heals a Man with Dropsy
14.context: On a Sabbath at the house of a prominent Pharisee, Jesus heals a man suffering from dropsy and asks who would not immediately pull out a child or an ox that fell into a well on the Sabbath, and they have nothing to say.

14.title: The Parable of the Guests
14.context: Noticing how the guests pick the places of honor, Jesus advises taking the lowest place, for all who exalt themselves will be humbled and those who humble themselves will be exalted; and when giving a banquet, invite the poor, crippled, lame and blind, and you will be blessed.

14.title: The Parable of the Banquet
14.context: When a guest says blessed is whoever eats in God’s kingdom, Jesus tells of a man whose invited guests all make excuses — a field, oxen, a new wife — so he sends his servant to bring in the poor, crippled, blind and lame to fill his house.

14.title: The Cost of Discipleship
14.context: Large crowds travel with Jesus, and he turns and says that anyone who does not put him before father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters and even their own life cannot be his disciple, nor anyone who does not carry their cross; they should count the cost, like someone building a tower or a king going to war.

14.title: Good Salt
14.context: Salt is good, but if it loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again? It is fit for neither soil nor manure pile and is thrown out; whoever has ears to hear should listen.

15.title: The Parable of the Lost Sheep
15.context: Tax collectors and sinners gather to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees and scribes mutter; Jesus tells of a man who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find the one that is lost, and says there is more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need to repent.

15.title: The Parable of the Lost Coin
15.context: A woman who loses one of her ten silver coins lights a lamp, sweeps the house and searches carefully until she finds it, then calls her friends to rejoice with her; in the same way there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents.

15.title: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
15.context: A younger son takes his inheritance, squanders it in a far country, ends up feeding pigs in a famine and comes home to confess; his father runs to embrace him and throws a feast. When the older son refuses to join, the father pleads that his brother was dead and is alive again, lost and now found.

16.title: The Parable of the Shrewd Manager
16.context: A dishonest manager about to be dismissed reduces the debts owed to his master so that people will welcome him later, and the master commends him for acting shrewdly; Jesus urges using worldly wealth to gain friends, being trustworthy with very little, and he says no one can serve both God and money.

16.title: The Law and the Prophets
16.context: The money-loving Pharisees sneer at Jesus, and he says what people value highly is detestable to God; the Law and Prophets were proclaimed until John, and since then the good news of the kingdom is preached, yet not a stroke of the law will fail; divorce and remarriage is adultery.

16.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
16.context: A rich man feasts daily while the beggar Lazarus lies at his gate; after death Lazarus is comforted at Abraham’s side and the rich man suffers in Hades. Abraham says those who ignore Moses and the Prophets will not be persuaded even by someone rising from the dead.

17.title: Temptations and Trespasses
17.context: Jesus says stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come; if a brother sins, rebuke him and forgive him if he repents. When the apostles ask for more faith, he says faith like a mustard seed is enough, and servants who do all they are told have only done their duty.

17.title: The Ten Lepers
17.context: On the way to Jerusalem ten men with leprosy call out from a distance for mercy; Jesus tells them to show themselves to the priests, and they are cleansed as they go. Only one, a Samaritan, comes back to thank him, and Jesus says his faith has made him well.

17.title: The Coming of the Kingdom
17.context: The Pharisees ask when the kingdom of God will come; Jesus says it is not something that can be observed, for the kingdom of God is in their midst. The day of the Son of Man will be like lightning, and like the days of Noah and Lot, when people went about ordinary life until destruction came; “Remember Lot’s wife!”

18.title: The Parable of the Persistent Widow
18.context: Jesus tells a parable to show they should always pray and not lose heart: a widow keeps pleading with an unjust judge until he grants her justice; will God not bring justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? Yet when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?

18.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
18.context: In the temple a Pharisee boasts of his good deeds while a tax collector stands far off, beating his breast and asking God for mercy. Jesus says the tax collector goes home justified, for those who exalt themselves will be humbled and the humble exalted.

18.title: Jesus Blesses the Children
18.context: People bring babies for Jesus to touch, and the disciples rebuke them, but Jesus calls the children to him and says that whoever does not receive God’s kingdom like a little child will never enter it.

18.title: The Rich Ruler
18.context: A rich ruler says he has kept the commandments; Jesus tells him to sell everything, give to the poor and follow him, and he becomes very sad. Jesus says those who leave everything for the kingdom will receive much more now and eternal life to come.

18.title: The Third Prediction of the Passion
18.context: Jesus takes the twelve aside and tells them that everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled in Jerusalem: he will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, insulted, spat on, flogged and killed, and on the third day he will rise again; the disciples understand none of this.

18.title: Jesus Heals a Blind Beggar
18.context: Near Jericho a blind beggar hears that Jesus of Nazareth is passing and cries out to the Son of David for mercy; Jesus asks what he wants, he says he wants to see, and Jesus says his faith has healed him. He receives his sight at once and follows Jesus, praising God.

19.title: Jesus and Zacchaeus
19.context: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector in Jericho, climbs a tree to see Jesus, who invites himself to his house; Zacchaeus pledges half his goods to the poor and fourfold repayment to anyone he cheated. Jesus says salvation has come, for the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.

19.title: The Parable of the Ten Minas
19.context: Because people think God’s kingdom will appear at once, Jesus tells of a nobleman who leaves to receive a kingdom and gives his servants money to trade; the faithful are given cities to rule, while the one who hid his money loses it.

19.title: The Triumphal Entry
19.context: As Jesus rides toward Jerusalem his disciples praise God aloud; when Pharisees object, he says the stones would cry out if they were silent. Seeing the city he weeps and foretells its destruction because it did not recognize the time of God’s visitation.

19.title: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
19.context: Jesus enters the temple and drives out the sellers, saying God’s house is to be a house of prayer but they have made it a den of robbers; he teaches daily in the temple, and the chief priests and scribes want to kill him but cannot, because all the people hang on his words.

20.title: Jesus’ Authority Challenged
20.context: The chief priests, scribes and elders demand to know by what authority Jesus is doing these things; he asks whether John’s baptism was from heaven or of human origin, and when they will not answer, he will not tell them either.

20.title: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
20.context: Jesus tells of tenants who kill the owner’s beloved son, so the owner will destroy them and give the vineyard to others; quoting the psalm about the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone, he says everyone who falls on that stone will be broken.

20.title: Paying Taxes to Caesar
20.context: The scribes and chief priests send spies pretending to be sincere to ask whether it is right to pay taxes to Caesar, hoping to hand him over to the governor; seeing their trickery, Jesus asks for a denarius and says to give Caesar what is Caesar’s and God what is God’s, and they cannot trap him before the people.

20.title: The Sadducees and the Resurrection
20.context: The Sadducees ask about a widow married to seven brothers; Jesus says those counted worthy of the resurrection neither marry nor die, being like angels and children of God, and Moses at the burning bush calls the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob — he is the God not of the dead but of the living.

20.title: Whose Son Is the Christ?
20.context: Jesus asks how people can say the Christ is David’s son when David himself in the Psalms calls him Lord.

20.title: Beware of the Scribes
20.context: While all the people are listening, Jesus warns his disciples to beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in flowing robes, love greetings in the marketplaces and the most important seats, devour widows’ houses and for a show make lengthy prayers; they will be punished most severely.

21.title: The Poor Widow’s Offering
21.context: Jesus sees the rich putting their gifts into the temple treasury and a poor widow putting in two very small copper coins, and says she has put in more than all the others, for they gave out of their wealth, but she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on.

21.title: Temple Destruction and Other Signs
21.context: When some remark on how the temple is adorned with beautiful stones and gifts, Jesus says the days are coming when not one stone will be left on another.

21.title: Witnessing to All Nations
21.context: Jesus warns against deception: wars, earthquakes, famines and signs will come, but first the disciples will be persecuted, which will be their chance to testify with words he gives them. By standing firm they will gain their lives.

21.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem
21.context: Jesus says that when they see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, its desolation is near, and those in Judea should flee to the mountains; its people will fall by the sword or be taken captive, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until their times are fulfilled.

21.title: The Return of the Son of Man
21.context: There will be signs in the sun, moon and stars, and nations will be in anguish at the roaring of the sea; then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory, and when these things begin, they should stand up and lift their heads, for their redemption is drawing near.

21.title: The Lesson of the Fig Tree
21.context: Jesus points to the fig tree and all the trees: when they sprout leaves, summer is near, and when they see these things, they will know God’s kingdom is near; heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will not.

21.title: Be Watchful for the Day
21.context: Jesus warns his disciples not to let their hearts be weighed down by carousing, drunkenness and the worries of life, lest that day close on them suddenly like a trap; they must stay alert and pray that they may escape all that is coming and stand before the Son of Man.

22.title: The Plot to Kill Jesus
22.context: As the Festival of Unleavened Bread approaches, the chief priests and scribes look for a way to get rid of Jesus, for they fear the people; Satan enters Judas called Iscariot, who goes to discuss with them how he might betray Jesus, and they are delighted and agree to give him money.

22.title: Preparing the Passover
22.context: On the day of Unleavened Bread when the Passover lamb has to be sacrificed, Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the meal, telling them to follow a man carrying a jar of water to a large upper room already furnished, and they find things just as he said.

22.title: The Last Supper
22.context: At the table with the apostles Jesus says he has eagerly desired to eat this Passover with them before he suffers; he breaks bread as his body given for them, to be done in remembrance of him, and gives the cup as the new covenant in his blood poured out for them, adding that his betrayer is at the table with him.

22.title: Who Is the Greatest?
22.context: The disciples argue about who is greatest; Jesus says Gentile kings lord it over people, but their leaders must be like servants, as he is among them as one who serves. He promises they will eat at his table and judge Israel’s twelve tribes.

22.title: Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial
22.context: Jesus says Satan has asked to sift them like wheat, but he has prayed for Simon that his faith may not fail, and when he has turned back he must strengthen his brothers; when Peter says he is ready to go to prison and death, Jesus says that before the rooster crows that day he will deny knowing him three times.

22.title: Purse, Bag and Sword
22.context: Jesus reminds them that when he sent them out without purse, bag or sandals they lacked nothing, but now they should take purse and bag and buy a sword, for the Scripture “He was numbered with the transgressors” must be fulfilled in him; when they say, “See, Lord, here are two swords,” he replies, “That’s enough!”

22.title: Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives
22.context: On the Mount of Olives Jesus kneels and asks the Father to remove this cup if he is willing, yet not his will but the Father’s; an angel strengthens him, and in anguish his sweat falls like drops of blood. He tells the disciples to pray so they will not fall into temptation.

22.title: The Betrayal of Jesus
22.context: Judas leads a crowd and approaches to betray the Son of Man with a kiss; when a disciple cuts off the high priest’s servant’s right ear, Jesus says no more of this and heals him. He tells the chief priests this is their hour, when darkness reigns.

22.title: Peter Denies Jesus
22.context: Jesus is taken to the high priest’s house, and Peter follows at a distance; sitting by the fire in the courtyard he is recognized three times and denies it three times. As he speaks the rooster crows, the Lord turns and looks at Peter, and Peter remembers his words and goes out and weeps bitterly.

22.title: The Guards Mock Jesus
22.context: The men guarding Jesus mock and beat him, blindfold him and demand, “Prophesy! Who hit you?” and they say many other insulting things to him.

22.title: Jesus before the Sanhedrin
22.context: At daybreak the council asks whether Jesus is the Christ; he says that from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of God’s power. When they ask if he is the Son of God, he answers, “You say that I am,” and they say they need no more testimony.

23.title: Jesus before Pilate
23.context: The council brings Jesus to Pilate, accusing him of misleading the nation, forbidding taxes to Caesar and claiming to be Christ, a king; when Pilate asks if he is king of the Jews, Jesus says it is as he says; Pilate finds no basis for a charge, but they insist that he stirs up the people.

23.title: Jesus before Herod
23.context: Learning that Jesus is a Galilean under Herod’s jurisdiction, Pilate sends him to Herod, who is in Jerusalem and hopes to see a miracle; Jesus answers none of his questions, so Herod and his soldiers mock him, dress him in a fine robe and send him back. That day Herod and Pilate, former enemies, become friends.

23.title: The Crowd Chooses Barabbas
23.context: Pilate tells the leaders and people that neither he nor Herod found Jesus guilty of a capital crime, so he will punish and release him; but they shout together to take him away and release Barabbas, and loudly demand his crucifixion; Pilate grants their demand and hands Jesus over to their will.

23.title: The Crucifixion
23.context: Simon of Cyrene carries the cross behind Jesus; at the Skull Jesus prays for the Father to forgive those crucifying him. When one of the criminals asks Jesus to remember him, Jesus promises that he will be with him in paradise.

23.title: The Death of Jesus
23.context: Darkness covers the land from noon to three and the temple curtain tears in two; Jesus cries out, entrusting his spirit into the Father’s hands, and dies. The centurion praises God and says this was surely a righteous man.

23.title: The Burial of Jesus
23.context: Joseph of Arimathea, a council member who had not agreed with its decision, asks Pilate for Jesus’ body, wraps it in linen and lays it in an unused rock tomb. The women from Galilee see where it is laid and go to prepare spices.

24.title: The Resurrection
24.context: Early on the first day of the week the women find the tomb empty, and two men in dazzling clothes ask why they seek the living among the dead, for he has risen. The apostles dismiss their report, but Peter runs to the tomb.

24.title: The Road to Emmaus
24.context: The risen Jesus walks with two disciples going to Emmaus and explains from Moses and all the Prophets what the Scriptures say about him. They recognize him as he breaks bread, he vanishes, and they hurry back to Jerusalem.

24.title: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
24.context: Jesus appears to the disciples, invites them to touch his hands and feet and eats fish before them. He opens their minds to the Scriptures, says repentance and forgiveness must be preached in his name to all nations, and tells them to wait for power from on high.

24.title: The Ascension
24.context: Jesus leads them out to the vicinity of Bethany, lifts up his hands and blesses them; while he is blessing them, he leaves them and is taken up into heaven, and they worship him and return to Jerusalem with great joy, staying continually at the temple, praising God.

1.title: The Beginning
1.context: John opens with “In the beginning,” echoing Genesis 1:1: the Word was with God, all things came through it, and in it was life, the light of humanity. The church’s reading: the Word is Yahweh’s own word and power, whose presence dwelt in Jesus — God in Christ (2 Cor 5:19; The Only True God, ch. 9–10).

1.title: The Mission of John the Baptist
1.context: The Jews send priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask John who he is. He says he is not the Christ, nor Elijah, but the voice calling in the wilderness.

1.title: Jesus the Lamb of God
1.context: Seeing Jesus approach, John calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world; he testifies that he saw the Spirit descend from heaven like a dove and remain on him, marking him as the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit, the Son of God.

1.title: The First Disciples
1.context: Two of John’s disciples hear him and follow Jesus; one is Andrew, who brings his brother Simon to Jesus, and Jesus names him Cephas, which is Peter.

1.title: Jesus Calls Philip and Nathanael
1.context: Jesus finds Philip and says, “Follow me.” Philip finds Nathanael, who, meeting Jesus, declares him the Son of God, the King of Israel.

2.title: The Wedding at Cana
2.context: At a wedding in Cana the wine runs out; Jesus has six stone jars filled with water and it becomes fine wine — the first of his signs, and his disciples believe in him.

2.title: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
2.context: As Passover approaches, Jesus makes a whip of cords and drives the sellers and money changers out of the temple, telling them not to turn his Father’s house into a market; he says if they destroy this temple he will raise it in three days, speaking of the temple of his body.

2.title: Jesus Knows What Is in Man
2.context: In Jerusalem many believe in his name when they see his signs, but Jesus does not entrust himself to them, for he knows what is in each person.

3.title: Jesus and Nicodemus
3.context: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night and is told no one can enter God’s kingdom without being born of water and the Spirit. The Son of Man must be lifted up as Moses lifted the snake, for God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that believers may have eternal life.

3.title: John’s Testimony about Jesus
3.context: John’s disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus, but John says he is not the Christ, only sent ahead of him; the bride belongs to the bridegroom, and the friend rejoices at his voice; he must increase, and John must decrease.

3.title: The One Who Comes from Heaven
3.context: The one who comes from above is above all; the one God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit; whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.

4.title: Jesus and the Samaritan Woman
4.context: Passing through Samaria, Jesus asks a woman at Jacob’s well for a drink and offers her living water; he says God is spirit and must be worshiped in spirit and truth, and she and many Samaritans believe he is the Savior of the world.

4.title: Jesus Heals the Official’s Son
4.context: Back in Cana, a royal official from Capernaum begs Jesus to heal his dying son; Jesus says, “Go, your son will live,” the man believes, and the boy recovers at that very hour — Jesus’ second sign in Galilee.

5.title: The Pool of Bethesda
5.context: At the pool of Bethesda Jesus tells a man who has been ill for thirty-eight years to pick up his mat and walk; because it is the Sabbath, the Jewish leaders begin to persecute Jesus.

5.title: The Son's Authority
5.context: Jesus says the Son can do nothing by himself but only what he sees the Father doing; the Father has entrusted all judgment to the Son, that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father, and whoever hears his word and believes the one who sent him has eternal life.

5.title: Testimonies about Jesus
5.context: Jesus says he does not testify about himself alone; John the Baptist, his works, the Father who sent him and the Scriptures all testify about him. They search the Scriptures thinking to find eternal life there, yet refuse to come to him for life, though Moses wrote about him.
