6.title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
6.context: Jesus feeds five thousand with a boy’s five barley loaves and two fish; when the people intend to make him king by force, he withdraws again to a mountain by himself.

6.title: Jesus Walks on Water
6.context: At night on the lake in a strong wind the disciples see Jesus walking on the water and are frightened; he says, “It is I; don’t be afraid,” and when they take him into the boat it immediately reaches the shore.

6.title: Jesus the Bread of Life
6.context: The crowd seeks Jesus, and he tells them not to work for food that spoils but for food that lasts to eternal life; he is the bread of life come down from heaven, and whoever comes to him will never hunger or thirst. Unless they eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, they have no life in them.

6.title: Many Disciples Turn Back
6.context: Many disciples find this teaching hard and turn back; Jesus says the Spirit gives life and his words are spirit and life. When he asks the Twelve if they will leave too, Peter answers that Jesus has the words of eternal life, so to whom else could they go?

7.title: Jesus Teaches at the Feast
7.context: Jesus stays in Galilee because the Jewish leaders want to kill him; as the Feast of Tabernacles approaches, his brothers, who do not believe in him, urge him to go and show himself.

7.title: Jesus at the Feast of Tabernacles
7.context: Jesus goes up to the Feast of Tabernacles privately while the crowds argue about him; midway through the feast he teaches in the temple, saying his teaching comes from the one who sent him, and anyone who chooses to do God’s will will know it is from God. They must not judge by appearances.

7.title: Is Jesus the Christ?
7.context: People in Jerusalem debate whether he is the Messiah; Jesus cries out that the one who sent him is true, and though they do not know him, he does, for he is from him.

7.title: Officers Sent to Arrest Jesus
7.context: The Pharisees and chief priests send temple guards to arrest Jesus; he says he will be with them only a little longer and then go to the one who sent him.

7.title: Living Water
7.context: On the last day of the feast Jesus stands and cries out that anyone who is thirsty may come to him and drink, and rivers of living water will flow from within those who believe in him; John explains that he meant the Spirit that believers would receive.

7.title: Division over Jesus
7.context: The crowd is divided over Jesus: some say he is the Prophet, others the Messiah, others ask how the Messiah can come from Galilee.

7.title: The Unbelief of the Jewish Leaders
7.context: The guards return without Jesus, saying, “No one ever spoke the way this man does”; the Pharisees scorn them, and Nicodemus asks whether the law condemns anyone without first hearing him.

8.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
8.context: A woman caught in adultery is brought to test Jesus; he says the one without sin should throw the first stone, and they leave one by one. He does not condemn her but tells her to sin no more. The earliest manuscripts lack this passage (7:53–8:11).

8.title: Jesus the Light of the World
8.context: Jesus says he is the light of the world, and whoever follows him will not walk in darkness but have the light of life; when the Pharisees say he testifies about himself, he says his testimony is true because the Father also testifies about him.

8.title: Where I Am Going You Cannot Come
8.context: Jesus says he is going away and where he goes they cannot come; if they do not believe that he is the one he claims to be, they will die in their sins, and when they have lifted up the Son of Man they will know.

8.title: The Truth Will Set You Free
8.context: Jesus says those who hold to his teaching are truly his disciples and the truth will set them free; when his hearers say they were never slaves, he says everyone who sins is a slave to sin, but if the Son sets them free they will be free indeed.

8.title: You Are of Your Father the Devil
8.context: They claim Abraham as their father; Jesus says if they were Abraham’s children they would do what Abraham did, but they belong to their father the devil, a murderer from the beginning and the father of lies.

8.title: Jesus and Abraham
8.context: They accuse Jesus of being a Samaritan and demon-possessed; he says whoever keeps his word will never see death, that Abraham rejoiced at the thought of seeing his day, and “before Abraham was born, I am”; at this they pick up stones to stone him.

9.title: Jesus Heals the Man Born Blind
9.context: Seeing a man blind from birth, the disciples ask who sinned; Jesus says neither he nor his parents, but this happened so that the works of God might be displayed; he puts mud on his eyes and tells him to wash in the Pool of Siloam, and he comes back seeing.

9.title: The Pharisees Investigate the Healing
9.context: The Pharisees question the healed man and his parents, since the healing was on the Sabbath; he says, “I was blind but now I see!” and that if this man were not from God he could do nothing, so they throw him out.

9.title: Spiritual Blindness
9.context: Jesus finds the man and asks if he believes in the Son of Man; he says, “Lord, I believe,” and worships him; Jesus says he came into the world for judgment, so that the blind will see and those who see will become blind.

10.title: Jesus the Good Shepherd
10.context: Jesus says the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep; the sheep listen to his voice, he calls them by name and leads them out, while the thief climbs in another way.

10.title: Jesus the Good Shepherd
10.context: Jesus says he is the gate for the sheep, and those who enter through him will be saved; he came so they may have abundant life. He is the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, and he has other sheep to bring, so there will be one flock and one shepherd.

10.title: Jesus at the Feast of Dedication
10.context: At the Feast of Dedication the Jews demand that Jesus say plainly whether he is the Christ; he says the works he does in the Father’s name testify about him and no one can snatch his sheep from the Father’s hand. When he says he and the Father are one, they take up stones.

11.title: The Death of Lazarus
11.context: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, falls ill; Jesus says the sickness will not end in death but is for God’s glory, waits two days, and then tells the disciples that Lazarus is dead and they will go to him.

11.title: Jesus Comforts Martha and Mary
11.context: Lazarus has been dead four days, and Martha says he would not have died had Jesus been there; Jesus says he is the resurrection and the life, and those who believe in him will live even though they die. Martha confesses that he is the Christ, the Son of God.

11.title: Jesus Wept
11.context: Mary comes and falls at Jesus’ feet weeping; seeing her and those with her weeping, he is deeply moved in spirit and troubled, and Jesus weeps.

11.title: Jesus Raises Lazarus
11.context: At the tomb Jesus has the stone taken away, looks up and thanks the Father for hearing him, then calls in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” and the dead man comes out, wrapped in strips of linen.

11.title: The Plot to Kill Jesus
11.context: Many believe in Jesus, but others report to the Pharisees; the high priest Caiaphas says it is better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish, which John says was a prophecy that Jesus would die for the nation, and from that day they plot to kill him.

12.title: Mary Anoints Jesus
12.context: Six days before Passover in Bethany, Mary anoints Jesus’ feet with a pint of expensive nard and wipes them with her hair; Judas objects that it could have been sold for the poor, but Jesus says she kept it for the day of his burial.

12.title: The Plot to Kill Lazarus
12.context: A large crowd comes to see Jesus and also Lazarus whom he raised; the chief priests plan to kill Lazarus too, because on his account many are believing in Jesus.

12.title: The Triumphal Entry
12.context: The festival crowds hear Jesus is coming and go out with palm branches shouting hosanna; he finds a young donkey and rides it, fulfilling Zechariah’s words, though the disciples understand only after he is glorified; the Pharisees say to one another that the whole world has gone after him.

12.title: Jesus Predicts His Death
12.context: Some Greeks ask to see Jesus; he says the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, and unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a single seed, but if it dies, it produces many seeds.

12.title: The Son of Man Must Be Lifted Up
12.context: Jesus is troubled, yet says he came for this very hour and asks the Father to glorify his name, and a voice from heaven answers. He says that when he is lifted up from the earth he will draw all people to himself, indicating how he would die.

12.title: Belief and Unbelief
12.context: Even after so many signs they still do not believe, fulfilling Isaiah; many leaders believe in him but will not confess it for fear of the Pharisees, for they love human praise more than praise from God.

12.title: Jesus' Words Will Judge
12.context: Jesus cries out that whoever believes in him believes in the one who sent him; he came not to judge the world but to save it, and the word he has spoken will judge those who reject him on the last day, for he speaks just what the Father commanded him, and his command leads to eternal life.

13.title: Jesus Washes His Disciples’ Feet
13.context: Before Passover, knowing his hour has come to leave this world and go to the Father, Jesus shows his disciples the full extent of his love: during supper he washes their feet and says that since he, their Lord and Teacher, has washed their feet, they also should wash one another’s feet.

13.title: Jesus Foretells His Betrayal
13.context: Troubled in spirit, Jesus says one of them will betray him; he dips a piece of bread and gives it to Judas, who takes it and goes out immediately — and it is night.

13.title: Love One Another
13.context: After Judas leaves, Jesus says the Son of Man is now glorified and God is glorified in him; he gives the disciples a new command to love one another as he has loved them, so that everyone will know they are his disciples.

13.title: Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial
13.context: Peter asks where Jesus is going; he says Peter cannot follow now but will follow later, and when Peter says he will lay down his life for him, Jesus says that before the rooster crows he will disown him three times.

14.title: In My Father’s House Are Many Rooms
14.context: Jesus tells the disciples not to be troubled, for he goes to prepare a place for them and will return for them. He is the way, the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through him, and whoever has seen him has seen the Father.

14.title: Jesus Promises the Holy Spirit
14.context: Jesus says that if the disciples love him they will keep his commands, and he will ask the Father to give them another Helper, the Spirit of truth, to be with them forever; the Spirit will teach them all things and remind them of everything he said, and he leaves them his peace.

15.title: Jesus the True Vine
15.context: Jesus says he is the true vine, the Father is the gardener and the disciples are the branches, which bear fruit only by remaining in the vine. No one has greater love than to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.

15.title: The Hatred of the World
15.context: Jesus says that if the world hates the disciples, it hated him first; a servant is not greater than the master, so if they persecuted him they will persecute the disciples too. But the Helper sent from the Father will testify about him, and the disciples will testify as well.

16.title: The Promise of the Holy Spirit
16.context: Jesus says it is for their good that he is going away, for unless he goes the Advocate will not come; when the Advocate comes, the world will be proved wrong about sin, righteousness and judgment, and the Spirit of truth will come and guide them into all the truth.

16.title: Grief Will Turn to Joy
16.context: Jesus says that in a little while they will no longer see him, and then after a little while they will see him again; they will weep while the world rejoices, but their grief will turn to joy, like a woman who forgets her pain after childbirth, and no one will take away their joy.

16.title: Ask in My Name
16.context: Jesus says the time is coming when he will speak plainly rather than in figures; they will ask in his name, for the Father himself loves them; he came from the Father into the world and is now leaving it to go to the Father. In the world they will have trouble, but they can take heart, for he has overcome the world.

17.title: Prayer for the Son
17.context: Jesus looks toward heaven and asks the Father to glorify the Son so the Son may glorify him; he says eternal life is to know the Father, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom he sent. He prays for his disciples and for all who will believe through them, asking the Father to protect them and make them one.

18.title: The Betrayal of Jesus
18.context: Judas leads soldiers and officials to the garden to arrest Jesus; when he says “I am he,” they fall back to the ground. Peter cuts off the ear of Malchus, the high priest’s servant, and Jesus tells him to put away his sword, for he must drink the cup the Father has given him.

18.title: Jesus Is Brought to Annas
18.context: The soldiers and officials arrest Jesus, bind him and bring him first to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.

18.title: Peter’s First Denial
18.context: Simon Peter and another disciple follow Jesus; the other disciple, known to the high priest, brings Peter into the courtyard; the girl at the door asks if he is one of Jesus’ disciples, Peter says he is not, and he stands warming himself at the fire with the servants and officials.

18.title: Jesus before the High Priest
18.context: The high priest questions Jesus about his disciples and teaching; Jesus says he has spoken openly to the world, and when an official strikes him he asks why; Annas then sends him bound to Caiaphas.

18.title: Peter’s Second and Third Denials
18.context: As Peter warms himself, he is asked again if he is a disciple and denies it; a relative of Malchus asks if he did not see him in the garden, and Peter denies it again, and at that moment a rooster crows.

18.title: Jesus before Pilate
18.context: Pilate asks Jesus if he is king of the Jews; Jesus says his kingdom is not of this world and he came to testify to the truth. Pilate asks what truth is, then goes out and says he finds no basis for a charge against him.

18.title: Jesus Is Sentenced to Die
18.context: Pilate offers to release “the king of the Jews,” but they shout for Barabbas; he has Jesus flogged, the soldiers crown him with thorns and dress him in purple, and Pilate brings him out: “Here is the man!” The chief priests shout, “Crucify! Crucify!” and Pilate finally hands him over to be crucified.

19.title: The Crucifixion
19.context: Carrying his own cross, Jesus goes out to the place of the Skull, where they crucify him with two others; Pilate’s notice in Aramaic, Latin and Greek reads “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews”; the soldiers cast lots for his garment, and Jesus entrusts his mother to the disciple whom he loved.

19.title: The Death of Jesus
19.context: Knowing that everything has now been finished, and so that Scripture would be fulfilled, Jesus says, “I am thirsty”; they lift a sponge soaked in wine vinegar to his lips, and when he has received it, he says, “It is finished,” bows his head and gives up his spirit.

19.title: Jesus’ Side Is Pierced
19.context: The soldiers break the legs of the two criminals but, finding Jesus already dead, pierce his side with a spear instead, and blood and water flow out. This fulfills the Scriptures that none of his bones would be broken and that they would look on the one they pierced.

19.title: The Burial of Jesus
19.context: Joseph of Arimathea, a secret disciple for fear of the Jewish leaders, asks Pilate for the body, and Nicodemus brings about seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes; they wrap the body with the spices in linen, according to Jewish burial customs, and lay it in a new tomb in a nearby garden.

20.title: The Resurrection
20.context: Early on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene finds the stone removed from the tomb and runs to tell Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved; they run to the tomb and find the strips of linen and the burial cloth folded by itself, and the other disciple sees and believes.

20.title: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
20.context: Mary weeps outside the tomb, and when the risen Jesus calls her by name she recognizes him. He sends her to tell his brothers that he is ascending to his Father and their Father, to his God and their God.

20.title: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
20.context: That evening, with the doors locked for fear of the Jewish leaders, Jesus stands among the disciples: “Peace be with you!” He shows them his hands and side, sends them as the Father sent him, breathes on them and says, “Receive the Holy Spirit.”

20.title: Jesus Appears to Thomas
20.context: Thomas was absent when Jesus appeared and says he will not believe unless he touches the nail marks and the wound in his side; eight days later Jesus comes again and invites him to do so, and Thomas says, “My Lord and my God.” Jesus says blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe.

20.title: The Purpose of John’s Book
20.context: Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples that are not written in this book; but these are written so that people may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and by believing have life in his name.

21.title: Jesus Appears by the Sea of Tiberias
21.context: Jesus appears again by the Sea of Tiberias; after a fruitless night, he tells the disciples to cast the net on the right side of the boat, and they catch 153 large fish; on the shore he has a fire of coals with fish and bread, and invites them to breakfast.

21.title: Jesus and Peter
21.context: Three times Jesus asks Peter, “Do you love me?” and three times Peter answers that he does; three times Jesus tells him to feed his sheep, foretells the kind of death by which Peter will glorify God, and says, “Follow me!”

21.title: Jesus and the Beloved Disciple
21.context: Peter asks what will happen to the disciple Jesus loved, and Jesus says that is not his concern — he must follow. A rumor spreads that this disciple will not die, though Jesus never said so; this is the disciple who testifies to these things and wrote them down.

1.title: Prologue
1.context: Luke continues his “former book” to Theophilus: for forty days after his resurrection Jesus appears to the apostles, speaks about the kingdom of God, and tells them to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit the Father promised.

1.title: The Ascension
1.context: The disciples ask if Jesus will now restore the kingdom to Israel; he says the times are not for them to know, but they will receive power when the Spirit comes and be his witnesses to the ends of the earth. He is taken up, and two men in white say he will return the same way.

1.title: Matthias Replaces Judas
1.context: Back in Jerusalem the apostles devote themselves to prayer with the women and Jesus’ brothers; Peter says Judas’s place must be filled, and by lot Matthias is added to the eleven.

2.title: The Holy Spirit at Pentecost
2.context: On the day of Pentecost a sound like a violent wind fills the house and tongues of fire rest on each of them; all are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak in other languages, and Jews from every nation hear them declaring God’s wonders in their own tongues.

2.title: Peter Addresses the Crowd
2.context: At Pentecost Peter explains the events through Joel’s prophecy and proclaims that God raised the crucified Jesus and made him Lord and Christ. Cut to the heart, the crowd is told to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins and receive the Spirit; about three thousand are baptized.

2.title: The Fellowship of Believers
2.context: The believers devote themselves to the apostles’ teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer; they share everything, meet daily in the temple courts and break bread in their homes, and the Lord adds daily those who are being saved.

3.title: A Lame Man Walks
3.context: Peter and John go to the temple to pray, and a man lame from birth asks them for money; Peter says he has no silver or gold but gives what he has, telling him in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth to walk, and the man leaps up and enters the temple praising God.

3.title: Peter Speaks in Solomon’s Colonnade
3.context: In Solomon’s Colonnade Peter tells the crowd that the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob has glorified his servant Jesus, whom they killed but God raised; he is the prophet like Moses, and they must repent and turn to God so that their sins may be wiped out.

4.title: Peter and John before the Sanhedrin
4.context: Peter and John are arrested for proclaiming Jesus’ resurrection; before the council Peter says the man was healed by Jesus’ name and there is salvation in no one else. Amazed at the boldness of these ordinary men, the rulers forbid them to speak in Jesus’ name, but they reply that they must obey God rather than people.

4.title: The Believers’ Prayer
4.context: Released, Peter and John report to the believers, who pray together to the Sovereign Lord, maker of heaven and earth, quoting Psalm 2 about the nations raging against the Lord and his anointed; they ask for boldness, the place shakes, and they are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak the word of God boldly.

4.title: Sharing among Believers
4.context: All the believers are one in heart and mind, sharing everything they have; the apostles testify with great power to the resurrection, and Joseph, called Barnabas, sells a field and lays the money at the apostles’ feet.

5.title: Ananias and Sapphira
5.context: Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell property but keep back part of the money while claiming to give all; Peter tells Ananias he has lied not to men but to God, and both fall dead, and great fear seizes the whole church.

5.title: The Apostles Heal Many
5.context: The apostles perform many signs and wonders among the people; people even carry the sick into the streets so that Peter’s shadow might fall on them, and more and more men and women believe in the Lord.

5.title: The Apostles Arrested and Freed
5.context: The high priest jails the apostles, but an angel frees them at night; before the council they say they must obey God rather than people. Gamaliel advises leaving them alone in case this is from God, and after a flogging they rejoice to suffer for the Name.

6.title: The Choosing of the Seven
6.context: The Greek-speaking believers complain that their widows are overlooked in the daily distribution; the apostles have the disciples choose seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom to oversee it, so that they can give themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word; Stephen is one of them.

6.title: The Arrest of Stephen
6.context: Stephen, full of grace and power, does great wonders; opponents cannot stand up against the wisdom the Spirit gives him, so they stir up false witnesses who accuse him of speaking against Moses and God, and bring him before the Sanhedrin.

7.title: Stephen’s Address: The Call of Abraham
7.context: Before the council Stephen reviews Israel’s history from Abraham’s call through Joseph and Moses to the tabernacle and temple, showing that the people have always resisted the Holy Spirit, persecuted the prophets and now killed the Righteous One; the Most High does not live in houses made by human hands.

7.title: The Stoning of Stephen
7.context: They are furious, but Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looks up to heaven and sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God; they drag him out of the city and stone him, and he falls on his knees crying, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them”; Saul approves of his killing.

8.title: Saul Persecutes the Church
8.context: That day a great persecution breaks out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles are scattered through Judea and Samaria; Saul begins to destroy the church, going from house to house and dragging off men and women to prison.

8.title: Philip in Samaria
8.context: Those scattered preach the word wherever they go; Philip proclaims the Messiah in Samaria with signs, and there is great joy; the sorcerer Simon also believes but later offers money for the power to give the Spirit and is sternly rebuked by Peter.

8.title: Philip and the Ethiopian
8.context: An angel sends Philip to the desert road to Gaza, where he meets an Ethiopian official reading Isaiah 53 in his chariot; beginning with that passage, Philip tells him the good news about Jesus, and when they come to water the official is baptized and goes on his way rejoicing.

9.title: The Road to Damascus
9.context: Saul travels to Damascus to arrest believers when a light from heaven flashes around him; he falls to the ground and hears Jesus ask why he is persecuting him. Blind for three days, he regains his sight when the Lord sends Ananias to lay hands on him, and he is baptized.

9.title: Saul Preaches at Damascus
9.context: At once Saul begins to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God, growing more and more powerful and baffling the Jews of Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Messiah.

9.title: The Escape from Damascus
9.context: The Jews conspire to kill Saul and watch the city gates day and night, but his followers lower him in a basket through an opening in the wall at night.

9.title: Saul in Jerusalem
9.context: In Jerusalem the disciples are afraid of Saul until Barnabas brings him to the apostles and tells how he saw the Lord; when Grecian Jews try to kill him, the believers send him to Tarsus, and the church throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria enjoys peace and grows.

9.title: The Healing of Aeneas
9.context: In Lydda Peter meets Aeneas, paralyzed for eight years, and tells him that Jesus Christ heals him and he should get up and make his bed; he rises at once, and the people of Lydda and Sharon turn to the Lord.

9.title: The Raising of Tabitha
9.context: In Joppa a disciple named Tabitha (Dorcas), known for doing good and helping the poor, dies; Peter kneels and prays and says, “Tabitha, get up,” and she opens her eyes and sits up, and many believe in the Lord.

10.title: Cornelius Sends for Peter
10.context: Cornelius, a God-fearing centurion in Caesarea, is told by an angel to send for Peter; meanwhile in Joppa Peter sees a vision of all kinds of animals let down from heaven and hears that he must not call unclean what God has cleansed, so he goes with the messengers to Cornelius.

10.title: Good News for the Gentiles
10.context: Peter says God shows no favoritism but accepts all who fear him and do right; he tells how God anointed Jesus with the Spirit and raised him after his crucifixion. While he speaks the Spirit falls on the Gentiles, and he has them baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

10.title: The Gentiles Receive the Holy Spirit
10.context: While Peter is still speaking, the Holy Spirit comes on all who hear the message, and the Gentiles speak in tongues and praise God; Peter orders that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

11.title: Peter’s Report at Jerusalem
11.context: Circumcised believers in Jerusalem criticize Peter for eating with Gentiles; he recounts the vision and how the Spirit fell on Cornelius’s household, and they praise God that he has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles too.

11.title: The Church at Antioch
11.context: Believers scattered by persecution bring the gospel to Antioch, where some also preach to Greeks and many believe; the Jerusalem church sends Barnabas, who brings Saul, and they teach there for a year. The disciples are first called Christians at Antioch.

12.title: James Killed, Peter Imprisoned
12.context: King Herod persecutes some in the church, has James the brother of John put to death with the sword, and seizes Peter, guarding him with four squads of soldiers, while the church prays earnestly to God for him.

12.title: The Rescue of Peter
12.context: The night before his trial, an angel wakes Peter, the chains fall off his wrists and the iron gate opens by itself; Peter goes to the house of Mary, John Mark’s mother, where many are praying, and the servant girl Rhoda is so overjoyed to recognize his voice that she forgets to open the door.

12.title: The Death of Herod
12.context: When Tyre and Sidon seek peace, Herod gives a speech in royal robes and the crowd shouts that this is the voice of a god, not a man; because he does not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord strikes him, and he is eaten by worms and dies. But God’s word continues to spread.

13.title: Paul’s First Missionary Journey Begins
13.context: While the Antioch church is worshiping and fasting, the Holy Spirit says, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them”; after more fasting and prayer they lay hands on them and send them off.

13.title: On Cyprus
13.context: Sent out by the Holy Spirit, they preach on Cyprus; at Paphos the sorcerer Elymas opposes them, and Saul, also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, makes him blind for a time, and the proconsul Sergius Paulus believes, amazed at the teaching about the Lord.

13.title: In Pisidian Antioch
13.context: In the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch Paul preaches from the exodus to David and then to Jesus, the Savior God brought from David’s line as promised, through whom everyone who believes is justified. The next Sabbath jealous Jews oppose them, so Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles.

14.title: Paul and Barnabas at Iconium
14.context: At Iconium many Jews and Greeks believe, and the Lord confirms the message with signs and wonders, but the city is divided, and when a plot forms to stone them they flee to Lystra and Derbe and continue preaching.

14.title: The Visit to Lystra and Derbe
14.context: In Lystra Paul heals a man lame from birth, and the crowd thinks he and Barnabas are gods and tries to sacrifice to them; tearing their clothes, they say they are only men and urge the people to turn to the living God who made heaven and earth. Later Jews stir up the crowd to stone Paul, leaving him for dead.

14.title: Strengthening the Disciples
14.context: Paul and Barnabas retrace their route strengthening the disciples, saying we must pass through many hardships to enter God’s kingdom; they appoint elders in each church and report in Antioch that God has opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

15.title: The Dispute over Circumcision
15.context: Some teach that Gentile believers must be circumcised to be saved, so the apostles and elders meet in Jerusalem; Peter says God cleansed Gentile hearts by faith, and James, citing Amos, proposes not to burden them but ask them to avoid food polluted by idols, sexual immorality, strangled animals and blood.

15.title: The Letter to the Gentile Believers
15.context: The apostles and elders send a letter with Judas and Silas along with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch, saying it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to them not to burden the Gentile believers beyond a few essentials; the church reads it and rejoices at its encouragement.

15.title: Paul’s Second Missionary Journey Begins
15.context: Paul proposes revisiting the churches, but he and Barnabas disagree sharply over taking Mark, who had left them earlier; they part ways, Barnabas taking Mark to Cyprus while Paul chooses Silas and travels through Syria and Cilicia strengthening the churches.

16.title: Timothy Joins Paul and Silas
16.context: At Lystra Paul meets Timothy, whose mother is a Jewish believer and father a Greek, and takes him along, circumcising him because of the Jews in that area; they deliver the council’s decisions to the churches, which grow stronger in faith and increase daily in numbers.

16.title: Paul’s Vision of the Macedonian
16.context: Kept by the Holy Spirit from preaching in Asia and prevented by the Spirit of Jesus from entering Bithynia, they come to Troas, where Paul sees a vision at night of a man of Macedonia begging, “Come over to Macedonia and help us,” and they set out at once, concluding that God has called them.

16.title: Lydia’s Conversion in Philippi
16.context: At Philippi, a leading city of Macedonia, they go on the Sabbath to a place of prayer by the river, where Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth and a worshiper of God, listens; the Lord opens her heart, she and her household are baptized, and she persuades them to stay at her home.

16.title: Paul and Silas Imprisoned
16.context: In Philippi Paul drives a fortune-telling spirit from a slave girl, and her owners have him and Silas beaten and jailed; at midnight, as they pray and sing, an earthquake opens the doors. The jailer asks how to be saved and is baptized with his household.

17.title: The Uproar in Thessalonica
17.context: For three Sabbaths in the Thessalonian synagogue Paul argues that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead; some Jews and many Greeks believe, but other Jews gather a mob and accuse them of turning the world upside down and defying Caesar by saying there is another king, Jesus.

17.title: The Character of the Bereans
17.context: The Bereans are more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, receiving the message with great eagerness and examining the Scriptures every day to see if what Paul said was true; many believe, but when agitators come from Thessalonica, the believers send Paul to the coast.

17.title: Paul in Athens
17.context: In idol-filled Athens Paul reasons with all comers and tells the Areopagus that their “unknown god” is the Creator, who does not live in man-made temples; God has set a day to judge the world through a man he appointed, proving it by raising him from the dead.

18.title: Paul Ministers in Corinth
18.context: In Corinth Paul works as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla and reasons in the synagogue every Sabbath; when the Jews oppose him he turns to the Gentiles, and Crispus the synagogue leader and many others believe; in a vision the Lord tells him not to fear, and he stays a year and a half.

18.title: Paul Returns to Antioch
18.context: After many days Paul sails for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila, having his hair cut at Cenchreae because of a vow; at Ephesus he reasons in the synagogue but declines to stay, promising to return if God wills; he lands at Caesarea, greets the church in Jerusalem and goes down to Antioch.

18.title: Paul’s Third Missionary Journey Begins
18.context: Apollos, a native of Alexandria and powerful in the Scriptures, comes to Ephesus knowing only the baptism of John; Priscilla and Aquila explain the way of God more accurately to him, and he goes on to Achaia, where he greatly helps the believers.

19.title: The Holy Spirit Received at Ephesus
19.context: Some disciples in Ephesus have received only John’s baptism, which Paul explains pointed to Jesus; they are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul lays hands on them the Spirit comes on them and they speak in tongues and prophesy.

19.title: Seven Sons of Sceva
19.context: God does extraordinary miracles through Paul, even through handkerchiefs and aprons he had touched; when the seven sons of Sceva try to use Jesus’ name to drive out a spirit, it says it knows Jesus and Paul but not them, and overpowers them; many former sorcerers burn their books publicly.

19.title: The Riot in Ephesus
19.context: The silversmith Demetrius, losing business from Artemis shrines because of Paul’s preaching, stirs up the city, and a crowd shouts “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians” in the theater for two hours; the city clerk calms them, saying any charges should be settled in a lawful assembly, and dismisses them.

20.title: Paul in Macedonia and Greece
20.context: After the uproar Paul travels through Macedonia encouraging the believers and spends three months in Greece; because of a plot against him, he returns through Macedonia, accompanied by Sopater, Aristarchus, Secundus, Gaius, Timothy, Tychicus and Trophimus.

20.title: Eutychus Revived at Troas
20.context: On the first day of the week the believers in Troas gather to break bread, and Paul talks until midnight; a young man named Eutychus falls asleep in a window and drops three stories to his death, but Paul goes down, embraces him and says his life is in him, and they take the boy home alive.

20.title: From Troas to Miletus
20.context: Paul walks to Assos while his companions sail ahead; they travel by Mitylene, Chios and Samos to Miletus, Paul having decided to sail past Ephesus so as not to spend time in Asia, for he is in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

20.title: Paul’s Farewell to the Ephesians
20.context: At Miletus Paul bids farewell to the Ephesian elders, recalling his humble and tearful service and his wish only to finish his course; he charges them to shepherd the church God bought with his own blood, guard against wolves and remember that giving is more blessed than receiving.

21.title: Paul’s Journey to Jerusalem
21.context: On the way to Jerusalem disciples in Tyre, moved by the Spirit, urge Paul not to go; in Caesarea the prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul’s belt and says Paul will be bound in Jerusalem and handed to the Gentiles, but Paul says he is ready not only to be bound but to die for the name of the Lord Jesus.

21.title: Paul’s Arrival at Jerusalem
21.context: In Jerusalem Paul reports to James and the elders what God has done among the Gentiles through him; the elders say Jewish believers have heard he teaches people to abandon Moses, so they advise him to join four men in a purification rite to show he keeps the law, and Paul does so.

21.title: Paul Seized at the Temple
21.context: Jews from Asia see Paul in the temple and falsely accuse him of bringing Greeks inside, and a mob drags him out to kill him; the Roman commander arrives with troops, chains him and takes him into the barracks.

21.title: Paul Addresses the Crowd
21.context: As he is about to be taken into the barracks, Paul asks the commander in Greek for permission to speak; the commander had assumed he was the Egyptian rebel, but Paul says he is a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, and standing on the steps he motions to the crowd and speaks to them in Aramaic.

22.title: Paul Tells How He Came to Faith
22.context: Paul tells the crowd how on the road to Damascus a great light shone on him, he heard Jesus speak and was blinded; Ananias came and restored his sight and told him to get up, be baptized and wash away his sins, calling on the Lord’s name.

22.title: Paul Is Sent to the Gentiles
22.context: Paul says that when he returned to Jerusalem and prayed in the temple he fell into a trance and saw the Lord telling him to leave, for Jerusalem would not accept his testimony, and that he would be sent far away to the Gentiles. At this the crowd shouts that such a man should not be allowed to live.

22.title: Paul the Roman Citizen
22.context: At the word “Gentiles” the crowd shouts, “Rid the earth of him!” and the commander orders him flogged and interrogated; as they stretch him out, Paul asks whether it is legal to flog a Roman citizen who has not been found guilty, and the commander, alarmed to learn that he is a Roman citizen born, withdraws.

22.title: Paul before the Council
22.context: Before the council Paul says he is on trial for the hope of the resurrection, setting Pharisees and Sadducees against each other; that night the Lord stands by him and says he must testify in Rome as he has in Jerusalem.

23.title: The Plot to Kill Paul
23.context: More than forty Jews vow not to eat or drink until they kill Paul and plan to ambush him on the way to another council hearing; Paul’s nephew hears of it and tells the commander, who sends Paul under heavy guard by night to Governor Felix in Caesarea.

23.title: Paul Sent to Felix
23.context: In his letter Claudius Lysias tells Felix that he rescued Paul, a Roman citizen, from the Jews and found that the accusation concerned questions about their law, with no charge deserving death or imprisonment; the soldiers bring Paul to Felix, who keeps him under guard in Herod’s palace until his accusers arrive.

24.title: Tertullus Prosecutes Paul
24.context: Five days later the high priest Ananias arrives with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who flatters Felix and accuses Paul of being a troublemaker who stirs up riots among the Jews all over the world, a ringleader of the Nazarene sect who even tried to desecrate the temple.

24.title: Paul’s Defense to Felix
24.context: Before Governor Felix Paul says he stirred up no one in the temple; he serves the God of his ancestors according to the Way they call a sect, believes the Law and Prophets, hopes for the resurrection and keeps a clear conscience. Felix postpones the case.

24.title: The Verdict Postponed
24.context: Felix and his wife Drusilla send for Paul to hear about faith in Christ Jesus; when Paul speaks of righteousness, self-control and the coming judgment, Felix grows afraid and sends him away until a more convenient time, hoping also for a bribe; after two years, to please the Jews, he leaves Paul in prison.

25.title: Paul’s Trial before Festus
25.context: When Festus takes office, the chief priests ask him to bring Paul to Jerusalem, planning an ambush; Festus hears the case in Caesarea, where many serious charges cannot be proved; when asked whether he will be tried in Jerusalem, Paul appeals to Caesar, and Festus says that to Caesar he shall go.

25.title: Festus Consults Agrippa
25.context: King Agrippa visits, and Festus describes Paul’s case as a dispute over a dead man named Jesus whom Paul claims is alive; Agrippa wants to hear Paul himself, and the next day they assemble in great pomp.

26.title: Paul’s Testimony to Agrippa
26.context: Paul makes his defense before King Agrippa, saying he lived from youth as a Pharisee in the strictest sect of Judaism and is now on trial for hoping in God’s promise to their ancestors; he admits he once imprisoned many saints in Jerusalem and voted for their deaths.

26.title: Paul Tells How He Came to Faith
26.context: Paul recounts how on the Damascus road he saw a light brighter than the sun and heard Jesus send him to the Gentiles to open their eyes, turning them from darkness to light and from Satan’s power to God, so they may receive forgiveness of sins through faith in Jesus.

26.title: Paul Testifies to Jews and Gentiles
26.context: Paul says he obeyed the heavenly vision, calling people everywhere to repent and turn to God; he says only what the prophets and Moses foretold — that the Christ would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, bring light to Jews and Gentiles.

26.title: Festus Interrupts Paul’s Defense
26.context: Festus says Paul’s learning has driven him mad, but Paul says he speaks the truth; when Agrippa asks if he hopes to persuade him so quickly, Paul wishes all his hearers were like him, minus the chains. Afterward they agree he could have been freed had he not appealed to Caesar.

27.title: Paul Sails for Rome
27.context: Paul and other prisoners are put in the charge of a centurion named Julius and sail for Italy; slowed by contrary winds, they reach Fair Havens, where Paul warns that continuing will bring disaster to cargo, ship and lives, but the centurion follows the pilot and owner and they set out for Phoenix to winter there.

27.title: The Storm at Sea
27.context: A violent storm hits and for days no sun or stars appear, so all hope is lost; Paul says an angel of God told him that no one on board will die, though the ship will be lost. He urges them to eat, gives thanks and eats first.

27.title: The Ship Runs Aground
27.context: The ship runs aground and breaks apart in the surf; the soldiers want to kill the prisoners, but the centurion stops them to save Paul. Swimmers jump first, the rest float on planks, and everyone reaches shore safely.

28.title: Ashore on Malta
28.context: They land on Malta and the islanders show them kindness; a viper fastens on Paul’s hand, but he shakes it into the fire unharmed. Paul heals the father of Publius, the chief official, and other sick islanders come and are cured.

28.title: Paul Arrives in Italy
28.context: After three months they sail on and reach Puteoli, where believers invite them to stay a week; the believers in Rome come out as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet them, and Paul thanks God and takes courage. In Rome Paul is allowed to live by himself with a soldier guarding him.

28.title: Paul Preaches at Rome
28.context: In Rome Paul calls the Jewish leaders and from morning to evening explains Jesus from Moses and the Prophets; some believe and some do not, and he says God’s salvation has gone to the Gentiles. For two years he lives in a rented house, preaching God’s kingdom boldly and without hindrance.

1.title: Paul Greets the Saints in Rome
1.context: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus called to be an apostle, greets the believers in Rome: the gospel concerns God’s Son, a descendant of David according to the flesh, appointed the Son of God in power by his resurrection from the dead.

1.title: Unashamed of the Gospel
1.context: Paul thanks God that their faith is reported all over the world, and longs to visit them to impart some spiritual gift and be mutually encouraged.

1.title: The Gospel Is the Power of God
1.context: The theme of the letter: the gospel is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Gentile, for in it the righteousness of God is revealed by faith, as Habakkuk says, “The righteous will live by faith.”

1.title: God’s Wrath against Sin
1.context: God’s wrath is revealed against all ungodliness; his eternal power has been clearly seen in what he has made, but people exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images, so God gave them over to their sinful desires.

2.title: God’s Righteous Judgment
2.context: Those who judge others condemn themselves, for God will repay each person according to what they have done, without favoritism; even Gentiles show that the requirements of the law are written on their hearts.

2.title: The Jews and the Law
2.context: Paul addresses Jews who rely on the law and boast in God: if they teach others, why not themselves? God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of them. True circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not the written code.

3.title: There Is No One Righteous
3.context: Jews and Gentiles alike are under sin: “There is no one righteous, not even one”; Paul strings together verses from the Psalms and Isaiah and concludes that no one will be declared righteous by works of the law.

3.title: Righteousness through Faith in Christ
3.context: But now a righteousness from God, apart from the law, has been made known through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe; all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and all are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus.

4.title: Abraham Justified by Faith
4.context: Paul uses Abraham as his example: Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness before he was circumcised, so he is the father of all who believe, circumcised or not.

4.title: Abraham Receives the Promise
4.context: The promise that Abraham would be heir of the world came through the righteousness of faith; against all hope he believed God could do what he had promised, and these words were written for us too, who believe in the God who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

5.title: The Triumph of Faith
5.context: Since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ; suffering produces perseverance, character and hope, and God demonstrates his own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

5.title: Death in Adam, Life in Christ
5.context: Sin entered the world through one man and death through sin; Adam was a pattern of the one to come: just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so through the obedience of the one man, Jesus Christ, the many will be made righteous; where sin increased, grace increased all the more.

6.title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God
6.context: Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase? By no means! All who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death, buried with him so that we too may live a new life; count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

6.title: The Wages of Sin
6.context: Being under grace is no license to sin, for people are slaves of whatever they obey. The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus.

7.title: Release from the Law
7.context: As a woman is released from the law of marriage when her husband dies, so believers have died to the law through the body of Christ, to belong to the one raised from the dead and bear fruit for God, serving in the new way of the Spirit.

7.title: God’s Law Is Holy
7.context: The law is holy and the commandment holy, righteous and good, but sin seized the opportunity to bring death through it. Paul describes wanting to do good yet failing, and ends by thanking God for rescue through Jesus Christ.

8.title: Walking by the Spirit
8.context: There is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus, for the law of the Spirit of life sets us free from the law of sin and death. Those led by God’s Spirit are God’s children; we cry “Abba, Father,” and the Spirit testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children, heirs, co-heirs with Christ.

8.title: Future Glory
8.context: Our present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory to be revealed in us; creation groans, waiting for the children of God to be revealed. God works all things together for the good of those who love him, who are called according to his purpose.

8.title: The Love of God
8.context: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Not trouble, hardship, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger or sword; in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.

9.title: Paul’s Concern for the Jews
9.context: Paul grieves for Israel, to whom belong the covenants, law and promises, and from whom the Messiah comes by human descent; readers punctuate the end of verse 5 in different ways. God’s choosing rests not on works but on him who calls.

9.title: God's Wrath and Mercy
9.context: Paul says the thing formed cannot challenge its maker, for the potter has the right to make vessels for different uses; quoting Hosea and Isaiah, he says God has called both Gentiles and a remnant of Israel.

9.title: Israel’s Unbelief
9.context: The Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it by faith, while Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain it, because they pursued it as if by works; they stumbled over the stumbling stone that Isaiah described.

10.title: Everyone Who Calls on the Name of the Lord Will Be Saved
10.context: Whoever confesses Jesus as Lord and believes that God raised him from the dead will be saved, and everyone who calls on the Lord’s name will be saved. But they cannot believe without hearing or hear without a preacher, so faith comes by hearing the message of Christ.

11.title: A Remnant Chosen by Grace
11.context: Has God rejected his people? By no means! As in Elijah’s day, when seven thousand had not bowed to Baal, so now there is a remnant chosen by grace — and if by grace, then it is no longer by works.

11.title: The Ingrafting of the Gentiles
11.context: Because of Israel’s transgression, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel envious; Gentile believers are like wild olive shoots grafted into a cultivated tree, sharing its nourishing sap, and must not be arrogant but afraid, for if God did not spare the natural branches, he will not spare them either.

11.title: All Israel Will Be Saved
11.context: Paul says a partial hardening has come on Israel until the full number of Gentiles comes in, and then all Israel will be saved, for God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable. He marvels at the depth of God’s riches, wisdom and knowledge, from whom and to whom are all things.

12.title: Living Sacrifices
12.context: In view of God’s mercy, offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God; do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you can test and approve what God’s will is; in Christ we, though many, form one body, each with different gifts.

12.title: Love, Zeal, Hope, Hospitality
12.context: Love must be sincere; hate what is evil, cling to what is good; be devoted to one another, joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer; share with the Lord’s people in need and practice hospitality; do not repay evil for evil, but “overcome evil with good.”

13.title: Submission to Authorities
13.context: Everyone must submit to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established; they are God’s servants for your good, which is why you pay taxes; give to everyone what you owe them.

13.title: Love Fulfills the Law
13.context: Let no debt remain outstanding except the continuing debt to love one another, for whoever loves others has fulfilled the law; the commandments are summed up in this one: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

13.title: The Day Is Near
13.context: It is time to wake from sleep, for salvation is nearer than when we first believed; the night is nearly over and the day is near, so they should put aside deeds of darkness, put on the armor of light and clothe themselves with the Lord Jesus Christ.

14.title: The Law of Liberty
14.context: Accept the one whose faith is weak without quarreling over disputable matters, such as whether to eat meat or observe certain days; each one should be fully convinced in their own mind, for none of us lives or dies to ourselves alone — we belong to the Lord, and each will give an account to God.

14.title: The Law of Love
14.context: Stop passing judgment on one another, and do not put a stumbling block in a brother’s way; the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit, so make every effort to do what leads to peace and mutual edification.

15.title: Accept One Another
15.context: The strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not please themselves, just as Christ did not; Paul prays that God will give them unity so they may with one voice glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

15.title: Christ the Servant of Jews and Gentiles
15.context: They should accept one another as Christ accepted them; Christ became a servant of the Jews to confirm God’s promises so that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. Paul cites several Old Testament texts, saying the nations will hope in the Root of Jesse.

15.title: Paul the Minister to the Gentiles
15.context: Paul says he writes boldly to remind them because God made him a minister to the Gentiles, so that their offering might be sanctified by the Spirit; he has preached from Jerusalem to Illyricum and aims not to build on someone else’s foundation.

15.title: Paul’s Travel Plans
15.context: Paul has often been hindered from coming to Rome; now he is going to Jerusalem with the gift for the poor from Macedonia and Achaia, and then plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain, asking them to pray that he may be rescued from the unbelievers in Judea.

16.title: Personal Greetings and Love
16.context: Paul commends Phoebe, a deacon of the church in Cenchreae, sends greetings to Priscilla and Aquila and many others by name, warns against those who cause divisions, and promises that the God of peace will soon crush Satan under their feet.

16.title: Doxology
16.context: A closing doxology: God is able to strengthen them by Paul’s gospel and the mystery long hidden but now revealed for the obedience of faith among all nations; to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ.

1.title: Greetings from Paul and Sosthenes
1.context: Paul, writing from Ephesus around AD 55, greets the church of God in Corinth, those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, and thanks God that they have been enriched in every way.

1.title: Unity in the Church
1.context: The Corinthian church has split into factions, some claiming Paul, Apollos, Cephas or Christ; Paul asks whether Christ is divided or Paul was crucified for them, and says Christ sent him not to baptize but to preach the gospel.

1.title: The Message of the Cross
1.context: The message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing but the power of God to those being saved; Jews demand signs and Greeks look for wisdom, but we preach Christ crucified; God chose the foolish and weak things of the world to shame the wise and strong.

2.title: Paul’s Message by the Spirit’s Power
2.context: Paul did not come with eloquence or human wisdom but resolved to know nothing among them except Jesus Christ and him crucified, so that their faith would rest not on human wisdom but on God’s power, shown by the Spirit.

2.title: Spiritual Wisdom
2.context: Paul speaks God’s hidden wisdom, destined for our glory before time began, revealed by the Spirit, which searches all things; the person without the Spirit does not accept the things of God’s Spirit, but the spiritual person discerns them, “for we have the mind of Christ.”

3.title: God’s Fellow Workers
3.context: Paul says they are still worldly, infants who need milk; neither the planter nor the waterer matters, only God who gives growth. Each must build carefully on the one foundation, Jesus Christ, for they are God’s temple and God’s Spirit dwells in them.

4.title: Servants of Christ
4.context: Paul and his colleagues should be regarded as servants of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries, who must prove faithful; judge nothing before the Lord comes. The apostles are fools for Christ, the scum of the earth, and Paul warns them as his dear children, sending Timothy to remind them of his way of life in Christ.

5.title: Immorality Rebuked
5.context: A man in the church is living with his father’s wife, yet they are proud; Paul tells them to hand him over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh so his spirit may be saved on the Lord’s day. A little leaven spreads through the whole batch, so they must clean it out, for Christ our Passover lamb has been sacrificed.

6.title: Lawsuits among Believers
6.context: Believers are suing one another before unbelievers, and Paul says it would be better to be wronged. Listing those who will not inherit God’s kingdom, he reminds them that some of them were such, but they were washed, sanctified and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by God’s Spirit.

6.title: Glorify God in Your Body
6.context: “I have the right to do anything” — but not everything is beneficial; the body is meant for the Lord, not for sexual immorality; their bodies are members of Christ and temples of the Holy Spirit received from God, and they are not their own but were bought at a price, so they should honor God with their bodies.

7.title: Principles of Marriage
7.context: Answering their letter, Paul says that because of immorality each man should have his own wife and each woman her own husband, and they should not deprive each other; he wishes all were single like him, but each has his own gift from God; a believer married to an unbeliever should not seek divorce.

7.title: Live Your Calling
7.context: Each person should live as a believer in whatever situation the Lord has assigned, as God has called them; circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, keeping God’s commands is what counts; they were bought at a price, so they should not become slaves of human beings.

7.title: The Unmarried and Widowed
7.context: Concerning virgins, because of the present crisis it is good to remain as one is; Paul wants them free from concern, for the unmarried can be devoted to the Lord, while the married must also care about the affairs of this world; a widow is free to remarry, but only in the Lord.

8.title: Food Sacrificed to Idols
8.context: Knowledge puffs up but love builds up; an idol is nothing, for there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things. But they must not let their freedom trip up the weak.

9.title: The Rights of an Apostle
9.context: Paul says as an apostle he has the right to be supported by the gospel and to travel with a wife, but has not used it lest he hinder the gospel; he becomes all things to all people to win as many as possible, and disciplines himself like an athlete so he will not be disqualified.

10.title: Warnings from Israel’s Past
10.context: Paul uses Israel’s wilderness history as a warning: all were blessed, yet many fell through idolatry, immorality, testing God and grumbling. Whoever thinks they stand should be careful, God provides a way out of temptation, and no one can drink both the Lord’s cup and the cup of demons.

10.title: All to God’s Glory
10.context: Everything is permissible, but not everything is beneficial; no one should seek their own good but the good of others. They may eat what is sold in the market, but not if someone points out it was offered to idols, for that person’s conscience; whatever they do, they should do it all for God’s glory.

11.title: Roles in Worship
11.context: Paul addresses head coverings in worship: the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is man, and God is the head of Christ; yet in the Lord woman is not independent of man nor man of woman, for everything comes from God.

11.title: Sharing in the Lord’s Supper
11.context: When they come together their divisions show: each eats his own supper, some go hungry and others get drunk, so it is not the Lord’s Supper they eat; they despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing.

11.title: The Institution of the Lord's Supper
11.context: Paul passes on what he received from the Lord: on the night of his betrayal Jesus broke bread as his body given for them, to be done in remembrance of him, and gave the cup as the new covenant in his blood. Each time they eat and drink, they proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

11.title: Eating the Lord's Supper Unworthily
11.context: Whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup in an unworthy manner sins against the body and blood of the Lord; each should examine themselves before they eat, for whoever eats without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on themselves; so when they gather to eat, they should wait for one another.

12.title: Spiritual Gifts
12.context: Paul says no one can say “Jesus is Lord” except by the Holy Spirit; there are different gifts but the same Spirit — wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discernment, tongues and interpretation — all worked by the one Spirit, which distributes them to each as it determines.

12.title: The Body of Christ
12.context: The body is one though it has many parts, and believers were all baptized by one Spirit into one body; no part can say it does not belong or that it does not need another, and the weaker parts are indispensable. They are the body of Christ, and each one is a part of it.

13.title: Love
13.context: Paul says that tongues, prophecy, mountain-moving faith and even martyrdom are nothing without love; love is patient and kind, does not envy or boast, and bears, believes, hopes and endures all things. Faith, hope and love remain, and the greatest of these is love.

14.title: Prophecy and Tongues
14.context: Follow the way of love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially prophecy, for one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself but one who prophesies edifies the church; in church Paul would rather speak five intelligible words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.

14.title: Orderly Worship
14.context: When they gather, each may bring a hymn, teaching, revelation, tongue or interpretation, but all must build up the church; tongues and prophecy should be taken in turn with interpretation, for God is a God of peace, not disorder, and everything should be done in order.

15.title: The Resurrection of Christ
15.context: The heart of the gospel is that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried and was raised on the third day; he appeared to Cephas, the Twelve, more than five hundred believers, James, the apostles and finally Paul, who says he is what he is by God’s grace.

15.title: The Resurrection of the Dead
15.context: If the dead are not raised, Christ was not raised and faith is futile; but Christ has been raised as the firstfruits of those who sleep. Death came through a man and so does resurrection; at the end Christ hands the kingdom to God the Father, and the Son himself becomes subject to him, so that God may be all in all.

15.title: The Resurrection Body
15.context: The resurrection body is like a seed: sown perishable, raised imperishable; the first Adam became a living being, the last Adam a life-giving spirit. All will be changed and death swallowed up in victory, so their labor in the Lord is not in vain.

16.title: The Collection for the Saints
16.context: About the collection for the Lord’s people: on the first day of every week each should set aside a sum in keeping with their income, so that no collections will have to be made when Paul comes; then their approved men will carry the gift to Jerusalem.

16.title: Paul’s Travel Plans
16.context: Paul plans to come through Macedonia and perhaps spend the winter with them, but will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost because a great door for effective work has opened, and there are many who oppose him; he asks them to welcome Timothy, and says Apollos will come when he has the opportunity.

16.title: Concluding Exhortations
16.context: Paul urges them to be watchful, stand firm in the faith, be courageous and strong, and do everything in love; he sends greetings in his own hand, adds the Aramaic “Maranatha” (our Lord, come), and wishes them the grace of the Lord Jesus.

1.title: Paul Greets the Corinthians
1.context: Paul, with Timothy, writes a second letter to the church in Corinth and all the saints throughout Achaia, probably from Macedonia around AD 56.

1.title: The God of All Comfort
1.context: Paul praises the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, who comforts them in trouble so they can comfort others; in Asia they were crushed beyond strength and despaired of life, but learned to rely not on themselves but on God who raises the dead.

1.title: Paul’s Change of Plans
1.context: Paul explains why he changed his travel plans: he did not make them lightly, saying yes and no at once, for in Christ, the Son of God, it has always been “Yes” — all God’s promises are “Yes” in Christ; he stayed away to spare them another painful visit.

2.title: Forgiving the Offender
2.context: The man who caused grief has been punished enough by the majority; now they should forgive and comfort him, so that he is not overwhelmed by excessive sorrow, and reaffirm their love for him, in order that Satan might not outwit them.

2.title: Triumph in Christ
2.context: Not finding Titus in Troas, Paul is restless and goes on to Macedonia; he thanks God who always leads them in triumph in Christ and spreads the fragrance of knowing him everywhere, for they do not peddle God’s word for profit but speak with sincerity.

3.title: Ministers of a New Covenant
3.context: The Corinthians are Paul’s letter of recommendation, written by God’s Spirit on hearts; they serve a new covenant, not of the letter, which kills, but of the Spirit, which gives life. Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

4.title: The Light of the Gospel
4.context: Paul says they renounce deception and openly set forth the truth; the god of this age has blinded unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel of Christ’s glory. They hold this treasure in jars of clay to show that the surpassing power is God’s, hard pressed on every side but not crushed.

4.title: Living by Faith
4.context: Paul says that though outwardly they are wasting away, inwardly they are renewed day by day; their light and momentary troubles are achieving an eternal glory far greater, so they fix their eyes not on what is seen, which is temporary, but on what is unseen, which is eternal.

5.title: Ambassadors for Christ
5.context: Christ’s love compels Paul, for one died for all, so those who live no longer live for themselves; anyone in Christ is a new creation. God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their sins against them, and Paul as Christ’s ambassador urges people to be reconciled to God.

6.title: Do Not Be Unequally Yoked
6.context: Believers should not be yoked with unbelievers, for righteousness and wickedness or light and darkness have nothing in common; they are the temple of the living God, so they must come out and be separate, and God will receive them as his sons and daughters.

7.title: Paul’s Joy in the Corinthians
7.context: Paul asks them to open their hearts to him; troubled on every side in Macedonia, he was comforted by Titus’ arrival and news of their longing, sorrow and zeal for him. His earlier letter grieved them, but it was godly sorrow that led to repentance.

8.title: Generosity Commended
8.context: The Macedonian churches gave generously despite affliction and poverty; Paul urges the Corinthians to finish their gift for the Jerusalem saints, for the Lord Jesus, though rich, became poor for their sake so that they might become rich.

8.title: Titus Commended
8.context: Paul thanks God for putting into Titus the same concern for them, and sends him with another brother praised by all the churches, to make sure the gift is handled honorably, not only in the eyes of the Lord but also in the eyes of man.

9.title: God Loves a Cheerful Giver
9.context: Paul says whoever sows sparingly reaps sparingly and whoever sows generously reaps generously; each should give what they have decided, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver. God can make all grace abound to them, and their gift will supply the saints’ needs and cause many to thank God.

10.title: Paul’s Apostolic Authority
10.context: Some say Paul is bold in letters but weak in person; he replies that though they live in the world they do not wage war as the world does, for their weapons have divine power to demolish strongholds and take every thought captive to obey Christ.

10.title: Boast Only in the Lord
10.context: Paul says they do not boast of others’ work but hope that as the Corinthians’ faith grows, the gospel can be preached in regions beyond; whoever boasts should boast in the Lord, for it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one the Lord commends.

11.title: Paul and the False Apostles
11.context: Paul is jealous for them with a godly jealousy, afraid their minds will be led astray from sincere devotion as Eve was deceived by the serpent; they readily put up with someone preaching another Jesus, but such people are false apostles masquerading as apostles of Christ, as Satan masquerades as an angel of light.

11.title: Paul’s Suffering and Service
11.context: Forced to boast like a fool, Paul lists his labors, imprisonments, floggings, stoning, shipwrecks and dangers on rivers, seas, in cities and wilderness, and his daily concern for all the churches; if he must boast, he will boast of his weakness.

12.title: Paul’s Revelation
12.context: Paul says he knows a man who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven, into paradise, and heard inexpressible things; to keep him from conceit he was given a thorn in the flesh, and when he asked three times for its removal the Lord said his grace is sufficient, for his power is made perfect in weakness.

12.title: Paul’s Concern for the Corinthians
12.context: Paul says the marks of an apostle were displayed among them with great perseverance; he is ready to visit a third time and wants not their possessions but them, and he fears he will find quarreling, jealousy and anger and many who have not repented of their sins.

13.title: Examine Yourselves
13.context: On his third visit Paul will settle matters by two or three witnesses and not spare those who sin; they should examine themselves to see whether they are in the faith. He urges unity and peace and blesses them with the grace of Christ, the love of God and the fellowship of the Spirit.

1.title: Paul’s Greeting to the Galatians
1.context: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia as an apostle sent not from men nor by a man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead; Christ gave himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father.

1.title: No Other Gospel
1.context: Paul is astonished that they are so quickly deserting the one who called them by the grace of Christ and turning to a different gospel, which is really no gospel at all; even if he or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel other than the one they accepted, let them be under God’s curse.

1.title: Paul Preaches the Gospel
1.context: Paul says the gospel he preaches did not come from people but by revelation of Jesus Christ; he once violently persecuted the church, but God called him by grace and revealed his Son in him so he might preach among the Gentiles, and he did not consult anyone, going to Jerusalem to see Cephas only after three years.

2.title: The Council at Jerusalem
2.context: Fourteen years later Paul goes to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus and lays out his gospel before the leaders; Titus, a Greek, is not forced to be circumcised, and James, Cephas and John recognize Paul’s calling to the Gentiles and extend the right hand of fellowship.

2.title: Paul Confronts Cephas
2.context: In Antioch Cephas at first eats with Gentiles but then withdraws for fear of the circumcision group, and even Barnabas is led into this hypocrisy; seeing that they are not acting in line with the gospel, Paul confronts Cephas publicly, asking why he forces Gentiles to live like Jews.

2.title: Jews and Gentiles Are Saved by Faith
2.context: Paul says a person is justified not by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ; he has been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer he who lives but Christ who lives in him, and the life he now lives he lives by faith in the Son of God, who loved him and gave himself for him.

3.title: Faith and Belief
3.context: Paul asks the Galatians whether they received the Spirit by works of the law or by believing the gospel; Abraham believed and was counted righteous, so people of faith are his children. Christ redeemed us from the law’s curse by becoming a curse for us.

3.title: The Purpose of the Law
3.context: A covenant previously established by God is not set aside by the law introduced 430 years later; the law was added because of transgressions until the Seed to whom the promise referred had come, and it was put in charge of us until Christ came that we might be justified by faith.

3.title: Slaves and Sons
3.context: The law was a guardian leading us to Christ to be justified by faith; now that faith has come we are no longer under it. All baptized into Christ have put him on, and there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for all are one in Christ.

4.title: Paul’s Concern for the Galatians
4.context: Paul says that formerly they did not know God, but now that they know him, why turn back to weak and miserable principles, observing days, months, seasons and years? He recalls how they first welcomed him and would have torn out their eyes for him, and says he is again in labor pains until Christ is formed in them.

4.title: Hagar and Sarah
4.context: Paul uses Abraham’s two sons as an allegory: one born of the slave woman Hagar according to the flesh, the other of the free woman Sarah through promise; the two women represent two covenants, and believers are children of promise, not of the slave woman but of the free.

5.title: Freedom in Christ
5.context: Christ has set them free, so they must not return to a yoke of slavery; in Christ circumcision counts for nothing, only faith working through love. Freedom is not license for the flesh but a call to serve one another in love.

5.title: Walking by the Spirit
5.context: Walk by the Spirit and do not gratify the flesh; the works of the flesh are obvious, but the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh.

6.title: Carry One Another’s Burdens
6.context: If someone is caught in a sin, the spiritual should restore them gently; carrying each other’s burdens fulfills the law of Christ. People reap what they sow, so they should not tire of doing good, for they will reap in due time.

6.title: Final Warnings and Blessings
6.context: Paul writes in large letters with his own hand that those pressing circumcision only want to boast in the flesh; he will never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, for neither circumcision nor uncircumcision matters, only a new creation. He bears on his body the marks of Jesus.

1.title: Paul’s Greeting to the Ephesians
1.context: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, writes from prison to the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus.

1.title: Spiritual Blessings
1.context: Paul praises God for every spiritual blessing in Christ: he chose us before the world’s foundation and adopted us according to his pleasure; through the beloved Son’s blood we have redemption and forgiveness, and we are sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.

1.title: Spiritual Wisdom
1.context: Paul asks the glorious Father to give them a spirit of wisdom and revelation, so they will know the hope of his calling, the riches of his inheritance and his great power toward believers; God raised Christ from the dead, put all things under his feet and made him head over all things for the church.

2.title: Alive with Christ
2.context: They were once dead in sins, following the ways of this world, but God, rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ; we are saved by grace through faith, not by ourselves but as God’s gift, and we are his workmanship, created for good works.

2.title: One in Christ
2.context: Gentiles were once excluded from Israel, without hope and without God, but now they have been brought near by Christ’s blood; he broke down the dividing wall, made the two one and reconciled both to God through the cross. They are members of God’s household, being built into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit.

3.title: The Mystery of the Gospel
3.context: Paul says God revealed to him the mystery of the gospel: through it the Gentiles are fellow heirs with Israel, one body and sharers in the promise. Though the least of the saints, he was given grace to preach Christ’s boundless riches to the Gentiles.

3.title: Paul’s Prayer for the Ephesians
